dervis-irab:38-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اثَّاقَلْتُمْ): its origin is تثاقلتم; the tāʾ was changed into a thāʾ, then assimilated into the thāʾ, then the connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in to make it possible to pronounce the vowelless letter. Al-Kisāʾī recited:
تولي الضجيع إذا ما اشتاقها خصرا ... عذب المذاق إذا ما اتّابع القبل
(She gives her bedfellow, when he longs for her, a cool mouth, sweet to the taste when kisses follow one another — cited for اتّابع < تتابع.)
(الغار): the cave; its plural is أغوار and غيران. Its alif is changed from a wāw. The cave of Ḥirāʾ is a hollow in Mount Thawr, to the right of Mecca, an hour's journey away. [Translator's note: the cave of the Hijra mentioned in this verse is commonly identified as the cave of Mount Thawr, while Ḥirāʾ is a separate mountain; the source text is translated as written.]

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has preceded. (ما لَكُمْ إِذا قِيلَ لَكُمُ انْفِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ): ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); لكم is the khabar (predicate); إذا is a future adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) اثاقلتم; قيل is a passive past verb; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; انفروا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); في سبيل الله is attached to انفروا; the clause اثاقلتم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and إلى الأرض is attached to اثاقلتم. The meaning is: What excuse do you have, being sluggish at the time when the Messenger says to you "انفروا", i.e. go out to jihad in the way of Allah? That was at the expedition of Tabūk in the year nine, after their return from al-Ṭāʾif; they were called to mobilize at a time of hardship, drought and scorching heat, with the great distance of the journey and the enemy's fierceness, so it was hard on them.
(أَرَضِيتُمْ بِالْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ): the interrogative is for disapproval and rebuke, joined with wonder. رضيتم is a verb and its fāʿil; بالحياة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رضيتم; الدنيا is an adjective; and من الآخرة is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "as a substitute for the Hereafter". (فَما مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); ما is negating; متاع is the mubtadaʾ; الحياة is muḍāf ilayhi; الدنيا an adjective; في الآخرة is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "reckoned beside the Hereafter"; إلا is a particle of restriction; and قليل is the khabar of متاع. It is also permissible to attach في الآخرة to قليل. Al-Shihāb called the «في» that comes before الآخرة "comparative" (qiyāsiyya), i.e. "in comparison with the Hereafter", and by my life, that is not far-fetched. (إِلَّا تَنْفِرُوا يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً وَيَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْماً غَيْرَكُمْ): إن is conditional and لا is negating; تنفروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and يعذبكم its apodosis (jawāb); عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and أليما an adjective; يستبدل is conjoined to يعذبكم; قوما is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and غيركم is an adjective of «قوما». (وَلا تَضُرُّوهُ شَيْئاً وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): ولا تضروه is conjoined to يستبدل; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi; شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "any harm"; الله is the mubtadaʾ and قدير its khabar; and على كل is attached to قدير. (إِلَّا تَنْصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ): إن is conditional and لا negating, and they have been assimilated as was mentioned before; تنصروه is the protasis; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; and the clause قد نصره الله is the apodosis. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it well, saying: "If you ask: how can قد نصره الله be an apodosis of the condition? I say: there are two ways. The first: if you do not help him in the future, then He will help the one whom He helped when there was with him only one man — and there is nothing less than one. So by saying قد نصره الله He indicated that He will help him in the future as He helped him at that time. The second: He made help obligatory for him and made him victorious at that time, so he will not be forsaken after it." The commentators agreed that the apodosis is omitted, because the expedition of Tabūk was in the ninth year, whereas His saying إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا was long before that; and they said that فقد نصره الله is in the place of a justification for the omitted apodosis, and this is close to al-Zamakhsharī's first view. (إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُما فِي الْغارِ): the adverb is attached to نصره الله; the clause أخرجه is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; الذين is the fāʿil and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); ثاني اثنين is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in أخرجه, the implied form being: "when those who disbelieved drove him out, he being alone, apart from all people except Abū Bakr". اثنين is muḍāf ilayhi. إذ is a badal (substitute) for the first إذ, i.e. the time of his expulsion is assumed to extend so as to include the time of their staying in the cave and the time of the said speech; so it is a badal of part from whole. هما is the mubtadaʾ and في الغار the khabar, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.
(إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصاحِبِهِ لا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنا): إذ is also a badal; the clause لا تحزن is the object of the saying; the clause إن الله معنا is causal (giving the reason); إنّ and its noun, and the adverb is attached to its omitted khabar. (فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْها): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أنزل الله سكينته is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; عليه is attached to أنزل; أيده is conjoined to أنزل; بجنود is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أيده; and the clause لم تروها is an adjective of جنود. (وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلى وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيا): the wāw is also a conjunction; جعل is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; كلمة is a mafʿūl bihi; الذين is muḍāf ilayhi and the clause كفروا is the ṣila; السفلى is the second mafʿūl bihi of جعل. As for وكلمة, the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); كلمة الله is the mubtadaʾ; هي is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; and العليا is the khabar of كلمة, or the khabar of هي with that clause being the khabar of كلمة. (وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): الله is the mubtadaʾ and عزيز and حكيم are its two khabars.

dervis-irab:41-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خِفافاً وَثِقالًا): the expressions of the commentators about these two differ, but they go back to one source, i.e. go out in the state in which jihad is light for you and in the state in which jihad is heavy for you. These two descriptions are so general and comprehensive that all categories fall under them. The story of the governor of Ḥimṣ will come in the section of Benefits.
(عَرَضاً): al-ʿaraḍ is whatever presents itself to you of the benefits and goods of this world. Among their sayings: "This world is a present good (ʿaraḍ ḥāḍir) from which the righteous and the wicked eat."
(قاصِداً): a qāṣid journey is one that is moderate and near.
(الشُّقَّةُ): a far and arduous distance.

* I'rab:
(انْفِرُوا خِفافاً وَثِقالًا وَجاهِدُوا بِأَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): انفروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); خفافا and ثقالا are two ḥāls (circumstantials); جاهدوا is conjoined to انفروا; بأموالكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاهدوا; أنفسكم is conjoined to بأموالكم; and في سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to جاهدوا. (ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ): ذلكم is the mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. what was mentioned of the two commands, انفروا and جاهدوا; خير is the khabar (predicate); لكم is attached to خير; إن is conditional; كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause تعلمون is the khabar of كنتم; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "then strive" or "then do not be sluggish". (لَوْ كانَ عَرَضاً قَرِيباً وَسَفَراً قاصِداً لَاتَّبَعُوكَ): لو is a conditional particle of impossibility (imtināʿiyya); كان عرضا: كان and its noun is latent, its implied form being "the matter" (al-shaʾn), i.e. what they were called to, and عرضا is its khabar; سفرا قاصدا is conjoined to it. لاتبعوك: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and اتبعوك is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause has no grammatical position. (وَلكِنْ بَعُدَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّقَّةُ): the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), made inoperative by being lightened; بعدت عليهم الشقة is a verb and its fāʿil; عليهم is attached to بعدت; and the clause is a ḥāl. (وَسَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَوِ اسْتَطَعْنا لَخَرَجْنا مَعَكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; the sīn is for the future; بالله is attached to يحلفون; the clause لو استطعنا is the answer to the oath; and the clause لخرجنا is the apodosis of لو. You may also make the clause لو استطعنا the object of an omitted saying in the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "saying", in which case لخرجنا stands in place of the answer to both the oath and the condition together. معكم is an adverb attached to خرجنا. (يُهْلِكُونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ): the clause يهلكون أنفسهم is a badal (substitute) for سيحلفون, or a ḥāl, i.e. "destroying"; أنفسهم is the mafʿūl bihi; الله is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم is the khabar; and إنّ with its noun and khabar stands in place of the two objects of يعلم. (عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْكَ لِمَ أَذِنْتَ لَهُمْ): a clause of supplication, in which «عفا» was put first in the context of reproach, to soften the heart of the Messenger and out of kindness to him. Al-Zamakhsharī erred when he explained it as: "You erred, and how evil is what you did." And well said the one who said about this verse: Among Allah the Exalted's gentleness with His Prophet is that He began with pardon before reproach; had He said to him from the start "لم أذنت لهم", his heart would have broken. لم: the lām is a preposition that entered upon the interrogative ما, so its alif was dropped — its ruling has preceded. Both lāms are attached to the permission (al-idhn), because their meanings differ: the first is for cause and the second for conveying (al-tablīgh). The genitive pronoun is for the group of those asking permission, and the disapproval is directed at the permission because it included all of them. (حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَتَعْلَمَ الْكاذِبِينَ): حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition, i.e. "until it becomes clear to you who was truthful in his excuse from who lied in it"; لك is attached to يتبين; الذين is the fāʿil and the clause صدقوا is the ṣila (relative clause); تعلم is conjoined to يتبين; and الكاذبين is the mafʿūl bihi.

* Benefits:
The story of the governor of Ḥimṣ and the Damascene:
In connection with jihad and the call to mobilize, we relate the following wonderful story, and we content ourselves with it because the discussions of jihad and mobilization are set out at length in the extensive works:
From Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, who said: I was governor of Ḥimṣ, and I met a very old man from the people of Damascus whose eyebrows had drooped over his eyes, on his mount, intending to go on a campaign. I said:
"Uncle, Allah has excused you." He raised his eyebrows and said: "Son of my brother, Allah has called us to go out, light and heavy. Indeed, whomever Allah loves, He tests."

Increasing the numbers and guarding the baggage:
From al-Zuhrī: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib went out on a campaign when one of his eyes had gone. It was said to him: "You are ill and have an impairment." He said: "Allah has called us to go out, the light and the heavy; if fighting is not possible for me, I will increase the numbers and guard the baggage."

dervis-irab:99-100.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ الْأَعْرابِ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): (ومن الأعراب) is a fronted khabar (predicate), and (من) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يؤمن بالله) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (اليوم الآخر) is conjoined to (الله). (وَيَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ قُرُباتٍ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَصَلَواتِ الرَّسُولِ): (ويتخذ) is conjoined to (يؤمن), and its fāʿil (agent) is "he"; (ما) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (ينفق) is the ṣila; (قربات) is a second mafʿūl bihi; (عند الله) is an adverb in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective). As for (صلوات الرسول), there are two views. The more evident of them is that it is conjoined to (قربات), the meaning being that what he spends is a means of attaining nearness to Allah and the prayers of the Messenger, because the Messenger used to pray for those who gave charity, asking good and blessing for them and seeking forgiveness for them. The second is that it is conjoined to (ما ينفق), its implied form being "and the prayers of the Messenger [he takes as] means of nearness", with (قربات) as the second object of (يتخذ). (أَلا إِنَّها قُرْبَةٌ لَهُمْ سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): (ألا) is a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh), and the clause is resumptive, emphasised by (ألا) and (إنّ) to affirm the matter. (إنّ), its noun and its khabar; (لهم) is a naʿt of (قربة). In (سيدخلهم), the sīn is a particle of the future, and (يدخلهم الله) is an imperfect verb, a direct object and an agent; (في رحمته) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يدخلهم). (إنّ), its noun and its two predicates. (وَالسَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ الْمُهاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصارِ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُمْ بِإِحْسانٍ): (السابقون) is a mubtadaʾ, (الأولون) is a naʿt, (من المهاجرين والأنصار) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), (الذين) is conjoined to (السابقون), (اتبعوهم) is the ṣila, and (بإحسان) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ): the clause is the khabar of (السابقون). There are two other views on the khabar, mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ and followed by most of the commentators, and I do not know how they found them acceptable: the first is that the khabar is (الأولون), which is plainly incoherent; the second is that it is (من المهاجرين والأنصار), which is even more incoherent. (وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the i'rab of parallels to this clause has been given many times before, so there is no need to repeat it.

dervis-irab:44-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلَأَوْضَعُوا): i.e. they would have hurried about among you with slanders and with spoiling relations between people. The origin of al-īḍāʿ is hastening.

* I'rab:
(لا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): the clause is resumptive, brought to establish what indicates that it is not the habit of the believers to ask your permission to strive. يستأذنك is an imperfect verb and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين is the fāʿil (agent); the clause يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause); بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يؤمنون; and اليوم الآخر is conjoined to الله. (أَنْ يُجاهِدُوا بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُتَّقِينَ): أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "regarding jihad", and it is attached to يستأذنك; بأموالهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يجاهدوا; أنفسهم is conjoined to أموالهم; الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and عليم the khabar (predicate); and بالمتقين is attached to عليم.
(إِنَّما يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and the i'rab of what follows has preceded. The meaning is: those who ask permission are the wavering and the perplexed; as for the clear-sighted believers, they are firm in what they have resolved upon and what is obligatory on them. This is among the highest refinements of good manners that ought to be followed: it is not fitting for a person to ask his brother's permission to do him a kindness, just as it is not fitting for a host to ask his guest's permission to serve him food, for asking permission in this situation is a sign of affectation. It befits men of honour and people of chivalry not to be sluggish when they are summoned to an affair worthy of honour. Ṭarafa said:
إذا القوم قالوا من فتى خلت أنني ... عنيت فلم أكسل ولم أتبلد
(When the people say "Who is a brave youth?", I think that I am the one meant, so I am neither lazy nor dull.)
And another said:
إن تبتدر غاية يوما لمكرمة ... تلق السوابق منا والمصلينا
(If one day a goal of nobility is raced for, you will find the front-runners and the second-placers from among us.)
And their poems overflow with this.
(وَارْتابَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فَهُمْ فِي رَيْبِهِمْ يَتَرَدَّدُونَ): conjoined to لا يؤمنون; ارتابت قلوبهم is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. they doubted the religion. فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction and هم the mubtadaʾ; في ريبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يترددون; and the clause يترددون is the khabar.
(وَلَوْ أَرادُوا الْخُرُوجَ لَأَعَدُّوا لَهُ عُدَّةً): speech also conjoined, and you may make it resumptive. لو is conditional; أرادوا الخروج is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; أعدوا is a verb and its fāʿil; له is attached to أعدوا; and عدة is the mafʿūl bihi. (وَلكِنْ كَرِهَ اللَّهُ انْبِعاثَهُمْ): the wāw conjoins to something omitted, as if it were said: "They did not go out, but Allah disliked their setting forth." (فَثَبَّطَهُمْ وَقِيلَ اقْعُدُوا مَعَ الْقاعِدِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ثبطهم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; قيل is a passive past verb, because the speaker may possibly refer to Allah, or possibly to the wretchedness and evil destiny implanted in their souls; اقعدوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; مع is an adverb attached to اقعدوا; and القاعدين is muḍāf ilayhi. The secret of His saying مع القاعدين will come in the section of Rhetoric. (لَوْ خَرَجُوا فِيكُمْ ما زادُوكُمْ إِلَّا خَبالًا): resumptive speech, brought to establish the harms that would have resulted from their going out. خرجوا is a verb and its fāʿil; فيكم is attached to خرجوا; the clause ما زادوكم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; زادوكم is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; إلا is a particle of restriction; and خبالا is the second mafʿūl bihi. The exception here is connected (muttaṣil), not disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because a disconnected exception is where the excepted is not of the genus of that from which it is excepted, as when you say: "They added you no good, except corruption (ما زادوكم خيرا إلا خبالا)". The thing excepted from is not mentioned in the verse, and when it is not mentioned, the exception is from the most general of generals, which is "thing", so it is a connected exception, since خبال is part of the most general of generals; as if it were said: "They would not have added you anything except خبال." Al-khabāl is corruption and evil, and that by making the believers lose heart and bringing weakness into their hearts.
(وَلَأَوْضَعُوا خِلالَكُمْ يَبْغُونَكُمُ الْفِتْنَةَ): لأوضعوا is conjoined to ما زادوكم, and the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; خلالكم is accusative as an adverb and attached to أوضعوا, i.e. they would have hurried among you with slanders and incitement; the clause يبغونكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of أوضعوا, i.e. they would have hastened among you seeking your trial (fitna). الفتنة is the object of يبغونكم, and the kāf is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "they seek fitna for you".
(وَفِيكُمْ سَمَّاعُونَ لَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is circumstantial; فيكم is a fronted khabar and سماعون a delayed mubtadaʾ; لهم is attached to سماعون. The meaning is: among you are spies for them who spy on you, convey your news to them and uncover your plans to them. الله is the mubtadaʾ and عليم the khabar, and بالظالمين is attached to عليم.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is al-tatmīm (completion), by mentioning مع القاعدين and not being content with mentioning اقعدوا; for had He confined it to the command, it would have conveyed nothing but staying behind. But He wanted to place them in the ranks of the chronically ill, the sick, those with disabilities, the feeble-minded, the women and the children, whose way is to stay crouched in houses — meaning that they are the ones described among people as lagging behind and sitting idle, and branded with the mark of hesitancy and cowardice. More of this wonderful art will come.

dervis-irab:101-104.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَرَدُوا): they became practised in it and persisted in it. One says تمرّد فلان when someone becomes insolent and overbearing; from it comes the devil described as المارد. تمرّد في معصيته means he held fast to his disobedience, made it his habit and did not repent of it. The root sense of مرد and تمرّد is softness, smoothness and bareness, as though they stripped themselves bare for hypocrisy. From it comes غصن أمرد, a branch with no leaves on it; فرس أمرد, a horse with no hair; غلام أمرد, a boy with no hair on his face; أرض مرداء, land with no vegetation; and صرح ممرّد, a bare (smooth) edifice. So the meaning is that they remained in hypocrisy, held fast to it and did not turn away from it.
(سَكَنٌ): السكن is tranquillity; it is of the pattern faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl (the thing done), like القبض in the sense of المقبوض.

* I'rab:
(وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ مُنافِقُونَ): a resumptive clause, brought to describe the state of the hypocrites among the people of Medina and the Bedouins around it, after describing the state of the people of the desert. (ممن) is a fronted khabar (predicate); the adverb (حولكم) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (من الأعراب) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and (منافقون) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ مَرَدُوا عَلَى النِّفاقِ): (ومن أهل المدينة) may be conjoined to (من) which is in the genitive by (من), so that the two genitive phrases share in being predicated of the mubtadaʾ, namely (منافقون), as though it were said: the hypocrites are from a people around you and from the people of Medina. It is also possible that the sentence is complete at His saying (منافقون), and that His saying (ومن أهل المدينة) is a fronted khabar whose mubtadaʾ after it is omitted, its naʿt (adjective) standing in its place. Omitting the qualified noun and putting its adjective in its place is a regular pattern, as in منّا ظعن ومنّا أقام ("of us [some] departed and of us [some] stayed"), and as in the poet's saying:
أنا ابن جلا وطلاع الثنايا ... متى أضع العمامة تعرفوني
(I am the son of [one who] made things clear, a climber of mountain passes; whenever I lay down the turban, you will know me.)
The implied form is "and of the people of Medina are a people who persisted in hypocrisy". (لا تَعْلَمُهُمْ نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُمْ سَنُعَذِّبُهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ): the clause is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of (منافقون), or it is resumptive. (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (نعلمهم) is its khabar; the second object of (نعلمهم) is omitted, its implied form being "hypocrites", and likewise the second object of (تعلمهم). In (سنعذبهم), the sīn is a particle of the future, and (نعذبهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (مرتين) is an adverb. (ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ إِلى عَذابٍ عَظِيمٍ): the clause is conjoined; (يردون) is a verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يردون); and (عظيم) is a naʿt. (وَآخَرُونَ اعْتَرَفُوا بِذُنُوبِهِمْ خَلَطُوا عَمَلًا صالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً): (وآخرون) is conjoined to (منافقون), or it is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (اعترفوا بذنوبهم) is its naʿt and the clause (خلطوا) is its khabar. (عملا) is the object of (خلطوا), (صالحا) is a naʿt, (آخر) is conjoined to (عملا), and (سيئا) is a naʿt. In the section on Benefits the manner of this mixing and the subtleties in it will be discussed. (عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): (عسى) is one of the verbs of proximity (afʿāl al-muqāraba) and conveys hope; (الله) is its noun, and (أن) with what falls under it is its khabar; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتوب). (إنّ), its noun and its two predicates. (خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِها): (خذ) is an imperative verb whose agent is "you"; (من أموالهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خذ), the meaning of (من) being partitive; (صدقة) is a direct object. (من أموالهم) may also be attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt of (صدقة), and when it was placed first it became accusative as a ḥāl from it. The clause (تطهرهم) is a ḥāl from the agent of (خذ) if the tāʾ in (تطهرهم) is of address to the Prophet ﷺ, or a naʿt of (صدقة) if the tāʾ is of the absent third person [feminine, referring to the charity]; (وتزكيهم بها) is conjoined to (تطهرهم). (وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ صَلاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): (وصلّ) is conjoined to (خذ) and (عليهم) is attached to (صلّ); (إنّ), its noun and its khabar; (لهم) is a naʿt of (سكن); (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (سميع عليم) are its two predicates.
(أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبادِهِ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; (يعلموا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم). (أنّ) with what falls under it stands in place of the two objects of (يعلموا). (أنّ) and its noun; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يقبل) is its khabar, and that clause is the khabar of (أنّ). (هو) cannot be a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), because what follows it cannot be confused with an adjective. (عن عباده) is attached to (يقبل). (وَيَأْخُذُ الصَّدَقاتِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ): a coordination by conjunction with what preceded. Here (هو) may be a pronoun of separation, or it may be a mubtadaʾ.

* Benefits:
1- Omitting the qualified noun and putting its adjective in its place:
It is frequently permitted to omit the qualified noun (manʿūt) if it is known and the naʿt is fit to be governed directly by the governing word, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «أن اعمل سابغات», that is, coats of mail that are ample (دروعا سابغات); or if the naʿt is a clause or a quasi-clause [a preposition phrase or adverb] and the qualified noun is nominative and part of a noun preceding it that is in the genitive by «من» or «في». The first [case with من] is as in their saying منّا ظعن ومنّا أقام: ظعن and أقام are two clauses in the position of nominative, and they are adjectives of two omitted qualified nouns that are nominative as mubtadaʾ, i.e. منّا فريق ظعن ومنّا فريق أقام ("of us is a party that departed and of us is a party that stayed"). The second [with في] is as in the saying of Abū al-Aswad al-Ḥimmānī describing a woman:
لو قلت ما في قومها لم تيثم ... يفضلها في حسب وميثم
(Were you to say: there is none among her people — you would not sin — who surpasses her in lineage and beauty.)
Its original form is: "Were you to say there is not among her people anyone (أحد) who surpasses her, you would not sin in your statement." So the qualified noun, namely أحد, was omitted and the clause يفضلها was put in its place.
Further, it is permitted to omit the naʿt if it is known, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وكان وراءهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة غصبا», i.e. every sound ship; and the saying of ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās:
وقد كنت في الحرب ذا تدرأ ... فلم أعط شيئا ولم أمنع
(I was in war a man of strong defence, yet I was not given anything, nor was I refused.)
He omitted the naʿt and kept the qualified noun, i.e. "anything worthwhile". What necessitated supposing this naʿt is the aim of truthfulness, for in reality he was given something, as shown by his saying "nor was I refused", but he was not pleased with it; so one needs to suppose an adjective by which the speech is clothed in the garment of truth and adorned with the weight of right. And the saying of al-Muraqqish al-Akbar:
ورب أسيلة الخدين بكر ... مهفهفة لها فرع وجيد
(Many a smooth-cheeked virgin, slender-waisted, having hair and a neck…)
i.e. jet-black hair and a long neck, as shown by the fact that fine love poetry calls for affirming the hair and the neck qualified by two beloved qualities.
It remains that both the qualified noun and the naʿt may be omitted together, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «لا يموت فيها ولا يحيا», i.e. a beneficial life. They may also both be omitted when the word governed by the naʿt stands in its place, as they said in «والله ما هي بنعم الولد», i.e. by Allah, she is not a child of whom it is said "what an excellent child"; and «ونعم السير على بئس العير», i.e. on a caravan of which it is said "what a wretched caravan".

2- Which of them is the thing mixed and which the thing it is mixed with?
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا» He made each of them a thing mixed; so what is the thing it is mixed with?
The answer is that each one is both mixed and mixed-with, because the meaning is that each of the two was mixed with the other, as when you say خلطت الماء واللبن ("I mixed the water and the milk"), meaning you mixed each of them with its companion. This carries what is not in your saying خلطت الماء باللبن ("I mixed the water with the milk"), because there you have made the water the thing mixed and the milk the thing it is mixed with; whereas when you say it with the wāw, you have made the water and the milk both mixed and mixed-with, as though you said: I mixed the water with the milk and the milk with the water.
From another angle, the turning away from the bāʾ is because "mixing" is made to include the meaning of "doing", as though it were said: they did a righteous deed and another evil one; then the meaning of mixing was added to the doing, and both were expressed together by it.

dervis-irab:48-51.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدِ ابْتَغَوُا الْفِتْنَةَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَقَلَّبُوا لَكَ الْأُمُورَ): the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; ابتغوا الفتنة is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من قبل is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ابتغوا, and قبل is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. before the expedition of Tabūk. وقلبوا لك الأمور is conjoined to what precedes it. Turning affairs over (taqlīb al-amr) is managing it in various ways to contrive a stratagem and a plot; a man who handles all kinds of stratagems is called "ḥuwwal qullab" (wily, resourceful). (حَتَّى جاءَ الْحَقُّ وَظَهَرَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَهُمْ كارِهُونَ): حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition, i.e. they continued turning affairs over, weaving intrigues and plotting by night [until…]. جاء الحق is a verb and its fāʿil, and ظهر أمر الله is also a verb and its fāʿil. وهم كارهون: the wāw is circumstantial, هم كارهون is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ ائْذَنْ لِي وَلا تَفْتِنِّي): the wāw is a conjunction; منهم is a fronted khabar and من, a relative noun, is the delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause يقول is the ṣila (relative clause); ائذن is an imperative verb, and لي a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تفتني is jussive (majzūm) by لا; the nūn is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya); and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi. (أَلا فِي الْفِتْنَةِ سَقَطُوا): ألا is a particle of alerting; في الفتنة is attached to سقطوا; and the pronoun is plural although the speaker was one person, out of regard for the meaning. (وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكافِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); محيطة is the khabar of إنّ; and بالكافرين is attached to محيطة. The speech is conjoined to the preceding clause and falls within the scope of the alerting. (إِنْ تُصِبْكَ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ): إن is conditional; تصبك is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; حسنة is the fāʿil; and تسؤهم is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(وَإِنْ تُصِبْكَ مُصِيبَةٌ يَقُولُوا قَدْ أَخَذْنا أَمْرَنا مِنْ قَبْلُ): conjoined to what preceded. The meaning of أخذنا أمرنا is: we forestalled and avoided every mistake and took the means of caution, wariness, guarding and resolve. (وَيَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ فَرِحُونَ): يتولوا is conjoined to يقولوا, i.e. they turn away from the Prophet's gathering; the wāw is circumstantial; هم فرحون is a mubtadaʾ and khabar; and the nominal clause is a ḥāl from the two pronouns in يقولوا and يتولوا, not from the last only, because the rejoicing accompanies both of them together. (قُلْ لَنْ يُصِيبَنا إِلَّا ما كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنا): the clause لن يصيبنا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is the fāʿil; and the clause كتب الله لنا is the ṣila; i.e. say this to them to overthrow the false belief on which they built their joy and delight. (هُوَ مَوْلانا): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl from الله. (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the fāʾ is causal; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتوكل; the lām is the lām of command; يتوكل is jussive by the lām; and المتوكلون is the fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source writes «المتوكلون», but the word in the verse is الْمُؤْمِنُونَ, which is the fāʿil.]

* Rhetoric:
There is majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in His saying «ألا في الفتنة سقطوا», the relation being that of the occupant (al-ḥāliyya), i.e. into Hell: the occupant was mentioned and the place was meant. For a person does not fall into fitna, since it is an abstract notion; he only comes into its place. So using الفتنة for its place is a trope in which the occupant is mentioned and the place is meant.

* Benefits:
History relates that when the Prophet ﷺ prepared for the expedition of Tabūk, he said to al-Jadd ibn Qays: "O Abū Wahb, would you like to fight the Banū al-Aṣfar?" — they were the kings of the Byzantines. Al-Jadd said: "The Anṣār know that I am infatuated with women, so do not tempt me with the daughters of al-Aṣfar" — meaning the Byzantine women — "but I will help you with my wealth, so leave me."

dervis-irab:52-54.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنا إِلَّا إِحْدَى الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ): هل is an interrogative particle; تربصون is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped, i.e. "you wait"; بنا is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تربصون; إلا is a particle of restriction; and إحدى الحسنيين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَنَحْنُ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمْ أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِعَذابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ أَوْ بِأَيْدِينا): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; نحن is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause نتربص is the khabar (predicate); بكم is attached to نتربص; أن and what is within its scope is the mafʿūl bihi; الله is the fāʿil (agent); بعذاب is attached to يصيبكم; من عنده is an adjective of عذاب; and أو بأيدينا is conjoined to من عنده, i.e. "with a punishment by our hands".
(فَتَرَبَّصُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُتَرَبِّصُونَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), and تربصوا is an imperative verb, i.e. if you want to know the outcomes and what each of us and of you will meet, then wait. إنّ and its noun; معكم is an adverb attached to متربصون; and متربصون is the khabar of إنا. (قُلْ أَنْفِقُوا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً): the clause أنفقوا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the wāw is the fāʿil; طوعا and كرها are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "willingly or unwillingly". (لَنْ يُتَقَبَّلَ مِنْكُمْ إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ): لن is a particle of negation, of the subjunctive (naṣb) and of the future; يتقبل, being passive, is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by لن; منكم is attached to يتقبل; إنّ and its noun, and the clause كنتم قوما, made of كان with its noun and khabar, is the khabar of إنّ; and فاسقين is an adjective of قوما. (وَما مَنَعَهُمْ أَنْ تُقْبَلَ مِنْهُمْ نَفَقاتُهُمْ إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَبِرَسُولِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction and ما negating; منعهم is a verb and mafʿūl bihi; أن تقبل: أن and what is within its scope is the second object of منع; منهم is attached to تقبل; نفقاتهم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); إلا is a particle of restriction; and أنّ with what is within its scope is the fāʿil of منع, i.e. nothing at all prevented the acceptance of their spending except their disbelief and what is conjoined to it. (وَلا يَأْتُونَ الصَّلاةَ إِلَّا وَهُمْ كُسالى): the wāw is a conjunction and لا negating; يأتون الصلاة is an imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; إلا is a particle of restriction; هم كسالى is a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the wāw is circumstantial and the clause is a ḥāl.
(وَلا يُنْفِقُونَ إِلَّا وَهُمْ كارِهُونَ): conjoined to what preceded.

* Rhetoric:
The art of al-taʿaṭṭuf (turning back) or al-mushāraka (sharing):
It is that the speaker attaches a word of the speech to one meaning, then brings it back exactly and attaches it to another meaning, the two being separated, each word of them at one end of the speech. It occurs in His saying: «قل هل تربصون بنا إلا إحدى الحسنيين ونحن نتربص بكم أن يصيبكم الله بعذاب من عنده فتربصوا إنا معكم متربصون». The taʿaṭṭuf came at the beginning of the verse in His saying «تربصون بنا» and at its end in His saying «فتربصوا إنا معكم متربصون», together with the paronomasia of pairing (tajnīs al-izdiwāj). Along with the taʿaṭṭuf there occurs a correspondence in meaning (muqābala maʿnawiyya), in which the speech takes the form of concision by omission (ījāz al-ḥadhf). For what eloquence would require as the implied arrangement of the wording is: "Say: do you wait for us except one of the two best things: that Allah strike us with a punishment from Himself or by your hands; and we wait for you that Allah strike you with a punishment from Himself or by our hands." So, aiming at concision, He omitted the explanation of الحسنيين from the first clause and stated it in the second clause, fleeing from repeating and multiplying the wording; just as He omitted الحسنيين from the second clause, dispensing with it by having mentioned it first. Thus in the verse there came together taʿaṭṭuf, muqābala, ījāz and tafsīr (explanation), and four kinds of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment) were completed in it. This is lawful magic — "and indeed some eloquence is magic."
[Translator's note: the reconstruction quoted for the first clause («that Allah strike us with a punishment… or by your hands») is translated exactly as written in the source.]

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَسِيحُوا): al-siyāḥa is travelling. One says sāḥa fī al-arḍ yasīḥu siyāḥatan, suyūḥan and sayaḥānan (he roamed the land). From it come sayḥ al-māʾ fī al-arḍ (water flowing over the land) and sayḥ al-khayl (horses running freely), and from it are the words of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd:
لو خفت هذا منك ما فلتني ... حتى ترى خيلا أمامي تسيح
(Had I feared this from you, you would not have escaped me until you saw horses racing before me.)

* I'rab:
(بَراءَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): براءة is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a disavowal"; من الله is a naʿt (adjective) of براءة — it [من] indicates the starting point and is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of براءة; it is not attached to البراءة [itself], as in your saying bariʾtu min al-dhanbi wa-l-dayn (I am free of the sin and the debt). The meaning is: this is a disavowal reaching [them] from Allah and His Messenger. إلى الذين is attached to what من is attached to, i.e. "reaching to those". It is also possible that براءة is a mubtadaʾ — beginning with it [though indefinite] being permissible because it is specified by the adjective — and that إلى الذين is its khabar, as you say: rajulun min Tamīm fī al-dār (a man of Tamīm is in the house). من المشركين is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Tabūk, the hypocrites were spreading alarming rumours and the polytheists began breaking their covenants. That is the word of the Exalted «وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة» to the end of the verse. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did what he was commanded and cast their covenants back to them. Al-Zajjāj said: i.e. Allah and His Messenger are free of fulfilling their covenants when they have broken them. What history relates will come in the section of Benefits.
(فَسِيحُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); the clause سيحوا is the maqūl al-qawl (object) of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "so say, O Muslims, to the polytheists: travel"; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to سيحوا; أربعة أشهر is an adverb of time attached to سيحوا. What is meant by the four months is Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja and al-Muḥarram; and it was said: they are twenty [days] of Dhū al-Ḥijja, al-Muḥarram, Ṣafar, the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal and ten [days] of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir.
(وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; اعلموا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); أنّ and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا; أنّ and its noun, غير معجزي is its khabar, and الله is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْزِي الْكافِرِينَ): وأن is conjoined to أنكم; الله is its noun and مخزي الكافرين its khabar.
(وَأَذانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى النَّاسِ يَوْمَ الْحَجِّ الْأَكْبَرِ): the nominative of أذان is like the nominative of براءة, according to the two ways [above], and the clause is conjoined to its like. Al-adhān is announcement (al-iʿlām), in the sense of al-īdhān. من الله is its adjective or attached to it; إلى الناس is the khabar; and يوم الحج الأكبر is an adverb attached to what إلى الناس is attached to.
(أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَرَسُولُهُ): with fatḥa on the hamza of أنّ. There are two ways regarding it: one, that it is the khabar of أذان; the second, that it is an adjective, i.e. "and an announcement consisting in the disavowal". It was also said that the implied construction is "and an announcement from Allah of the disavowal", so that the [implied] bāʾ is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) itself. أنّ with its noun and its khabar; من المشركين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بريء. As for رسوله, there are several ways regarding it: first, that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "and His Messenger is free of them", omitted only because the first indicates it — and this is the soundest of the ways; and it was said that it is conjoined to the position of the noun of أنّ, or conjoined to the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the khabar. The grammatical discussions related to this verse will come in the section of Benefits.
(فَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction or resumptive; إن is conditional; تبتم is a past verb and its agent, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; هو is a mubtadaʾ and خير its khabar; and لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خير.
(وَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي اللَّهِ): وإن توليتم is conjoined to إن تبتم; أنكم is أنّ and its noun, and it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا; غير is the khabar of أنّ, and معجزي الله is the muḍāf ilayhi.
(وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; بشر is an imperative verb with a latent agent; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); بعذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بشر; and أليم is an adjective.

* Benefits:
1- What history says about the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a covenant with Quraysh on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya that they would lay down war for ten years, during which people would be safe. Khuzāʿa entered into the covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Banū Bakr entered into the covenant of Quraysh. Then Banū Bakr attacked Khuzāʿa and harmed them, and Quraysh helped them with weapons. When Banū Bakr and Quraysh had joined against Khuzāʿa and broken their covenant, ʿAmr ibn Sālim al-Khuzāʿī set out until he stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and recited:
لا هم إني ناشد محمدا ... حلف أبينا وأبيه الأتلدا
إن قريشا أخلفوك الموعدا ... ونقضوا ذمامك المؤكدا
هم بيّتونا بالحطيم هجّدا ... وقتلونا ركّعا وسجدا
(O Allah, I adjure Muhammad by the ancient alliance of our father and his father. Quraysh have broken their promise to you and violated your firm pledge; they attacked us by night at al-Ḥaṭīm while we slept, and killed us bowing and prostrating.)
He (upon him be blessing and peace) said: "May I not be helped if I do not help you," and he prepared [to march] on Mecca. He conquered it in the year eight of the Hijra. When the year nine came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to perform the Hajj, and it was said to him: "The polytheists attend and circumambulate the House naked." He said: "I do not wish to perform the Hajj until that no longer happens." So that year he sent Abū Bakr as leader of the season to establish the Hajj for the people, and sent with him forty verses from the opening of Barāʾa to recite to the people of the season. Then after him he sent ʿAlī on his she-camel al-ʿAḍbāʾ to recite to the people the opening of Barāʾa, and commanded him to proclaim at Mecca, Minā and ʿArafa that the protection of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is withdrawn from every polytheist, and that no naked person shall circumambulate the House. Abū Bakr returned and said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, has something been revealed concerning me?" He said: "No, but it is not fitting that anyone convey this except a man of my family. Are you not pleased, O Abū Bakr, that you were with me in the cave and that you will be with me at the Pool?" He said: "Indeed, O Messenger of Allah." So Abū Bakr went as leader of the pilgrims, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib proclaimed Barāʾa. On the day before the Day of Tarwiya, Abū Bakr stood and addressed the people, told them about their rites and established the Hajj for the people; the Arabs that year kept to the practices of the Hajj that they had followed in the Jāhiliyya. When the Day of Sacrifice came, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib stood and proclaimed among the people what he had been commanded and recited to them the beginning of Sūrat Barāʾa.
Yazīd ibn Tubayʿ said: We asked ʿAlī: "With what were you sent on that Hajj?" He said: "I was sent with four [things]: no naked person shall circumambulate the House; whoever has a covenant with the Prophet, it holds until its term, and whoever has no covenant, his term is four months; none shall enter Paradise except a believing soul; and the polytheists and the Muslims shall not come together in the Hajj after this year of theirs." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Farewell Hajj in the year ten.

The reason for the founding of the science of grammar:
A man was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb who was reciting «إن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله» with the genitive [i.e. wa-rasūlihi]. He asked him, and he said: "This is how I was taught to recite it in Medina." ʿUmar said: "It is not so; it is only wa-rasūluhu, with ḍamma on the lām, for Allah does not disavow His Messenger." Then he ordered that none should recite the Qur'an except one learned in Arabic, and he summoned Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī and ordered him to lay down grammar. What this report entails is that this science was not known before Abū al-Aswad, and that people's speech before him was by mere natural disposition, which is the familiar view.
Further, it is well known that Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī was the first to lay down the science of grammar. They said that one day he heard his daughter make a grammatical error (laḥn), so he went to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said to him: "Errors have spread among our children, and I fear that the language will be lost." The Imam said to him: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. All speech is three: noun, verb and particle. The noun is such-and-such, the verb such-and-such and the particle such-and-such. Nouns are three: overt, pronominal and vague (mubham). The agent is always nominative, the object always accusative, and the annexed [i.e. the muḍāf ilayhi] always genitive. So understand and draw analogies, and whatever additions occur to you, join them [to it]."
However, al-Suyūṭī said in al-Muzhir that prosody and grammar were ancient, and time passed over them until they became scarce in people's hands, so al-Khalīl and Abū al-Aswad renewed them. He argued for the antiquity of prosody with what he set out at length there, and for the antiquity of grammar with [evidence] including the writing of the Muṣḥaf in the manner that the grammarians explain with regard to words with wāw, yāʾ and hamza, and lengthening and shortening: they wrote words with [final radical] yāʾ with yāʾ, and words with wāw with alif.
We support this original view of al-Suyūṭī, arguing from the following:
1- ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib's explanation to Abū al-Aswad of a number of previously established technical rules; for it is unlikely that these were inspired to the Imam specifically. It is also made unlikely by his saying to Abū al-Aswad: "Whatever additions occur to you, join them to it", i.e. of the kind of these rules. This is explicit, or nearly explicit, that this science was known among them, or among individuals of them, and not mere correctness of pronunciation by instinct.
2- The words of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: "None shall recite the Qur'an except one learned in the Arabic language." What comes first to mind from this is its rules and principles, by which the aspects of speech are known with the help of context. For if what were meant were merely those who speak correctly, it would entail barring every non-Arab from it, and there would be no reason to single out the one learned in the language with regard to the Arabs, since the people were all Bedouin Arabs of naturally sound tongues. His permitting the Qur'an to one who was knowledgeable and not to others is explicit that among them were those knowledgeable of the language and those ignorant of it; so the knowledge of the knowledgeable must have been something beyond what the others had, and that can only be the rules and principles.
3- Since the science of prosody and its technical terms were known to some of the Arabs — as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra stated explicitly when he said about the Qur'an, when it was said to be poetry: "I have measured it against its hazaj and its rajaz, and I did not find it resembling any of that" — and poetry belonged only to individuals among the Arabs, then it is all the more fitting that the rules of Arabic, which was the tongue of them all, were known to some of them.

dervis-irab:105-110.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُرْجَوْنَ): a passive participle from أرجيته, i.e. I postponed it; one also says أرجأته with a hamza, and from it comes [the name of the sect] al-Murjiʾa.
(وَإِرْصاداً): and as a preparation and a lying in wait.
(شَفا): an edge, a brink.
(جُرُفٍ): with ḍamma on the rāʾ or with sukūn, the side of a well that has not been lined [with stone]. It is also said to be the chasm, and what the torrent sweeps away of the valleys. Abū ʿUbayda said — and it is also said — that it is the place which the water eats away and sweeps off (يجرفه), i.e. carries away.
(هارٍ): there are three views about it. The first, which is the well-known one, is that it is metathesised (maqlūb), its lām being placed before its ʿayn. That is because its original form is هاور or هاير, with wāw or yāʾ, since both letters are heard in it: they said هار يهور and يهار, and هار يهير, and تهوّر البناء and تهيّر (the building collapsed). So the lām, which is the rāʾ, was placed before the ʿayn, which is the wāw or yāʾ, and it became like غاز and رام, and was weakened by deficiency (naqṣ) as they are weakened. Its pattern after the metathesis is فالع, and then after the omission it came down to فال. The second view is that its ʿayn was omitted arbitrarily, i.e. without any necessitating cause; on this view the case inflections run on its lām, so one says هذا هارٌ، ورأيت هاراً، ومررت بهارٍ, and its pattern is likewise فال. The third view is that there is neither metathesis nor omission in it, and that its original form is هَوِر or هَيِر; the weak letter was voweled and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif, and the case inflections likewise run on it as in the previous view, just as you say هذا بابٌ، ورأيت باباً، ومررت ببابٍ. This is the most balanced of the views because it is spared from claiming metathesis and omission, both of which are contrary to the base, but it is not well known among the morphologists. The meaning of هار is crumbling, falling and collapsing.

* I'rab:
(وَقُلِ اعْمَلُوا فَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the clause (اعملوا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa [indicating an implied condition]; the sīn is with regard to the recompense, not to knowledge, because the knowledge already exists and is not bound by time. (الله) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يرى), (عملكم) is its object, and (رسوله) and (المؤمنون) are conjoined to (الله). (وَسَتُرَدُّونَ إِلى عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ): conjoined to (سيرى); (إلى عالم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تردون); (الغيب) is a muḍāf ilayhi, and (الشهادة) is conjoined to (الغيب). (فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (بما) is attached to (ينبئكم), and the clause (كنتم تعملون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ): a coordination by conjunction with what preceded, i.e. "and others who confessed"; (مرجون) is its naʿt (adjective) and (لأمر الله) is attached to (مرجون). That is: and others among those who stayed behind whose matter is suspended.
(إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): (إما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (يعذبهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they are deferred, either to be punished or to be forgiven. (إما) here is for doubt with respect to the addressee, and for leaving the matter vague (ibhām) with respect to Allah the Exalted, meaning that He the Exalted left their matter and their fate vague to the addressees. We may also parse (آخرون) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with (مرجون) as its naʿt and the clause (إما يعذبهم) as the khabar (predicate) of (آخرون); (وإما يتوب عليهم) is conjoined; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (عليم حكيم) are its two predicates. (وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مَسْجِداً ضِراراً وَكُفْراً وَتَفْرِيقاً بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): you have two options for (الذين): the accusative by specification for blame (ikhtiṣāṣ bi-l-dhamm), like His saying «والمقيمين الصلاة» by specification for praise; or the nominative as a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, its meaning being "among those we have described are those who took", like the saying of Allah the Exalted «والسارق والسارقة». This view is the one Sībawayh approved, and his statement on it has been given in full before; its implied form is "among what is recited to you are those who…", so the khabar was omitted and the mubtadaʾ kept. The wāw is resumptive in either case. The clause (اتخذوا) is the ṣila; (مسجدا) is a direct object; (ضرارا) is a second object of (اتخذوا), or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. they cause harm thereby, a harming, or a ḥāl, i.e. causing harm to their brothers; all these views are of equal weight. (كفرا) and (تفريقا) are conjoined to (ضرارا), and (بين) is an adverb attached to (تفريقا). (وَإِرْصاداً لِمَنْ حارَبَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ): (وإرصادا) is also conjoined; (لمن حارب الله) is attached to (إرصادا); the clause (حارب الله) is the ṣila; and (من قبل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (حارب). (وَلَيَحْلِفُنَّ إِنْ أَرَدْنا إِلَّا الْحُسْنى): the lām falls in the answer to an implied oath; (إن) is negative; (أردنا) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is the answer to the oath; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (الحسنى) is the object of (أردنا). (وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يشهد) is the khabar; (إنّ) with what falls under it is the object of (يشهد); (إنّ) and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (كاذبون) is its khabar. The story of the Mosque of Harm will come in the section on Benefits. (لا تَقُمْ فِيهِ أَبَداً): (لا) is prohibitive; (تقم) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the prohibitive (لا); (فيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تقم); (أبدا) is an adverb also attached to (تقم), i.e. do not pray in it ever. (لَمَسْجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلَى التَّقْوى مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَقُومَ فِيهِ): the lām is of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (مسجد) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (أسس على التقوى) is a naʿt of (مسجد), (على التقوى) being a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أسس); (أحق) is its khabar; (من أول يوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, or to (أسس); (أن تقوم) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "for that you stand in it", attached to (أحق); and (فيه) is attached to (تقوم). (فِيهِ رِجالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَتَطَهَّرُوا وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُطَّهِّرِينَ): (فيه) is a fronted khabar and (رجال) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause (يحبون) is a naʿt of (رجال); (أن) with what falls under it is the object of (يحبون), i.e. they love purity from sins, crimes and acts of disobedience. It is also said: from sins, the purity of the inner self, and from ritual impurities (aḥdāth), the purity of the outer self. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يحب المطهرين) is the khabar. (أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى تَقْوى مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٍ خَيْرٌ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), and the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something implied, i.e. "after their state has become known, is then he who founded his building on piety…" etc. (من) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (أسس بنيانه) is the ṣila; (على تقوى) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أسس); (من الله) is a naʿt of (تقوى); (رضوان) is conjoined to (تقوى); and (خير) is the khabar of (من). (أَمْ مَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى شَفا جُرُفٍ هارٍ): (أم) is a conjunction and (من) is conjoined to the first (من); its khabar is omitted, its implied form being "better"; (على شفا جرف هار) is attached to (أسس). (فَانْهارَ بِهِ فِي نارِ جَهَنَّمَ وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction and (انهار) is conjoined to (أسس). Its agent is either the pronoun of the building or the pronoun of the bank (الجرف), and the latter is preferable, because its collapse entails the collapse of both the brink and the building, while their collapse, or the collapse of one of them, does not entail its collapse. (به) is attached to (انهار) if the bāʾ is for transitivity, and to an omitted ḥāl if it is for accompaniment; both are permissible. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يهدي القوم الظالمين) is the khabar. (لا يَزالُ بُنْيانُهُمُ الَّذِي بَنَوْا رِيبَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ): (بنيانهم) is the noun of (لا يزال); (الذي) is a naʿt of (بنيانهم); the clause (بنوا) is the ṣila; (ريبة) is the khabar of (لا يزال); and (في قلوبهم) is a naʿt of (ريبة). (إِلَّا أَنْ تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): an exception from the most general of times, so the thing excepted from is accordingly omitted, i.e. their building will remain a doubt at every one of the times except the time of their hearts being cut up. (أن) is maṣdar-forming, and (تقطع), originally (تتقطع), is accusative by it; (قلوبهم) is the agent; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (عليم حكيم) are its two predicates.

* Rhetoric:
These verses comprise several arts of rhetoric, which we list below:
1- The art of tardīd (repetition with a shifted reference): the speaker attaches a word of the speech to one meaning, then repeats the very same word and attaches it to another meaning, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون، يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة»: the first يعلمون is negated and the second affirmed, and each of the two meanings has an appropriateness that called for that meaning. Likewise His saying with which we are concerned: «لمسجد أسس على التقوى من أول يوم أحق أن تقوم فيه، فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا»: the first فيه is attached to تقوم and the second فيه is a fronted khabar, and each of them has a meaning.
Among the examples of tardīd in poetry is a verse that occurs in lines spoken by Sayf al-Dawla. He had a slave girl, one of the daughters of the Byzantines, without whom he did not see the world [worth anything], and he feared for her even from the blowing wind. All his other concubines envied her for the tenderness of her place with him and resolved to do her some harm, by poison or otherwise. This reached Sayf al-Dawla, so he ordered that she be moved to one of the fortresses as a precaution for her life, and he said about that:
راقبتني العيون فيك فأشفقت ولم أخل قط من إشفاق ورأيت العذول يحسدني فيك مجدّا يا أنفس الأعلاق
(Eyes watched me on your account, so I grew fearful — and I was never free of fear; and I saw the censurer envying me earnestly on your account, O most precious of treasures.)
فتسنيت أن تكوني بعيدا ... والذي بيننا من الود باق
(So I arranged that you be far away, while the love between us remains.)
رب هجر يكون من خوف هجر ... وفراق يكون خوف فراق
(Many a desertion comes from fear of desertion, and many a parting from fear of parting.)
[Translator's note: the first two hemistich-pairs are printed in the source as continuous prose; they are given here as printed.]
2- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من الله», i.e. on a firmly rooted, stable, solid foundation, namely piety towards Allah. Piety and good pleasure are likened to a foundation on which a building rests, the likening being concealed in the mind (istiʿāra makniyya), and "founded his building" is an imaginative attribution (takhyīl) on the pattern of the explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya).
3- Extended metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in the collapse of the building standing on the brink of a crumbling bank. Neglecting to uphold the matters of religion is likened to one whose building was built on a brink, so that it falls with him. The thing likened to is building on a spot about to fall, and the thing likened is arranging the rulings and works of religion on unbelief and hypocrisy.

* Benefits:
The story of the Mosque of Harm (masjid al-ḍirār):
History relates that when Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf built the mosque of Qubāʾ, they sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to come to them; he came to them and prayed in it. Their brothers, Banū Ghanm ibn ʿAwf, envied them and said: "We shall build a mosque and send to the Messenger of Allah to pray in it, and Abū ʿĀmir the monk will pray in it when he comes from Syria", so as to establish for themselves merit and superiority over their brothers. [Abū ʿĀmir] is the one whom the Messenger of Allah named "the corrupt one" (al-fāsiq); he said to the Messenger of Allah on the day of Uḥud: "I will not find any people fighting you but I will fight you along with them." He went on fighting him until the day of Ḥunayn; when Hawāzin were routed, he went out fleeing to Syria and sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Caesar, and I will bring troops and drive Muhammad and his companions out of Medina." So they built a mosque beside the mosque of Qubāʾ and said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We have built a mosque for those with illness and need, and for the rainy night and the winter night, and we would like you to pray for us in it and invoke blessing for us." The Prophet said: "I am on the point of travelling and in a state of preoccupation; when we return, if Allah wills, we shall pray in it." When he returned from the expedition of Tabūk, they asked him to come to the mosque, and [this passage] was revealed to him. He called for Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum, Maʿn ibn ʿAdī, ʿĀmir ibn al-Sakan and Waḥshī and said to them: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, and demolish it and burn it." They did so, and he ordered that its site be made a rubbish dump into which carcasses and refuse were thrown. Abū ʿĀmir died in Syria, at Qinnasrīn.

dervis-irab:55-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُعْجِبْكَ): to admire (al-iʿjāb) a thing is to be pleased with it with the pleasure of one who is content with it and wonders at its beauty. The meaning is: do not think well of, and do not be lured by, what they have been given of the adornment and tinsel of this world. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Wonder (al-taʿajjub) is used in two ways. One is for what the doer praises, and its meaning is approval and stating his satisfaction with it; the second is for what he dislikes, and its meaning is disapproval and blame of it. For approval one says أعجبني (it pleased me), and for blame and disapproval عجبت, on the pattern of تعبت."
(يَفْرَقُونَ): they fear. In al-Mukhtār: "فرق, فرقا, of the pattern of تعب: he feared; it is made transitive with the hamza, so one says أفرقته (I frightened him)."
(مَغاراتٍ): plural of مغارة, which is a low place in the ground or in a mountain. al-ghawr, with fatḥa, of anything is its bottom; al-ghawr is the depressed land; غار الرجل غورا: the man came to the ghawr, which is the low land, and أغار with the alif is the same. al-ghār, al-maghār and al-maghāra are like a cave in a mountain, and al-kahf is like a house in a mountain, its plural kuhūf. Then look at the precision in the ordering, through which the composition of the speech reaches the loftiest limits: He first mentioned the most general thing, which is a refuge of whatever kind; then He mentioned the caves in which one hides in the highest places, namely the mountains; then the places in which one hides in low places, which He expressed by المدخل.
(يَجْمَحُونَ): they hasten with a haste that nothing turns back, from the jamūḥ horse, which, when it charges, the bridle cannot hold back. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "جمح الفرس براكبه يجمح, with two fatḥas, of the pattern of خضع, jimāḥan with kasra and jumūḥan: the horse became unruly until it overpowered him; so it is jamūḥ with fatḥa, and jāmiḥ, the masculine and feminine being alike in it."
(يَلْمِزُكَ): he finds fault with you in the division of the alms and attacks you. In al-Miṣbāḥ:
"لمزه لمزا, of the pattern of ضرب: he found fault with him — and the Seven read with it — and of the pattern of قتل is a dialect variant. Its origin is signalling with the eye and the like." So it is more specific than al-ghamz, since that is signalling with the eye and the like, whether it is by way of belittling or not, while al-lamz is specifically by way of finding fault. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "غمزه غمزا, of the pattern of ضرب: he signalled to him with an eye or an eyebrow."

* I'rab:
(فَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction — the secret of its use will come; لا is prohibitive; تعجبك is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you". [Translator's note: the source says «والفاعل مستتر تقديره أنت» (the fāʿil is latent, "you"), although it then names أموالهم as the fāʿil; the kāf of تعجبك is the addressee. Translated as written.] The address, although directed to the Prophet ﷺ, is meant for all the believers. أموالهم is the fāʿil (agent), and ولا أولادهم is conjoined to it. (إِنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ بِها فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); يريد الله is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the lām is causal; يعذبهم is subjunctive by an implied أن; the lām was brought for reinforcement, the origin being يريد أن يعذبهم; بها is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعذبهم; and في الحياة الدنيا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَتَزْهَقَ أَنْفُسُهُمْ وَهُمْ كافِرُونَ): «تزهق» is conjoined to «ليعذبهم»; أنفسهم is the fāʿil; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and كافرون the khabar (predicate). (وَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُمْ لَمِنْكُمْ وَما هُمْ مِنْكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; يحلفون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحلفون; إنّ and its noun, the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and منكم is its khabar; the wāw is circumstantial; ما is the Ḥijāzī negating ما, هم is its noun and منكم its khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. (وَلكِنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ يَفْرَقُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لكنّ and its noun, قوم is its khabar, and the clause يفرقون is an adjective.
(لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأً أَوْ مَغاراتٍ أَوْ مُدَّخَلًا لَوَلَّوْا إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ): لو is conditional; يجدون ملجأ is an imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أو مغارات أو مدخلا are both conjoined to ملجأ. لولوا: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; إليه is attached to ولوا; وهم: the wāw is circumstantial, هم is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يحجمون is the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. [Translator's note: the source writes «يحجمون»; the word in the verse is يَجْمَحُونَ.] The clause لولوا has no grammatical position. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَلْمِزُكَ فِي الصَّدَقاتِ): the wāw is a conjunction; منهم is a fronted khabar and من a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause يلمزك is the ṣila (relative clause); and في الصدقات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يلمزك. (فَإِنْ أُعْطُوا مِنْها رَضُوا وَإِنْ لَمْ يُعْطَوْا مِنْها إِذا هُمْ يَسْخَطُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; أعطوا is a passive past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منها is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi, because the wāw, which is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), is its first object; وإن لم يعطوا منها is conjoined to the first clause; إذا is the إذا of surprise (fujāʾiyya); هم is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يسخطون the khabar; and the clause إذا هم يسخطون is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because «إذا» takes the place of the fāʾ. (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ رَضُوا ما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ): أنّ and what is within its scope is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, i.e. "if their contentment were established"; ما is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause آتاهم الله ورسوله is the ṣila. (وَقالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ سَيُؤْتِينَا اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَرَسُولُهُ): حسبنا is the mubtadaʾ and الله the khabar, or the reverse, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); سيؤتينا الله is an imperfect verb, mafʿūl bihi and fāʿil; من فضله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤتينا; and رسوله is conjoined to الله. (إِنَّا إِلَى اللَّهِ راغِبُونَ): إنّ and its noun; إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to راغبون; and راغبون is the khabar of إنا. (إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقاتُ لِلْفُقَراءِ وَالْمَساكِينِ وَالْعامِلِينَ عَلَيْها وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ): إنما is kāffa wa-makfūfa, and it is for restriction (qaṣr): it restricted the alms to the enumerated categories. الصدقات is the mubtadaʾ and للفقراء the khabar; المساكين is conjoined to الفقراء; العاملين عليها is also conjoined, by which He meant the collectors who receive it: the levier, the distributor, the clerk, the gatherer and the accountant. المؤلفة قلوبهم is also conjoined to what preceded, and قلوبهم is the nāʾib fāʿil. (وَفِي الرِّقابِ وَالْغارِمِينَ وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ): وفي الرقاب is conjoined to His saying للفقراء, i.e. "and spent on the necks", and a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "and on freeing the necks". الغارمين is also conjoined, i.e. those who are weighed down by debts, if they borrowed for something other than sin, or to reconcile between people. في سبيل الله is also conjoined, i.e. those carrying out jihad. ابن السبيل is also conjoined: he is the one cut off [from his means], so he is poor where he is, rich where his wealth is. (فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "Allah has ordained that as an ordinance". It is permissible to parse it as a ḥāl from الفقراء and those after them, i.e. the alms are only for them, being an ordinance. It is of the pattern faʿīla in the sense of mafrūḍa (ordained); the tāʾ entered it — although its due is that masculine and feminine be alike in it — because it is treated like nouns, like al-naṭīḥa. من الله is an adjective; الله is the mubtadaʾ, عليم the first khabar and حكيم the second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
Varying the particles:
In His saying «إنما الصدقات للفقراء» to the end of the verse there is a charming art among the arts of eloquence, subtle in its approach and fine in its purport, which few notice. He turned from the lām to في in the last four, and that is for a secret hidden from the superficial reader: the first four categories — the poor, the needy, those working on it and those whose hearts are to be reconciled — are owners of whatever may be paid to them, so the entry of the lām suited them. As for the last four, they do not own what is spent towards them; indeed it is not paid to them at all, but on interests connected with them. The money spent on the necks is taken only by the masters who made the manumission contracts and by the sellers, so their share is not paid into their hands such that it would be expressed by the lām, which suggests their ownership of what is spent towards them; rather, they are the loci of this spending and of the interest connected with it. Likewise the workers (al-ʿāmilūn) — their share is paid only to their creditors, to free their liability, not to them. [Translator's note: the context indicates the debtors (al-ghārimūn) are meant here; the source has «العاملون».] As for the way of Allah, this is clear in it. As for the wayfarer, it is as though he was included in the way of Allah, and he was mentioned separately only to point out his special status, though he is devoid of both particles; conjoining him to the noun made genitive by the lām is possible, but [conjoining him] to what is nearer to him is more likely. When this is established, it becomes clear to you how the four imams were distinguished by delicacy of taste and correctness of intuition in deriving juristic principles from the variation of the particles. There is another aspect, which al-Zamakhsharī pointed to and Ibn al-Athīr mentioned in his delightful book «al-Mathal al-Sāʾir», which we summarize as follows:
He turned from the lām to «في» in the last three only to signal that they are more firmly established in deserving to be given alms than those mentioned before with the lām, because «في» is for the container. So He pointed out that they are worthy of having the alms placed in them as a thing is placed in a container, and of being made its proper place; that is because of the release and rescue there is in freeing necks and in [paying off] debt. The repetition of «في» in His saying «وفي سبيل الله» is evidence of its preference over the necks and the debtors. The ordinary course of speech would be to say:
"and in the necks, the debtors, the way of Allah and the wayfarer". So when «في» was brought a second time, separating the debtors from the way of Allah, it was known that the way of Allah is more emphatic in deserving spending in it. These are subtleties and fine points found only in this noble speech.

* Benefits:
Below is a delightful section written by a distinguished scholar among the scholars of al-Azhar, which we record for its authenticity regarding alms and zakāt. He said: "Zakāt is paid to eight categories:
1- The poor (al-faqīr): the one who has no wealth and no suitable earning that goes some way toward his sufficiency, in that it is less than half of what he needs, like one who needs ten and neither owns nor earns more than two or three dirhams.
2- The needy (al-miskīn): one who has wealth or earning that does not suffice him, like one who needs ten dirhams and has seven.
3- Those working on it: those striving to collect it, like the clerk of the zakāt funds.
4- Those whose hearts are to be reconciled: those who have embraced Islam while their Islam is weak, or it is strong but by giving to them the Islam of others is expected.
5- The necks: they are slaves with a valid manumission contract (mukātabūn) with someone other than the zakāt-payer.
6- The debtor (al-ghārim): one who incurred a debt for himself, the debt has fallen due and he is unable to pay it, and he intended to spend it on something permissible or did spend it on that; or who incurred a debt to reconcile between people, if the debt has fallen due and he has not paid it from his own wealth, even if he is rich; or who incurred a debt as a guarantee, if both he and the one guaranteed are in hardship.
7- The people of the way of Allah: they are the fighters volunteering for jihad, even if they are rich, as help for the jihad.
8- The wayfarer (ibn al-sabīl): the traveller on a permissible journey from the land of the zakāt, even if passing through, to his homeland or elsewhere; he is given from the zakāt funds what will bring him to his destination, if he is in need.

dervis-irab:111-112.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوالَهُمْ): a resumptive clause, brought to encourage the believers to jihad by setting out its merit and what follows upon martyrdom in the way of Allah. (إنّ) and its noun, and the clause (اشترى) is its khabar (predicate); (من المؤمنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (اشترى); (أنفسهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (أموالهم) is conjoined to (أنفسهم). (بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ): the bāʾ and what it enters on are attached to (اشترى) — more on the reality of this purchase will come under Rhetoric; (لهم) is the fronted khabar of (أنّ), and (الجنة) is its postponed noun. (يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive clause, not to explain the purchase itself — since their fighting in the way of Allah is not Allah's purchasing their selves and their wealth — but to explain the sale which the mentioned purchase calls for, as though it were asked: how do they sell them for Paradise? and it was answered: they fight. (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يقاتلون). (فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا فِي التَّوْراةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ وَالْقُرْآنِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (يَقتُلون), active, and (يُقتَلون), passive, are both conjoined to (يقاتلون). (وعدا) and (حقا) are two maṣdars (verbal nouns), accusative by their omitted verbs, i.e. He promised them a promise and that promise is due, a being-due. (في التوراة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (وعدا), i.e. a promise existing and mentioned in the Torah; it may also be attached to (اشتروا) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is (اشترى)]. (الإنجيل) and (القرآن) are conjoined to (التوراة).
(وَمَنْ أَوْفى بِعَهْدِهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أوفى) is its khabar; (بعهده) and (من الله) are attached to (أوفى).
