(فَاسْتَبْشِرُوا بِبَيْعِكُمُ الَّذِي بايَعْتُمْ بِهِ وَذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (استبشروا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (ببيعكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استبشروا); (الذي) is a naʿt; (بايعتم به) is the ṣila (relative clause); (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; (الفوز) is the khabar of (ذلك) or the khabar of (هو); and (العظيم) is a naʿt. (التَّائِبُونَ الْعابِدُونَ الْحامِدُونَ السَّائِحُونَ الرَّاكِعُونَ السَّاجِدُونَ الْآمِرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَالنَّاهُونَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَالْحافِظُونَ لِحُدُودِ اللَّهِ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ):
predicates of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the repentant, the worshippers…" etc., that is, by way of praise. Al-Zajjāj permitted it to be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. the repentant, the worshippers are also among the people of Paradise, «وان ثم يجاهدوا» [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently a misprint for وإن لم يجاهدوا, "even if they do not wage jihad"]. It is also said that it is nominative as a badal (substitute) from the wāw in (يقاتلون). The upshot of what is mentioned is nine qualities: the first six relate to dealings with the Creator, the seventh and eighth relate to dealings with created beings, and the ninth covers both groups. (وبشر المؤمنين): the wāw is a conjunction; (بشر) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) agent; and (المؤمنين) is a direct object.

* Rhetoric:
These verses contain kinds of rhetoric which we set out below:
1- The dependent implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-tabaʿiyya) in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة». He borrowed "purchase" for Allah the Exalted's accepting from the believers their selves and their wealth which they expended in His way, and His rewarding them in return for it with Paradise. Then He made the thing sold — which is the mainstay and the aim in the contract — the selves and wealth of the believers, and made the price — which is the means in the transaction — Paradise.
2- The shift of person (iltifāt) in His saying «فاستبشروا», as an increase in their joy. The fāʾ al-faṣīḥa is for making the command to rejoice follow upon what precedes it and making that equivalent to a condition for it. The sīn is not for request but for compliance (muṭāwaʿa), as in استوقد.
3- Tadhyīl (appended confirmation): the speaker appends to his speech, after its meaning is complete, a clause that confirms what precedes it. This addition is of two kinds:
a- A kind that adds nothing to the first meaning but only emphasises and confirms it.
b- A kind that the speaker casts in the form of a current proverb so that the meaning becomes widely known through its frequent circulation on tongues. Both kinds have come in this noble verse:
a- His saying: «وعدا عليه حقا», for the speech was complete and finished before that, then the clause of tadhyīl came to confirm and emphasise what precedes it.
b- His saying: «ومن أوفى بعهده من الله», casting it in the form of a proverb. So glory be to the One who speaks such speech!

* Benefits:
1- The wāw of eight (wāw al-thamāniya): Allah enumerated nine qualities and did not join them with the wāw until, when the eighth came, He brought in the wāw. That is because of a secret in their speech, namely that the Arabs have a wāw they called "the wāw of eight", which enters on whatever is eighth. Thus some scholars asserted, and others refuted them, at great length and in detail. Since the discussion on this topic is not without enjoyment and benefit, we think it best to summarise it as follows:
Those who affirm this wāw cite as evidence the saying of Allah the Exalted «وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها»: He brought the wāw here and did not bring it in mentioning Hell, because the Fire has seven gates and Paradise eight; and the saying of Allah the Exalted «ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم». Some of the verifying scholars rejected this and said: it [the wāw] occurs only between two opposites, because the previously married (الثيبات) are other than the virgins (الأبكار) in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ثيبات وأبكارا», and because those who command are the opposite of those who forbid in the verse we are discussing. Abū Ḥayyān said: "When adjectives are repeated and are for praise, blame or compassion, it is permitted for them to follow the qualified noun, or to be cut off [from its case] in all of them or some of them; and when the two descriptions are distinct from each other, conjunction is permitted. Since commanding is distinct from forbidding — for commanding is the request to do an act and forbidding is [the request for] leaving an act — conjunction was fitting in His saying والناهون. The claim of redundancy, or of the wāw of eight, is weak." And he said about the story of the People of the Cave: "He brought the wāw with the eight only because the third statement is closer to the truth, or is the truth, because He said of the [first] two statements «رجما بالغيب» (guessing at the unseen), and of the third He said: «قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم»." And he said about the story of the people of Paradise — where He affirmed the wāw — that it is because the gates of Hell are opened only when its people enter, as an increase in the constriction upon those in it, whereas the gates of Paradise are opened for its people before they enter it, to honour them, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted «جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب». Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn al-Ḥājib, may Allah have mercy on him, said: al-Qāḍī al-Fāḍil used to believe the wāw redundant in this verse, meaning «ثيبات وأبكارا», and used to say it is the wāw of eight — until he mentioned that in the presence of Shaykh Abū al-Jūd the Qur'an-reciter, who made clear to him that it was a mistake and that necessity calls for its entry here, otherwise the meaning would be corrupted, unlike the wāw of eight, which is brought without need. So he said: "You have guided us, O Abū al-Jūd."
We say: among those who acknowledged the wāw of eight is Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī in his Great Commentary (al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr); he said that the wāw in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وثامنهم كلبهم» is the wāw of eight.
Further discussion of it will come when speaking about these verses in their places.

السائحون (al-sāʾiḥūn):
The scholars differed about the third quality [Translator's note: so in the source; السائحون is the fourth in the verse's list], namely السائحون. The soundest of the views is that they are those who fast; they were likened to those who travel through the land (siyāḥa) in their abstaining from their desires. It is also said that they are the seekers of knowledge, who seek it where it is to be found and journey through the regions of the earth to acquire it. In al-Qāmūs: "السياحة, with kasra, is going about the land for worship, and from it [comes the name] al-Masīḥ son of Maryam. السائح is one who fasts, persevering in siyāḥa."

dervis-irab:4-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المرصد): a noun of place for the spot where the enemy sits [in wait], or which he passes by or crosses, so it is like mamarr (passage) and mujtāz (crossing). It is from raṣadtu al-shayʾ, when I watched for the thing.

* I'rab:
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): there are two ways regarding this exception (istithnāʾ):
The first is that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), i.e. "but those with whom you made a covenant — their ruling is such-and-such"; so الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause فأتموا. The second is that it is connected (muttaṣil), so that it is excepted from the polytheists in the words of the Exalted «براءة من الله ورسوله» up to «الذين عاهدتم من المشركين». They were Banū Ḍamra, a clan of Kināna. Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to complete their covenant until its term, and nine months of their term remained. The reason for this was that they had not broken the covenant. The meaning in either case is: do not treat the innocent like the guilty, nor the faithful like the treacherous. The clause عاهدتم is the ṣila (relative clause), and من المشركين is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنْقُصُوكُمْ شَيْئاً وَلَمْ يُظاهِرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَحَداً): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and the jussive; ينقصوكم is jussive (majzūm) by لم; شيئا is either a second object of naqaṣa, since it is transitive to one or two objects, or a maṣdar (verbal noun) as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "anything of diminution", or "neither little nor much of diminution". لم يظاهروا is conjoined to لم ينقصوكم; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يظاهروا; and أحدا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. they did not help any enemy against you, as Banū Bakr attacked Khuzāʿa — whose story has preceded.
(فَأَتِمُّوا إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ إِلى مُدَّتِهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أتموا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أتموا; عهدهم is the direct object; إلى مدتهم is a badal (substitute) of إليهم; and إنّ and its noun, with the clause يحب المتقين as its khabar.
(فَإِذَا انْسَلَخَ الْأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُمُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction or resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause انسلخ is annexed to the adverb; الأشهر is the agent and الحرم a naʿt (adjective). It has preceded that they are Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja and al-Muḥarram, which are the months in which the covenant-breakers were permitted to travel freely.
(فَاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ): the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; اقتلوا المشركين is an imperative verb, its agent and its object; حيث is an adverb attached to اقتلوا; and the clause وجدتموهم is annexed to the adverb.
(وَخُذُوهُمْ وَاحْصُرُوهُمْ وَاقْعُدُوا لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ): خذوهم is conjoined to اقتلوا, i.e. "and take them captive"; احصروهم is also conjoined, i.e. "restrain them and prevent them from moving about the land"; اقعدوا is also conjoined; لهم is attached to اقعدوا; and كل مرصد is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), as in His words «لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم» — this is the preference of al-Zajjāj. Some preferred that it be accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the implied preposition being «على», or «the locative bāʾ», or «في». It may also be parsed as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, as though it were said: "and watch for them with every watching". Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī judged al-Zajjāj mistaken in making it an adverb.
(فَإِنْ تابُوا وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكاةَ فَخَلُّوا سَبِيلَهُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; تابوا is a verb and its agent, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); أقاموا الصلاة is conjoined to تابوا, and likewise His words وآتوا الزكاة; فخلوا: the fāʾ links [the apodosis], خلوا is an imperative verb and its agent, and سبيلهم is the direct object.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): its i'rab has preceded.

dervis-irab:6-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الإلّ): the lexicographers and exegetes differed greatly over this word. In Asās al-Balāgha: «لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلّا ولا ذمة», i.e. kinship. In al-Qāmūs and its commentaries: al-ill is covenant, the protected neighbour, good lineage, enmity and rancour. Abū ʿUbayda said that what is meant by it is covenant; al-Farrāʾ said that what is meant by it is kinship. Others said that al-ill is al-juʾār, which is raising the voice when making an alliance — for when they made alliances they would cry out loudly with it. It was also said to be from alla al-barq, when the lightning flashed. Al-ill has as its plural of paucity ālul [written آلّ in the source]; its origin is aʾlul on the pattern afʿul, then the second hamza was changed into an alif because it follows another hamza with fatḥa, and the lām was assimilated into the lām. A verse of Ḥassān ibn Thābit was recited:
لعمرك إن إلّك من قريش ... كإلّ السقب من رأل النعام
(By your life, your kinship with Quraysh is like the kinship of the young camel with the ostrich chick.)
This is explicit that its meaning is kinship. Al-saqb is the khuwār of the she-camel [Translator's note: so in the source, «خوار الناقة»; al-saqb is the young male camel, as the explanation of the verse below makes clear], and al-raʾl is the ostrich chick. The meaning of the verse is: by your life, your kinship with Quraysh is remote or non-existent, like the kinship of the camel's young with the ostrich's young. Al-Zajjāj said: "Al-ill, in my view, according to what the language requires, revolves around the meaning of sharpness. From it is al-alla for the short spear, and from it udhun muʾallala, i.e. a sharpened [pointed] ear." And from it are the words of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd describing the ears of his she-camel as sharp and erect:
مؤللتان تعرف العتق فيهما ... كسامعتي شاة بحومل مفرد
(Two pointed [ears] in which you recognise good breeding, like the two ears of a lone wild bull at Ḥawmal.)

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ اسْتَجارَكَ): the wāw is resumptive; إن is conditional; أحد is nominative by the verb of the condition, implied and explained by the overt one, its implied form being: "and if anyone seeks your protection, seeks your protection". It is not nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because the condition requires a verb, and إن, being among the governors of the verb, does not enter upon anything else. The meaning is: if one of the polytheists with whom you have no covenant comes to you and asks you for safety, grant him safety. من المشركين is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause استجارك is explicative (mufassira).
(فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ كَلامَ اللَّهِ): the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; أجره is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يسمع is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أجره; كلام الله is the direct object.
(ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُ): ثم is a conjunction; أبلغه is an imperative verb and its first object; and مأمنه is the second object.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, i.e. that command, meaning the command to grant protection and to convey him to his place of safety. بأنهم is the khabar (predicate); قوم is the khabar of إنّ; and the clause لا يعلمون is an adjective.
(كَيْفَ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَعِنْدَ رَسُولِهِ): this is a construction in which several parsings are permissible, equal in preponderance: كيف is an interrogative noun in the sense of disapproval and deeming unlikely, a khabar of يكون placed first, and عهد is the noun of يكون placed after; للمشركين is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also possible that the khabar is للمشركين and كيف a ḥāl. It is also possible that His word عند الله is the khabar, with كيف again a ḥāl of العهد. In the two previous ways, عند is an adverb for العهد. عند رسوله is conjoined to عند الله.
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ): what was said about an exception like this has preceded, and that it may be disconnected or connected.
(فَمَا اسْتَقامُوا لَكُمْ فَاسْتَقِيمُوا لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; ما is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (forming a temporal maṣdar), in the position of the accusative as an adverb, i.e. "be upright towards them for the duration of their being upright towards you". It may also be conditional, and in that case there are two ways regarding its position: first, accusative as an adverb of time, the implied construction being "whatever time they are upright towards you, be upright towards them" — Abū al-Baqāʾ compared it to the words of the Exalted «ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها»; second, that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and regarding the khabar there is the well-known discussion about the khabar of a conditional particle. استقاموا is a past verb, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) if it is considered conditional; the fāʾ links in either case; and استقيموا is an imperative verb and its agent. Further, Ibn Mālik allowed the temporal maṣdariyya ما to be at the same time conditional and causing the jussive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: it cannot be negative, because the meaning would be corrupted, since the meaning would become "be upright towards them because they were not upright towards you", which is false. وإن الله: إنّ and its noun, and the clause يحب المتقين is its khabar.
(كَيْفَ؟ وَإِنْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ لا يَرْقُبُوا فِيكُمْ إِلًّا وَلا ذِمَّةً): كيف repeats what preceded, to deem unlikely the polytheists' holding fast to the covenant. The verb is omitted because it is known; so it is a ḥāl, or the khabar of an omitted كان. This omission occurs in their poetry; Kaʿb al-Ghanawī said, lamenting his brother:
وخبر تماني انما الموت بالقرى ... فكيف وهاتا هضبة وقليب
(You two told me that death is only in the villages — so how [did he die], when here are a hill and a well?)
i.e. how did my brother die in it [this place]. Al-qalīb is the well, because its earth was turned over (qulib) from the belly of the earth to its surface. وإن: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إن is conditional; يظهروا is the protasis; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; لا يرقبوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); فيكم is attached to يرقبوا; إلّا is the direct object; and ذمة is conjoined to it.
(يُرْضُونَكُمْ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ وَتَأْبى قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): a resumptive clause introduced to describe their state, the outward contradicting the inward. بأفواههم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يرضونكم; تأبى قلوبهم is conjoined to it, i.e. their speech is embellished and ornamented, and may please its hearer, but it contains no truthfulness whatever, because the rancour lodged in their hearts prevents them from making their honeyed speech come true [Translator's note: the source has «المعمول», apparently a misprint for «المعسول» (honeyed)]. أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ and فاسقون the khabar, i.e. they are dissolute, wicked men who care nothing for disgrace and pay no heed to the evil talk said about them.
(اشْتَرَوْا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا): i.e. they took in exchange for the signs of Allah a small price, namely their being carried along with whims and dragged along with lusts and sins. ثمنا is the object of اشتروا and قليلا an adjective.
(فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ إِنَّهُمْ ساءَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): it is possible for ساء to be in its ordinary sense, being fully conjugated and transitive, so that ما is the agent and the object is omitted, i.e. "what they used to do grieved them", or "their deed [grieved them]" if ما is made maṣdariyya. It is also possible that it functions like biʾsa, so that it is transferred to the pattern faʿula with ḍamma, ceases to be conjugated and becomes [a verb] of blame, the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) being omitted; this has been established before.
(لا يَرْقُبُونَ فِي مُؤْمِنٍ إِلًّا وَلا ذِمَّةً): the i'rab of its like has preceded; He repeated it to further show the ugliness of their state and the abhorrence of their end.
(وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُعْتَدُونَ): this has also preceded; هم may be a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ.

dervis-irab:61-63.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُذُنٌ): with two ḍammas, the well-known organ, the member of hearing; it is feminine and its plural is ādhān. The udhun of a jug is its handle, and its diminutive is udhayna. "So-and-so is an udhun (an ear)" when he listens to what everyone says; it takes a single form for all [numbers]. And it is said:
"He came wearing his two ears", i.e. heedless. More detail about it will come in the sections of Rhetoric and Benefits.
(يُحادِدِ): he opposes. In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: حادّه: he showed enmity to him and angered him.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْهُمُ الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ النَّبِيَّ): resumptive speech, brought to speak about a group of the hypocrites, as will come in the section of Benefits. منهم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الذين a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يؤذون النبي is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَيَقُولُونَ: هُوَ أُذُنٌ قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ): يقولون is conjoined to يؤذون; the clause هو أذن, made of the mubtadaʾ and khabar, is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); قل is an imperative verb; أذن is a khabar whose mubtadaʾ is omitted; خير is muḍāf ilayhi; and لكم is an adjective. (يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ): the clause يؤمن بالله is explicative of his being "an ear of good" for them; ويؤمن للمؤمنين is conjoined to يؤمن بالله. Belief was made transitive to Allah with the bāʾ because it includes the meaning of affirming as true (al-taṣdīq), and to correspond to its opposite, disbelief, in His saying «من كفر بالله»; and it was made transitive to the believers with the lām because it includes the meaning of submitting (al-inqiyād), and in agreement with many verses, such as His saying «وما أنت بمؤمن لنا» and His saying «أفتطمعون أن يؤمنوا لكم». It may also be answered that He made the verb of belief transitive to Allah with the bāʾ and to the believers with the lām because the belief of security from eternity in the Fire — which is the counterpart of disbelief — properly takes the bāʾ, whereas belief in the sense of affirming as true and accepting is made transitive with the lām to distinguish between the two, although properly it would be transitive by itself like al-taṣdīq, for one says صدقتك. ورحمة للذين آمنوا is conjoined to أذن خير; للذين آمنوا is an adjective of رحمة; and منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in آمنوا. (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): الذين is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يؤذون رسول الله is the ṣila; لهم is a fronted khabar and عذاب a delayed mubtadaʾ; أليم is an adjective; and the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين. (يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكُمْ لِيُرْضُوكُمْ): the clause is a second khabar of الذين; لكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحلفون; the lām is causal; يرضوكم is subjunctive by an implied أن; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the causal lām with its genitive noun is also attached to يحلفون. (وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ إِنْ كانُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is circumstantial; الله is the mubtadaʾ and رسوله conjoined to الله; أحق is a fronted khabar and أن with what is within its scope a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the khabar of الله. The pronoun was made singular because the two acts of pleasing are inseparable. The singular pronoun in يرضوه is either to magnify the divine majesty by mentioning it alone, and because there is no difference between pleasing Allah and pleasing His Messenger — pleasing Allah is pleasing His Messenger; or the meaning is "Allah is more worthy that they please Him, and His Messenger likewise", as Sībawayh said and al-Naḥḥās preferred; or because the pronoun is put in the place of a demonstrative, which can point to one or to several; or the pronoun refers to "what was mentioned", which applies to both. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "His Messenger is more worthy that they please him", and [the mention of] Allah is an opening of speech, as you say "what Allah wills and you will". إن is conditional; كانوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); مؤمنين is the khabar of كانوا; and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then Allah and His Messenger are more worthy". It is also permissible that the speech be two clauses, the khabar of one of them omitted because the second indicates it, the implied form being: "Allah is more worthy that they please Him, and His Messenger likewise." (أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّهُ مَنْ يُحادِدِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): the hamza is for the disapproving, rebuking interrogative; لم is a particle of negation, of converting [the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; يعلموا is jussive (majzūm) by لم; أنّ and what is within its scope stands in place of the two objects of يعلموا; أنّ and its noun [the pronoun of the matter]; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يحادد is the protasis; the Name of Majesty is its object; and رسوله is conjoined to the lām. [Translator's note: the source says «عطف على اللام»; presumably the Name of Majesty (لفظ الجلالة) is meant.] (فَأَنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِداً فِيها ذلِكَ الْخِزْيُ الْعَظِيمُ): the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; أنّ is a particle resembling the verb; له is its fronted khabar and نار جهنم its delayed noun; خالدا is a ḥāl from the pronoun made genitive by the lām; فيها is attached to خالدا; the clause made of the conditional noun, its verb and its apodosis is the khabar of the first أنّه; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ, الخزي its khabar and العظيم an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal (metonymic trope):
In His saying «هو أذن» there is majāz mursal, just as "the eye" is used for a man when he is a lookout, because the eye is what is intended of him, so it became as if it were the whole person. It is a case of applying the name of the part to the whole, for hyperbole, and the relation is called "partiality" (al-juzʾiyya). The poet said:
كم بعثنا الجيش جرّا ... را وأرسلنا العيونا
(How often we sent out a huge army and dispatched the "eyes" [scouts].)
In Allah the Exalted's reply to them with His saying «قل أذن خير» there is first a raising of their hopes by conceding, then a signal of despair. Nothing is more effective than replying to them in this way: after apparently agreeing with it, it turns decisively upon their hope and follows it with despair of it. This is called «al-qawl bi-l-mūjib» (conceding the premise while turning its consequence). المُوجِب with kasra of the jīm, because what is meant is the attribute that necessitates the ruling, so it is an active participle of أوجب; and the jīm may take fatḥa if by "saying" is meant the ruling that the attribute necessitated, in which case it is a passive participle. Both meanings are correct. It is of two kinds:
1- That an attribute occurs in the other person's speech as an allusion to something for which a ruling has been asserted, and you assert that attribute in your speech without addressing whether that ruling is established for it or negated from it. For example His saying: «يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجنّ الأعز منها الأذل ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين». الأعز is an attribute that occurred in the speech of the hypocrites as an allusion to their own party, and الأذل as an allusion to the believers. They asserted expulsion for their own party, alluded to as الأعز; so Allah the Exalted, in replying to them, asserted the attribute of might for other than their party, namely Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and did not address whether that ruling — expulsion — is established for those described with might, that is, Allah, His Messenger and the believers, nor its negation from them. Of this kind is what al-Qabaʿtharī said to al-Ḥajjāj when the latter threatened him, saying:
"I will surely mount you on the adham (the black one)", meaning the fetter. Al-Qabaʿtharī saw that al-adham can be an attribute of a fetter and of a horse, so he took his words to mean the horse and said: "The like of the Emir mounts [people] on the black and the grey." Al-Ḥajjāj said: "It — i.e. the adham — is iron (ḥadīd)." Al-Qabaʿtharī said: "That it be ḥadīd (sharp, spirited) is better than that it be dull (balīd)." So he also took ḥadīd contrary to what was meant.
2- Taking a word that occurred in the other person's speech contrary to what he meant, in a sense it can bear, by mentioning what is connected to it. This kind has spread on the tongues of poets and they have used it much in their poems. Ibn Ḥajjāj said:
قال: ثقلت إذ أتيت مرارا ... قلت: ثقلت كاهلي بالأيادي
قال: طوّلت قلت أوليت طولا ... قال: أبرمت قلت: حبل ودادي
(He said: "I have been a burden, coming so many times." I said: "You have burdened my shoulders — with favours." He said: "I have stayed long." I said: "You have bestowed bounty (ṭawl)." He said: "I have wearied you (abramtu)." I said: "[You have firmly twisted] the rope of my affection.")
We cited, near the end of Sūrat al-Anʿām, verses by Ṣafī al-Dīn al-Ḥillī in which he repeated this kind. The noble verse can properly be taken as this kind, by mentioning what the ear is connected to, namely خير.

* Benefits:
History relates that some people of the hypocrites gathered, among them al-Julās ibn Suwayd and Wadīʿa ibn Thābit, and they spoke ill of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and disparaged him. Al-Julās ibn Suwayd — on the pattern of ghurāb, as in al-Qāmūs — said: "We say what we like, then we come to him and deny what we said and swear, and he believes us in what we say, for Muhammad is only an ear." There was with them a youth called ʿĀmir ibn Qays; he came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him. He summoned them and asked them, and they denied it and swore that ʿĀmir was a liar, and ʿĀmir swore that they were liars. ʿĀmir began to pray, saying: "O Allah, confirm the truthful and belie the liar." So Allah revealed this verse.

dervis-irab:113-116.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأواه): of the pattern faʿʿāl from أوّه, like لآلّ from اللؤلؤ; it is one who sighs "ah!" (التأوّه) much. Its meaning is that, out of his excessive love for his father, his compassion, tenderness and forbearance, he used to show kindness to his unbelieving father and seek forgiveness for him despite his harshness towards him. This is what al-Zamakhsharī said. Abū Ḥayyān corrected him, saying: "Likening أوّاه from أوّه to لآلّ from اللؤلؤ is not good, because the root of أوّه is present in the form أوّاه, whereas the root of لؤلؤ is absent from لآلّ owing to the difference in composition, since لآلّ is triliteral and لؤلؤ quadriliteral, and the condition of derivation is agreement in the radical letters." In al-Mukhtār: "The man أوّه, تأويهاً, and تأوّه, تأوّهاً, when he says أوّه (ah!)." Beautiful is the statement of al-Zajjāj, which we quote verbatim: "Abū ʿUbayda said: it is the one who sighs out of compassion and fear, the one who humbly entreats out of certainty and adherence to obedience. All that has been said about al-awwāh is gathered in the statement of Abū ʿUbayda. Its origin is from التأوّه, which is that a sound is heard from the chest as one heaves a deep sigh." It is also said that the word is Abyssinian and that its meaning is "the one who is certain". Ibn al-Naqīb said in his book Khaṣāʾiṣ al-Qur'an: "The Qur'an comprises all the dialects of the Arabs, and a great deal was revealed in it in the languages of others: the Byzantines, the Persians and the Abyssinians." The non-Arabic words which the ancients noticed will come up with us when we speak about the language of the Qur'an.

* I'rab:
(ما كانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ): (ما) is negative; (كان) is a deficient past verb; (للنبي) is the fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (الذين) is conjoined to (النبي); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (أن) with what falls under it is the postponed noun of (كان); (يستغفروا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by (أن); and (للمشركين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يستغفروا). (وَلَوْ كانُوا أُولِي قُرْبى مِنْ بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and (لو) is connective (waṣliyya); (كانوا) is (كان) and its noun; (أولي) is its khabar and (قربى) a muḍāf ilayhi. (من بعد) is attached to the verbal meaning contained in the negation, i.e. seeking forgiveness is negated from after…; (ما) is maṣdar-forming, and it with what falls under it is in a genitive construct with (بعد), i.e. "from after the becoming clear". (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تبين); (أنهم): (أنّ) with what falls under it is the fāʿil (agent) of (تبين), and (أصحاب الجحيم) is the khabar of (أنّ). (وَما كانَ اسْتِغْفارُ إِبْراهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَها إِيَّاهُ): the clause is resumptive, brought to establish what preceded, support it with evidence and indications, and ward off any impression of contradiction that might arise from the outward appearance. (كان) and its noun; (إبراهيم) is a muḍāf ilayhi; (لأبيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استغفار); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (عن موعدة) is the khabar of (كان). So the exception is emptied (mufarragh) from the most general of causes, i.e. Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father did not arise except from a promise he had made him, that is, for its sake. (فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُ إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ لَأَوَّاهٌ حَلِيمٌ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking (rābiṭa); (له) is attached to (تبين); (أنّ) with what falls under it is the agent of (تبين); the clause (تبرأ منه) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (لما). (إنّ) and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), (أواه) is the first khabar of (إنّ) and (حليم) its second khabar. (وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْماً بَعْدَ إِذْ هَداهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (كان) and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); (يضل) is accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of denial, and it with what it enters on is the khabar of (كان) — this has come many times before. (قوما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بعد) is an adverb attached to (يضل), and it is muḍāf, the adverb (إذ) being muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause (هداهم) is what the adverb is construct to. It was stated in Āl ʿImrān that there are two views on it: one, that (إذ) is in the sense of (أن); the second, that it is an adverb in the sense of "time", i.e. "after that He guided them" or "after the time of their guidance". (حَتَّى يُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ ما يَتَّقُونَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): (حتى) is a particle of limit and genitive; (يبين) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied (أن) after (حتى); (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يبين); (ما) is a direct object and the clause (يتقون) is the ṣila. (إنّ), its noun and its khabar, and (بكل شيء) is attached to (عليم). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ): (إنّ) and its noun; (له) is a fronted khabar and (ملك السموات والأرض) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يحيي) is a second khabar of (إنّ), the first khabar being the clause (له ملك السموات); (يميت) is conjoined to (يحيي). (وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (من دون الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (من) is redundant (zāʾida); (ولي) is a postponed mubtadaʾ in position; and (ولا نصير) is conjoined to (من ولي).

dervis-irab:64-66.t:
* I'rab:
(يَحْذَرُ الْمُنافِقُونَ أَنْ تُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُورَةٌ تُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ): a resumptive clause, brought to explain the envy and enmity towards the believers that burns in the breasts of the hypocrites: they fear that [a sūra] be sent down upon them [i.e. the believers] informing them of what the souls of the hypocrites harbour. Do not say that the pronouns are disjointed, for how easy it is to refer each pronoun to its owners. يحذر المنافقون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); أن تنزل عليهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) made accusative by يحذر, for it is transitive by itself — contrary to al-Mubarrad, who claimed that حذر is not transitive and said that it is one of the states of the soul, like فزع. The reply to him is from several angles:
a- That is neither necessary nor consistent; many states of the soul are transitive, like خاف and خشي.
b- His saying: «ويحذركم الله نفسه»: had it not originally been transitive to one object, it would not have acquired a second object through doubling [of the middle radical].
c- The dictionaries of the language agree that it is transitive by itself and by a particle.
عليهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنزل; سورة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause تنبئهم is an adjective of سورة; بما is in the place of the second object of تنبئهم; and في قلوبهم is attached to an omitted [verb that forms the] ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (قُلِ اسْتَهْزِؤُا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْرِجٌ ما تَحْذَرُونَ): استهزئوا is an imperative verb by which threat is meant; إنّ with its noun and khabar; ما, a relative noun, is the object of مخرج, since it is an active participle; and the clause تحذرون is the ṣila of ما. (وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّما كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ): the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause نخوض is the khabar of كنا. Say: أبالله وآياته ورسوله كنتم, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). [Translator's note: the preceding two sentences appear to be a corruption in the source text — fragments displaced from elsewhere; they are translated as written. The intended analysis presumably is: the wāw is resumptive, the lām prepares for an oath, إن is conditional and سألتهم is the protasis in the position of the jussive.] ليقولن: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; يقولن is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the presence of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the doubled nūn is for emphasis; the clause إنما كنا نخوض ونلعب is the object of the saying, and the clause نخوض is the khabar of كنا. (قُلْ: أَبِاللَّهِ وَآياتِهِ وَرَسُولِهِ كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the hamza is for the disapproving, rebuking interrogative; بالله is attached to تستهزءون; آياته and رسوله are conjoined to الله; كنتم تستهزئون: كان and its noun, and the verbal clause is its khabar. (لا تَعْتَذِرُوا قَدْ كَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمانِكُمْ): لا is prohibitive; تعتذروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); كفرتم is a verb and its fāʿil; بعد is attached to كفرتم; and إيمانكم is muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنْ نَعْفُ عَنْ طائِفَةٍ مِنْكُمْ نُعَذِّبْ طائِفَةً بِأَنَّهُمْ كانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ): إن is conditional; نعف is the protasis; عن طائفة is attached to نعف; منكم is an adjective; نعذب is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); طائفة is the mafʿūl bihi; بأنهم is attached to نعذب, and the bāʾ is causal; أنّ and its noun, and the clause كانوا مجرمين is its khabar; and [that clause is] كان with its noun and khabar.

dervis-irab:67-69.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الخلاق): with fatḥa on the khāʾ, the share; it is what has been created for a person, i.e. allotted to him, of good.

* I'rab:
(الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالْمُنافِقاتُ بَعْضُهُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ): المنافقون is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and المنافقات is conjoined to it; بعضهم is a mubtadaʾ and من بعض a khabar (predicate), i.e. they resemble one another like the parts of one thing. (يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمُنْكَرِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ): the clause is a second khabar of المنافقون, the first being the nominal clause; وينهون عن المعروف is conjoined to the previous clause, and ويقبضون أيديهم is also conjoined; its meaning will come in the section of Rhetoric. (نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَنَسِيَهُمْ إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ): نسوا الله is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فنسيهم is conjoined to نسوا — the discussion of this majāz mursal will come. إنّ and its noun; هم is a second mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); الفاسقون is the khabar of «هم» or the khabar of إنّ; and [in the first case] the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ. (وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْمُنافِقاتِ وَالْكُفَّارَ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ): وعد الله المنافقين is a verb, fāʿil and object; المنافقات is conjoined, and likewise الكفار; and نار جهنم is the second mafʿūl bihi. وعد is used for both good and evil. (خالِدِينَ فِيها هِيَ حَسْبُهُمْ): خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first object; هي is the mubtadaʾ and حسبهم the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. (وَلَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; لعنهم الله is a verb, mafʿūl bihi and fāʿil; لهم is a fronted khabar and عذاب a delayed mubtadaʾ; and مقيم is an adjective. (كَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ كانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْكُمْ قُوَّةً): the kāf is a noun meaning "like", the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "you are like those who…". It is also permissible that the kāf be a preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun being the khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ. من قبلكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; كانوا أشد is كان with its noun and khabar; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشد; and قوة is a tamyīz (specification). (وَأَكْثَرَ أَمْوالًا وَأَوْلاداً): conjoined to أشد منكم قوة.
(فَاسْتَمْتَعُوا بِخَلاقِهِمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; استمتعوا is a verb and its fāʿil; and بخلاقهم is attached to استمتعوا. (فَاسْتَمْتَعُوا بِخَلاقِهِمْ): conjoined to what preceded. [Translator's note: the source repeats this lemma; the second instance presumably refers to فَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِخَلاقِكُمْ.]
(كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ بِخَلاقِهِمْ): the position of the kāf is the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); الذين is the fāʿil; من قبلكم is the ṣila of الذين; and بخلاقهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استمتع. (وَخُضْتُمْ كَالَّذِي خاضُوا): the kāf and what it governs are in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq. (أُولئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ): أولئك is the mubtadaʾ and the clause حبطت is the khabar; أعمالهم is the fāʿil; and في الدنيا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حبطت. (وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and هم is a pronoun of separation or a second mubtadaʾ.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are several arts of eloquence:
1- Kināya (allusion) in His saying (وَيَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ): an allusion to stinginess. The origin of this allusion is that the giver extends his hand and spreads it in giving, so of one who withholds and is miserly it was said: "he has closed his hand."
2- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in His saying «نسوا الله فنسيهم», because forgetting is not applicable here: with respect to them, it would lift the obligation from them, and with respect to Him the Exalted it is impossible. Therefore the speech must be taken as majāz mursal with the relation of concomitance (al-lāzimiyya): what is meant is the concomitant of forgetting, which is abandoning, i.e. they neglected the remembrance of Allah, so He left them out of His mercy and bounty. Or one may say there is the art of mushākala (verbal correspondence) in it, because real forgetting cannot properly be ascribed to Allah, Glorified is He; it was ascribed to Him here only by way of mushākala, i.e. they abandoned what He commanded them, so He left them out of His mercy and bounty.
3- Repetition (al-takrīr) in the reiteration of استمتعوا: He likened their state to the state of the earlier ones, and in the repetition there is emphasis and exaggeration in blaming those addressed, showing their state to be ugly and their affair to be disgraceful.
4- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in خضتم: He likened falsehood to water, omitted the thing likened and kept what it is likened to — water — by way of dependent explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya).
5- Al-tankīt (pointing to a subtle reason) in His saying: «المنافقون والمنافقات» to the end of the verse, then His saying after that «والمؤمنون والمؤمنات» to the end of the verse. Someone may ask: what is the subtle point that required describing the hypocrite men and women with intense cohesion, and not the believing men and women, such that it is not permissible to exchange the two predicates, making the cohesion among the believers and something else among the hypocrites? The answer is:
Since the hypocrite men and women were all Jews, and they were of the Children of Israel, their connection with one another was a connection of lineage, or what we call race and kind. And since the believers came from various peoples and diverse nations, their connection was a connection of a bond (sabab), namely what Islam placed between them of loving one another for Allah's sake, loyalty in Him and fighting in His way. From here it was not permissible to exchange the two predicates by making the connection of lineage for the believers and the connection of bond for the hypocrites.

dervis-irab:11-12.t:
* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ تابُوا وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكاةَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; تابوا is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); أقاموا الصلاة and آتوا الزكاة — the two clauses are conjoined to تابوا.
(فَإِخْوانُكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ): the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; إخوانكم is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then they are your brothers"; في الدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(وَنُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is parenthetical and the clause is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa), as though it were said: whoever reflects on their detailed exposition is the one who knows their reality. لقوم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نفصل, and the clause يعلمون is a naʿt (adjective).
(وَإِنْ نَكَثُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ وَطَعَنُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; من بعد عهدهم is a ḥāl; طعنوا في دينكم is also conjoined, i.e. they disparaged it and found fault with it; and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to طعنوا.
(فَقاتِلُوا أَئِمَّةَ الْكُفْرِ إِنَّهُمْ لا أَيْمانَ لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَنْتَهُونَ): the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; قاتلوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); أئمة الكفر is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); انهم: إنّ and its noun; لا is the lā of generic negation, أيمان is its noun and لهم its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of إنهم; and لعلّ with its noun, the clause ينتهون being its khabar.

dervis-irab:13-15.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلا تُقاتِلُونَ قَوْماً نَكَثُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ): ألا is a particle of incitement (taḥḍīḍ) — the particles of incitement will come in the section of Benefits; تقاتلون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); قوما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause نكثوا أيمانهم is a naʿt (adjective) of قوما. It is also possible that the hamza is interrogative and لا negative, the hamza entering upon it to affirm the negation of fighting, and, from another aspect, to urge it.
(وَهَمُّوا بِإِخْراجِ الرَّسُولِ): conjoined to نكثوا; بإخراج is attached to (mutaʿalliq) هموا. It has preceded that they intended one of three things: killing him, imprisoning him or expelling him.
(وَهُمْ بَدَؤُكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; هم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause بدءوكم the khabar (predicate); أول مرة is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), attached to بدءوكم — and the one who starts is the greater wrongdoer.
(أَتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ فَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَخْشَوْهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the hamza is interrogative and its meaning is prohibition, i.e. do not fear them. فالله: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); الله is a mubtadaʾ and أحق the khabar; أن تخشوه, the interpreted maṣdar, is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of الله, i.e. fear of Allah is more deserving. إن is conditional; كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); مؤمنين is the khabar of كنتم; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the fāʾ faṣīḥa.
(قاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ): قاتلوهم is an imperative verb, its agent and its object; يعذبهم is the answer to the command (jawāb al-ṭalab), made jussive by it. It is one of five answers that will follow, namely:
(وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنْصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُؤْمِنِينَ وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ): all of them are conjoined to يعذبهم.
(وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive and يتوب is a resumptive clause; He did not join it to the preceding answers because Allah's turning to whom He wills is not a consequence of fighting the disbelievers.

* Benefits:
1- The particles of incitement (taḥḍīḍ) are: lawlā, law mā, hallā and alā. Allah the Exalted said: «لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب», and He said: «لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة». ʿAntara said:
هلا سألت الخيل يا ابنة مالك ... إن كنت جاهلة بما لم تعلمي
(Why did you not ask the horsemen, O daughter of Mālik, if you were ignorant of what you did not know?)
Taḥḍīḍ is urging toward something; one says ḥaḍaḍtuhu ʿalā fiʿlihi when I urged him to do it. When the imperfect follows them, they express incitement; when the past follows them, they express reproach and rebuke for what the addressee has left undone. They behave like the particles of condition in requiring verbs, so neither a mubtadaʾ nor any other noun occurs after them. If a noun does occur after them, it is intended to come later, as in your saying hallā Zaydan ḍarabta, meaning hallā ḍarabta Zaydan; or [it is] on the supposition of an omitted verb, as in your saying to one who is showing generosity: hallā Zaydan, i.e. hallā akramta Zaydan. The poet — Jarīr — said:
تعدون عقر النيب أفضل مجدكم ... بني ضوطرى لولا الكمي المقنعا
(You count the slaughtering of old she-camels as your highest glory, O sons of Ḍawṭarā — why not [face] the helmeted warrior?)
So he implied a verb that made الكمي المقنعا accusative. The meaning is: these sons of Ḍawṭarā — al-ḍawṭarā being the bulky man who is of no use — go about with feeding and hospitality and make generosity their greatest glory. What makes al-kamiyy accusative is the verb intended after lawlā, its implied form being "you meet", "you duel with" or the like.
2- The imperfect verb is made jussive when it occurs as the answer to a command, a prohibition, a question, a wish, an offer or an incitement, and that is by an implied in, as in your saying: akrimnī ukrimka (honour me and I will honour you), lā tafʿal yakun khayran laka (do not do it, it will be better for you), alā taʾtīnī uḥaddithka (will you not come to me, I will talk to you), ayna baytuka azurka (where is your house, I will visit you), alā māʾa ashrabhu (is there no water I may drink), and laytahu ʿindanā yuḥaddithnā (would that he were with us, he would talk to us). [Translator's note: in the source the examples alā taʾtīnī uḥaddithka, ashrabhu and yuḥaddithnā are written without the jussive marking; they are given here as written.] Al-Khalīl said: all these first [clauses] contain the meaning of «إن» (if), and that is why the answer became jussive. The grammarians said that it is not permitted to say lā tadnu min al-asad yaʾkulka (do not go near the lion, it will eat you), because the implied construction would be "if you do not go near the lion, it will eat you", which is absurd, since keeping one's distance cannot be a cause of being eaten. The grammarians have a long discussion here, to be consulted in the extended works.
3- The poets expanded at length on the meaning of the words of the Exalted «ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم», because the Arabs are a people formed by nature for ardour and pride, so their desire to attain vengeance and kill their enemies suits their natures. Abū Tammām gazed toward the heights of this meaning and said:
إن الأسود أسود الغاب همتها ... يوم الكريهة في المسلوب لا السلب
(The lions — the lions of the thicket — on the day of hateful battle, care for the one despoiled, not the spoils.)

dervis-irab:16-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلِيجَةً): of the pattern faʿīla from walaja, like dakhīla from dakhala. Anything you have put into something of which it is not a part is a walīja. It is used for the singular and others with one form, and it may be pluralised as walāʾij. A man's walīja is the one who is intimate with him in his inner affairs. In al-Miṣbāḥ: walaja al-shayʾ fī ghayrihi yaliju — of the pattern waʿada — wulūjan: it entered; and awlajtuhu īlājan: I made it enter. Al-walīja is the intimate circle (al-biṭāna).

* I'rab:
(أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تُتْرَكُوا): أم is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) — its ruling will follow; حسبتم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); أن and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of حسبتم. The meaning is: you will not be left as you are until the sincere among you become manifest.
(وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; لمّا is a particle causing the jussive, conveying expectation; يعلم is jussive (majzūm) by it; الله is the agent; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause جاهدوا is the ṣila (relative clause); and منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلا رَسُولِهِ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةً): the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and the jussive; يتخذوا is an imperfect, jussive by لم; من دون الله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتخذوا; ولا رسوله is conjoined to الله; and وليجة is the direct object.
(وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): its i'rab has preceded many times.
(ما كانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَنْ يَعْمُرُوا مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ): ما is negative; كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; للمشركين is the khabar (predicate) of كان placed first; and أن with what falls within its scope is its noun placed after.
(شاهِدِينَ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ بِالْكُفْرِ): شاهدين is a ḥāl of the wāw in يعمروا; على أنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شاهدين, and likewise His word بالكفر. That is: it is neither sound nor right, in custom or in nature, that they combine the upkeep of the mosques with disbelief, the two being contradictory.
(أُولئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ وَفِي النَّارِ هُمْ خالِدُونَ): أولئك is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause حبطت أعمالهم the khabar; في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدون; هم is a mubtadaʾ and خالدون the khabar.

* Benefits:
«أم» occurs in four ways:
1- Connected (muttaṣila), meaning that what precedes it and what follows it cannot do without one another. It is called muʿādila (counterbalancing) because it counterbalances the hamza in conveying equivalence (taswiya), if the hamza before it is the hamza of equivalence, as in the words of the Exalted in Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn: «سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم»; or [if the hamza] seeks specification, as in: a-fī al-dāri Zaydun am ʿAmr (is Zayd in the house or ʿAmr?).
2- Disconnected (munqaṭiʿa): it is preceded by a pure statement, as in the words of the Exalted «تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين أم يقولون افتراه», or preceded by a hamza conveying a meaning other than questioning, such as disapproval, as in «ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها», where it is equivalent to negation. And the meaning of disconnected «أم», which is never separated from digression (iḍrāb). [Translator's note: this sentence is incomplete in the source.]
3- That it occurs as redundant (zāʾida); Abū Zayd mentioned this and said, regarding the words of the Exalted «أفلا تبصرون أم أنا خير», that the implied construction is: afalā tubṣirūna anā bi-khayr. [Translator's note: so in the source, «أنا بخير»; the usual citation is «أنا خير».]
4- That it serves as the definite article in the dialect of Ḥimyar and Ṭayyiʾ.
Poetic examples of am:
1- وما أدري وسوف أخال أدري ... أقوم آل حصن أم نساء
(I do not know — and I think I shall come to know — whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)
Here it occurs connected, preceded by the interrogative hamza, which is not for equivalence.
2- ولست أبالي بعد فقدي مالكا ... أموتي ناء أم هو الآن واقع
(After losing Mālik I do not care whether my death is far off or happening now.)
Here it occurs connected, after the hamza of equivalence.
3- أحاد أم سداس في أحاد ... لييلتنا المنوطة بالتناد
(Is it one, or six in one — this little night of ours that is tied to the Day of Calling?)
Am here may be either connected or disconnected.

dervis-irab:117-118.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ تابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ وَالْمُهاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصارِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ فِي ساعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ): the meaning of Allah's turning in repentance to the Prophet will come in the section on Benefits. The clause is resumptive, brought to explain repentance and that there is no believer who is not in need of it. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (تاب الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (على النبي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تاب); (المهاجرين) and (الأنصار) are conjoined to (النبي); (الذين) is a naʿt (adjective); the clause (اتبعوه) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and (في ساعة العسرة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (اتبعوه). Mention of "the hour of hardship" will come in the section on Benefits.
(مِنْ بَعْدِ ما كادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِنْهُمْ): (من بعد) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), to show the severity [of the situation] and its reaching the utmost limit. The noun of (كاد) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause (يزيغ) is the khabar (predicate); (قلوب) is the agent; (فريق) is a muḍāf ilayhi; and (منهم) is a naʿt. (ثُمَّ تابَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّهُ بِهِمْ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): (ثم) is a conjunction of delay (tarākhī), and (تاب) is conjoined to the first (تاب). The benefit of the repetition is to draw attention to His having turned to them because of what they endured in the hour of hardship. (إنه): (إنّ) and its noun; (بهم) is attached to (رءوف); and (رءوف رحيم) are two predicates of (إنّ).
(وَعَلَى الثَّلاثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا): (وعلى الثلاثة) is conjoined to what preceded. Those meant by them are Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ and Hilāl ibn Umayya. (الذين) is a naʿt and the clause (خلفوا) is the ṣila; (خلفوا) is passive and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. [left behind] from the expedition.
(حَتَّى إِذا ضاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَرْضُ بِما رَحُبَتْ وَضاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ): (حتى) is a particle of limit; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, and the clause (ضاقت) is in a genitive construct with it; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ضاقت); (الأرض) is the agent. (بما رحبت) means "with its spaciousness": the bāʾ is a genitive particle of accompaniment and (ما) is maṣdar-forming. The meaning of the bāʾ here is accompaniment; its sign is that «مع» can properly take its place, or that a ḥāl can dispense with it and what accompanies it. Here «مع» is valid in it, i.e. "with its spaciousness". As for an example of a ḥāl dispensing with it and what accompanies it, it is the saying of Allah the Exalted «وقد دخلوا بالكفر», i.e. as unbelievers. In any case, it with what accompanies it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. in the state of its being spacious. (وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم) is conjoined to what preceded; it is a figure for perplexity in their affair, as though they could find no place in which to settle. (وَظَنُّوا أَنْ لا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ): (وظنوا) is conjoined to (ضاقت), and ẓann here is in the sense of certainty. (أن) is lightened from the heavy (أنّ), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (ملجأ) is its noun; (من الله) is its khabar; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ملجأ). (ثُمَّ تابَ عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَتُوبُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ): (ثم) is a conjunction; (تاب) is a past verb; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تاب). In (ليتوبوا), the lām is said to be causal, i.e. He enabled them to repent so that they would attain it and bring it about; thus a difference [between the two repentances] is obtained and the causal sense is valid. I see no objection to its being the lām of outcome (ʿāqiba) or becoming (ṣayrūra), i.e. their outcome was repentance. (إنّ) and its noun; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and (التواب الرحيم) are two predicates of (إنّ) or of (هو).

* Benefits:
1- These two verses contain many benefits. Before embarking on them we will speak about a difficulty that arises in them, namely the answer of (إذا) and the conjunction «ثم تاب عليهم». The scholars answered this with two answers. The first is that (إذا) is redundant (zāʾida), so it needs no answer and the meaning is sound. The second is that (ثم) is redundant, so that the clause (تاب عليهم) is the answer. The difficulty cannot be resolved except by supposing one of them redundant. Among those who held that (ثم) is redundant is Zakariyyā in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī, «أو غيره فاختاروا زيادة إذا» (or others, and they chose the redundancy of إذا) [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is probably "as for others, they chose the redundancy of إذا"].
And this is what Abū Ḥayyān said: "These clauses came under the wing of (إذا) in the utmost beauty and order. First He mentioned the earth's becoming narrow for them, which is a metonymy for their feeling of desolation and people's shunning conversation with them. Secondly, (وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم), which is a metonymy for the successive coming of worry and grief upon their hearts, until there was nothing of relief and ease in them. So He first mentioned the narrowness of the place and then secondly the narrowness of one's state in it, because the place may be narrow while the soul is at ease — «سم الخياط مع الأحباب ميدان» (the eye of a needle, with loved ones, is an open field). Then thirdly, when they despaired of creatures, they entrusted their affairs to Allah, devoted themselves to Him alone, and knew that none rescues from hardship or relieves it except He the Exalted: «ثم إذا مسكم الضر فإليه تجأرون». If (إذا) is conditional, its answer is omitted, its implied form being 'He turned to them', and His saying (ثم تاب عليهم) is parallel to His saying (ثم تاب عليهم) after His saying «لقد تاب الله على النبي…» to the end of the verse. The claim that (ثم) is redundant and that the answer of (إذا) is what comes after (ثم) is very far-fetched; the redundancy of (ثم) is not established from the tongue of the Arabs. And there are those who claimed that (إذا) after (حتى) may be stripped of condition and remain for mere time, so that it needs no answer but is rather a limit for the verb before it, namely His saying (خلفوا), i.e. they were left behind until this time. (ثم تاب عليهم ليتوبوا): then He returned to them with acceptance and mercy once again, so that they would remain steadfast in their repentance and turn [to Him], or so that they would also repent in the future if a sin escaped them, knowing that Allah turns in forgiveness to whoever repents, even if he relapses a hundred times a day."
The meaning of repentance:
The scholars likewise differed about the meaning of Allah's turning in repentance to the Prophet, and we shall set out the most important views held by the leading commentators and linguists.
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he placed it in the same thread as the saying of Allah the Exalted «ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر» and His saying «واستغفر لذنبك», and he said: it is an urging of the believers to repentance, and [a statement] that there is no believer who is not in need of repentance and seeking forgiveness, even the Prophet and the Emigrants and Helpers who were with him. This is the view we have followed, considering it logical and consistent.
As for al-Jalāl and the commentators on his tafsīr, they went to the meaning of perpetuity in the repentance, i.e. He made His turning to them perpetual. The commentators said in their remarks on what al-Jalāl held: "This is an answer to what is said, that the Prophet is protected from sin and that the Emigrants and Helpers did not commit any sin in this affair; so he made clear that what is meant by repentance in the case of all of them is its perpetuation, not its origin." This view is evidently confused.
As for al-Khāzin, he held a view that we almost preferred even over the first view, namely his saying: "The meaning of His turning to the Prophet is His not taking him to task for his giving the believers permission to stay behind from him in the expedition of Tabūk, and it is like His saying «عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم». So it is a matter of leaving what is better, not a sin that requires punishment."
There is also a view no less sound than the foregoing, which the scholars of meanings expressed by saying: it is speech for the sake of blessing (tabarruk), like the saying of Allah the Exalted: «فأن لله خمسه». The meaning of this is that mentioning the Prophet by [Allah's] turning to him is an honour for the Emigrants and Helpers in joining their repentance to the repentance of the Prophet ﷺ, just as the name of the Messenger was joined to the name of Allah in His saying «فأن لله خمسه وللرسول».

The hour of hardship (sāʿat al-ʿusra):
What is meant is its time, not the astronomical hour; "hour" is used in the sense of time in general, just as "morning", "evening" and "day" are used, as in the saying of Zufar ibn al-Ḥārith al-Kilābī:
وكنا حسبنا كل بيضاء شحمة ... عشية قارعنا جذام وحميرا
(We had thought every white thing a lump of fat, on the evening we clashed with Judhām and Ḥimyar;)
فلما قرعنا النبع بالنبع بعضه ... ببعض أبت عيدانه أن تكسرا
(but when we struck nabʿ-wood against nabʿ-wood, one against the other, its staves refused to break.)
What is meant is time in general, not the evening in its literal sense. And as in the saying of Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī:
إذا جاء يوما وارثي يبتغي الغنى ... يجد جمع كف غير ملأى ولا صفر
(When one day my heir comes seeking wealth, he will find a fistful neither full nor empty:)
يجد فرسا مثل العنان وصارما ... حساما إذا ما هزّ لم يرض بالهبر
(he will find a horse like the rein, and a keen cutting sword which, when brandished, is not content with slicing flesh,)
وأسمر خطّيا كأن كعوبه ... نوى القسب قد أربى ذراعا على العشر
(and a brown Khaṭṭī spear whose joints are like the stones of dry dates, exceeding ten cubits by one.)
What is meant by "day" is time in general, and this is the predominant usage of the Arabs. It is to be noted that he used the jussive after «إذا», likening it to the particles that put two verbs in the jussive; the grammarians have stated that this occurs, as in the poet's saying:
استغن ما أغناك ربك بالغنى ... وإذا تصبك خصاصة فتجمل
(Be content with wealth as long as your Lord enriches you, and if poverty strikes you, bear it with dignity.)
The hour of hardship which occurred in the expedition of Tabūk had events; we shall content ourselves with a report about it from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Tabūk in intense summer heat. We halted at a place where severe thirst afflicted us, until we thought our necks would be cut off, and until a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze out its stomach contents and drink it, and put what remained on his liver; and until a man would go off searching for water and not return before he thought his neck would be cut off. Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has accustomed you to good in supplication, so pray to Allah.' He said: 'Would you like that?' Al-Ṣiddīq said: 'Yes.' So he ﷺ raised his hands, and they did not come back down until the sky 'said' (qālat) and grew dark, then poured; they filled the vessels they had with them. Then we went to look at it, and we did not find that it had gone beyond the camp." The meaning of "the sky said" is: it inclined and fell.

dervis-irab:70-72.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمُؤْتَفِكاتِ): the cities of the people of Lot; it is also said: the towns of the people of Lot, Hūd and Ṣāliḥ. Their being "overturned" (iʾtifāk) is the turning of their conditions from good to evil; or [they are] the overturned ones whose top Allah made their bottom. One says أفكه when he overturned it, and its pattern is ضرب; and one says:
أفكته فائتفك — it is its reflexive (muṭāwiʿ), i.e. I overturned it and it was overturned. The root indicates change and turning.
(عَدْنٍ): residence; here it is a proper name for Paradise. Its origin is from عدن القوم بالبلد: the people resided in the land, and their residence (ʿadn, ʿudūn) there was long. "So-and-so is in the maʿdin (mine, source) of goodness and generosity", i.e. he is one of the centres and sources of goodness. "He wears ʿadaniyyāt", i.e. noble garments; its origin is the relation to ʿAdan, with two fatḥas. Among their sayings: "Girls of the towns passed by, wearing ʿAdanī wraps." It became frequent, until a man of noble character was called ʿadanī, just as an amazing thing in any field is called ʿabqarī. Ibn Jābir al-Muḥāribī said:
سرت ما سرت من ليلها ثم عرّست ... إلى عدنيّ ذي غناء وذي فضل
إلى ابن حصان لم تخضرم جدودها ... كريم النثا والخيم والعقل والأصل
(She journeyed as much of the night as she journeyed, then halted at a noble ʿadanī man of wealth and merit — the son of a chaste woman whose ancestors were of unmixed stock, noble in repute, nature, mind and origin.)

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ يَأْتِهِمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); لم is a particle of negation, of converting [the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; يأتهم is jussive (majzūm) by لم; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); نبأ is the fāʿil (agent); الذين is muḍāf ilayhi; and من قبلهم is the ṣila (relative clause). (قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَقَوْمِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَأَصْحابِ مَدْيَنَ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتِ): قوم is a badal (substitute) for الذين, a badal of part from whole. His saying وعاد to the end of the conjoined items are all conjoined to قوم نوح, except that the last, المؤتفكات, involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the towns of the people of Lot. The Noble Qur'an restricted itself to these six groups only because their traces remain and their lands are in Syria, Yemen and Iraq, all of which are near the land of the Arabs in their peninsula; they used to pass by them and seek out news of their inhabitants. (أَتَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ): the clause is resumptive, to explain their news and stories, and رسلهم is the fāʿil.
(فَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلكِنْ كانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction and ما negating; كان الله: كان and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); يظلمهم is subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām of denial; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar, i.e. "intending to wrong them". ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction and لكن is lightened and inoperative; كان and its noun; أنفسهم is a fronted object of يظلمون; and the clause يظلمون is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا. The mafʿūl bihi was put first out of concern for it, while observing the verse-ending (fāṣila). (وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتُ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ): المؤمنون is the mubtadaʾ (subject); بعضهم a second mubtadaʾ and أولياء the khabar; and the clause is the khabar of المؤمنون. Its contrast has passed, with a reference to the art of tankīt (pointing to a subtle reason) between the two clauses in the predicate.
(يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): the clause is a khabar, and its i'rab has preceded.
(وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ): conjoined to what preceded. (وَيُطِيعُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): also conjoined. (أُولئِكَ سَيَرْحَمُهُمُ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): أولئك is the mubtadaʾ and the clause سيرحمهم الله the khabar; and إنّ with its noun and its two khabars.
(وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): وعد الله المؤمنين is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; جنات is the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause تجري is an adjective; الأنهار is the fāʿil; and من تحتها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجري.
(خالِدِينَ فِيها وَمَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ): خالدين فيها is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المؤمنين; مساكن is conjoined to جنات; طيبة is an adjective; and في جنات عدن is a second adjective.
(وَرِضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ): a mubtadaʾ; it was permissible to begin with it [though indefinite] because it is qualified by His saying من الله; and أكبر is its khabar. He did not include it in the series of things promised because it is realized within every promised thing, and because it is the utmost to which the hopes of souls can rise. (ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, هو a second mubtadaʾ and الفوز the khabar of هو, and the clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; العظيم is an adjective.

dervis-irab:73-74.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ جاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ): جاهد is an imperative verb; الكفار is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and المنافقين is conjoined. (وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ): اغلظ is conjoined to جاهد, i.e. let no leniency take hold of you towards them; fight them with the sword and set right their falsehood with logic and proof.
(وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ): Abū al-Baqāʾ said in his i'rab: "If it is asked how the wāw is good here when the fāʾ is more suited to this place, there are three answers:
The first is that the wāw is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl), the implied form being: do that in the state of their deserving Hell, and that state is the state of their disbelief and hypocrisy. The second is that the wāw was brought to signal that an omitted verb is intended, its implied form being: and know that Hell is their abode. The third is that the speech is construed according to the meaning, and the meaning is that there has been combined for them the punishment of this world through jihad and harshness, and the punishment of the Hereafter through making Hell their abode." There is no need for all this, because the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the final outcome of their affair after explaining its immediate part. وبئس المصير: the wāw is a conjunction; بئس المصير is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted because it is known, i.e. "their destination". (يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ ما قالُوا): a resumptive clause, brought to explain the reprehensible deeds that issued from them which required the command to strive against them and be harsh with them. بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحلفون; ما is negating; قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; and the clause ما قالوا is the answer to the oath.
(وَلَقَدْ قالُوا كَلِمَةَ الْكُفْرِ وَكَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِسْلامِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; كلمة الكفر is the object of قالوا. It is said that it is the word of al-Julās ibn Suwayd mentioned above, and it has been said that it is the word of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl when he said: «لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل». كفروا is conjoined to قالوا, and بعد is an adverb attached to كفروا. (وَهَمُّوا بِما لَمْ يَنالُوا): conjoined to what preceded; بما is attached to هموا, and the clause لم ينالوا is the ṣila (relative clause). The story of this intent — namely, the attempt on the life of the Messenger of Allah — will come in the section of Benefits. (وَما نَقَمُوا إِلَّا أَنْ أَغْناهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction and ما negating; نقموا is a verb and its fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction; أن and what is within its scope is the object of نقموا; أغناهم الله is a verb, mafʿūl bihi and fāʿil; رسوله is conjoined to الله; and من فضله is attached to أغناهم. (فَإِنْ يَتُوبُوا يَكُ خَيْراً لَهُمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يتوبوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); يك is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive by the sukūn on the nūn, which was dropped for lightness — its rule has preceded among the special features of كان. The noun of يك is latent, i.e. "the repenting"; خيرا is the khabar (predicate); and لهم is attached to «خيرا». (وَإِنْ يَتَوَلَّوْا يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ عَذاباً أَلِيماً فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يتولوا is the protasis; يعذبهم is the apodosis; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi and الله the fāʿil; عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and أليما an adjective; في الدنيا is attached to يعذبهم; and الآخرة is conjoined to الدنيا. (وَما لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ): the wāw is a conjunction and ما negating; لهم is a fronted khabar; في الأرض is a ḥāl (circumstantial); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ولي is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) by position; and ولا نصير is conjoined to ولي.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse, «وما نقموا إلا أن أغناهم الله ورسوله من فضله», there is affirming praise by what resembles blame (taʾkīd al-madḥ bimā yushbih al-dhamm); the discussion of this art has preceded in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida. It is as if He said: he has no attribute to be faulted and disliked, except that, as a consequence of his coming to them and his emigration to them, Allah enriched them after want, poverty and severe need — and this is not an attribute of blame; so then he has no attribute to be blamed at all.

* Benefits:
The attempt on the life of the Prophet ﷺ:
History relates that they resolved among themselves to assassinate the Prophet ﷺ on the night of the ʿAqaba (the mountain pass) on his return from Tabūk; they were some ten-odd men. Their opinion agreed on pushing him off his mount so that he would fall into the valley and die. When he reached the ʿAqaba, his herald called out by his command: "The Messenger of Allah wants to take the ʿAqaba, so let no one but him take it; and you, O company of the army, take the floor of the valley, for it is easier and wider for you." So the people took the floor of the valley, and the Prophet ﷺ took the ʿAqaba. That was on a dark night. The hypocrites came, veiled their faces and took the ʿAqaba. The Prophet had ordered ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir to take hold of his she-camel's halter and lead her, and ordered Ḥudhayfa to drive her from behind. While the Prophet was travelling in the ʿAqaba, the hypocrites came upon him; his she-camel bolted until some of his baggage fell, and he shouted at them. They turned and fled, knowing that he had learned of their plot, and they descended from the ʿAqaba hurrying to the floor of the valley and mixed with the people. Ḥudhayfa came back striking the she-camel, and the Prophet said to him: "Did you recognize any of them?" He said: "No, they were veiled and the night was dark." He said: "Did you know what they intended?" He said: "No." The Prophet said: "They plotted and wanted to travel with me in the ʿAqaba and crowd me off it, and Allah has informed me of them and of their plot." When he returned, he gathered them and told them of what they had plotted, and they swore by Allah that they had not said or intended [it]. There are other narrations which do not depart from this meaning; they may be consulted in the extensive works.

dervis-irab:119-121.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَخْمَصَةٌ): hunger. Its verb has three forms: خمص, with fatḥa, kasra or ḍamma on the mīm. Its maṣdar is خمص and مخمصة. One says he is خميص البطن (lean of belly) and she is خميصة البطن; he is خمصان and she is خمصانة; they (masc.) are خماص and they (fem.) are خمائص. Among the figurative uses is زمن خميص, i.e. a time of famine; the poet said:
كلوا في بعض بطنكم تعفّوا ... فإن زمانكم زمن خميص
(Eat to fill part of your belly and you will remain chaste, for your time is a time of hunger.)
Anything you dislike approaching, you have تخامصت عنه (shrunk away from it). Al-Shammākh said:
تخامص عن برد الوشاح إذا مشت ... تخامص جافي الخيل في الأمعز الوجي
