(She shrinks from the coolness of the sash when she walks, as a horse with sore hooves shrinks on stony ground.)
تخامص الليل: its darkness grew thin at the time before dawn. Al-Farazdaq said:
فما زلت حتى صعدتني حبالها ... إليها وليلي قد تخامص آخره
(I kept on until her ropes lifted me up to her, and the end of my night had grown thin.)
(يَنالُونَ): in the lexicons: نال خيراً ينال نيلاً means he obtained [good]. Its original form is نَيِل يَنيَل, of the pattern of فهم [Translator's note: so in the source], and its imperative is نَل; when you speak of yourself you put kasra on the nūn and say نِلتُ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "نال من عدوه, of the pattern of تعب, نيلاً: he attained his aim against him; and from it is said: نال من امرأته ما أراد (he obtained from his wife what he wanted)."
(وادِياً): the valley (الوادي) is every opening between mountains and hills that serves as a channel for a torrent. It is originally an active participle (fāʿil) from ودى, when it flowed; from it comes الوَدْي. The Arabs commonly use it in the sense of land; they say: "Do not pray in another's valley", and that is what is meant here. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ودى الشيء when it flowed; from it is the derivation of الوادي, which is every opening between mountains or hills that serves as a channel for a torrent; the plural is أودية." In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: "ودى يدي وَدْياً ودِيَةً: the killer paid the slain man's guardian his blood-money (دية); ودى الأمر: he brought it near; ودى الشيء: it flowed, and from it is the derivation of الوادي, because water flows (يدي) in it, i.e. runs and streams. The plural is أودية, أوادية, أوداء and أوداه." So what has become common on the tongues of writers, pluralising it as وديان, is a plain error.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given many times. (اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ): (اتقوا الله) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كونوا) is conjoined to (اتقوا); the wāw is the noun of (كان); and (مع الصادقين) is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of (كونوا). They said it came in the sense of (من), i.e. "of the truthful". What led them to this is that it was read in an irregular (shādhdh) reading «وكونوا من الصادقين». There is no call for this strained interpretation, because keeping (مع) in its own meaning is preferable; the meaning is: be with the Emigrants and the Helpers, agree with them and fall into line with them. (ما كانَ لِأَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفُوا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ): (ما) is negative; (كان) is a deficient past verb; (لأهل المدينة) is the fronted khabar of (كان); (من) is conjoined to (أهل); (حولهم) is an adverb attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (من الأعراب) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (أن) with what falls under it is the postponed noun of (كان); and (عن رسول الله) is attached to (يتخلفوا). (وَلا يَرْغَبُوا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction. (يرغبوا) may be accusative by conjunction, with (لا) being negative, or jussive with (لا) being prohibitive. (بأنفسهم) is attached to (يرغبوا), the bāʾ being for transitivity; the expression رغبت عنه means "I turned away from it", and the meaning is: let them not make their selves turn away from his self. (عن نفسه) is a ḥāl. That is: it is incumbent on them to accompany him in every state, in hardship and adversity, to endure terrors with him and bear toil and hateful things, and to make their selves meet the hardships that his self meets. For it is as though he did not shield himself or hold himself aloof when he came close to hardships and endured terrors; how fitting it is, then, for them to follow his example and trace his footsteps. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ لا يُصِيبُهُمْ ظَمَأٌ وَلا نَصَبٌ وَلا مَخْمَصَةٌ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (بأنهم) is the khabar; (لا يصيبهم ظمأ) is a nominative imperfect verb, a direct object and an agent; (ولا نصب ولا مخمصة) are conjoined to (ظمأ); (في سبيل الله) is a ḥāl from the hāʾ, or a naʿt (adjective) of (مخمصة). (وَلا يَطَؤُنَ مَوْطِئاً يَغِيظُ الْكُفَّارَ): (ولا يطئون) is conjoined to (لا يصيبهم). (موطئا) is either a noun of place, in which case it is parsed as a direct object, i.e. they tread a place; or an adverb [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense of the parsing as maṣdar suggests "or a maṣdar"], in which case it is parsed as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause (يغيظ الكفار) is a naʿt of (موطئا).
(وَلا يَنالُونَ مِنْ عَدُوٍّ نَيْلًا): conjoined to what preceded; (من عدو) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ينالون). (إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُمْ بِهِ عَمَلٌ صالِحٌ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and the clause (كتب) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; so the exception is emptied (mufarragh) from the most general of states. (كتب) is a passive past verb; (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كتب), and likewise (به); (عمل) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and (صالح) a naʿt. (إنّ) and its noun, and the clause (لا يضيع أجر المحسنين) is the khabar of (إنّ). (وَلا يُنْفِقُونَ نَفَقَةً صَغِيرَةً وَلا كَبِيرَةً): conjoined to (لا ينالون); (نفقة) is a direct object, i.e. even a single date or more. (وَلا يَقْطَعُونَ وادِياً): conjoined to what preceded. (إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُمْ):
the clause is one of exception from the most general of states, as stated before, and the deputy agent is omitted because it was mentioned before, i.e. "a righteous deed". (لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the lām is causal; (يجزي) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām; the hāʾ is a first direct object; (الله) is the agent; (أحسن) is a second direct object, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq in meaning, i.e. He recompenses them with the best recompense. (ما) is a relative noun in a genitive construct with (أحسن); (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يعملون) is its khabar.

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّما يَعْمُرُ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَأَقامَ الصَّلاةَ وَآتَى الزَّكاةَ): إنما is [inna as] a restraining particle with the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); يعمر مساجد الله is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed before [the agent]. What is meant by their upkeep is repairing what needs repair in them, cleaning them, lighting them, honouring them and furnishing them with fine, acquired furnishings. من is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of يعمر; the clause آمن is the ṣila (relative clause), and what follows it is conjoined to it; its i'rab is evident.
(وَلَمْ يَخْشَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and the jussive; يخش is jussive (majzūm) by لم, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من آمن; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and the name of Majesty is the direct object.
(فَعَسى أُولئِكَ أَنْ يَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُهْتَدِينَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); عسى is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope; أولئك is its noun and أن يكونوا its khabar (predicate); من المهتدين is the khabar of يكونوا. That is: the state of these described with the four qualities is to be hoped for, and the outcome is known to Allah.
(أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقايَةَ الْحاجِّ وَعِمارَةَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ كَمَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): a resumptive clause introduced to address the polytheists by way of iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person in His words «ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله». The hamza is for a disapproving, rebuking question; جعلتم سقاية الحاج is a verb, its agent and its first object; عمارة المسجد الحرام is conjoined to سقاية الحاج; the kāf is a noun meaning "like", the second object; من is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause آمن is the ṣila. A muḍāf must be omitted either from the first or from the second, so that the two things made [equal] correspond. The implied form is: "Have you made the people of the watering of the pilgrims and the upkeep of the Sacred Mosque like one who believed", or "Have you made the watering and the upkeep like the faith of one who believed", or "like the deed of one who believed".
(وَجاهَدَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): conjoined to آمن.
(لا يَسْتَوُونَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): a resumption emphasising the nullification of equality, i.e. the two parties are not equal. الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause لا يهدي القوم الظالمين the khabar; He brought it as the reason for negating equality in meaning.
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهاجَرُوا وَجاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech introduced to establish the state of those described by these three qualities mentioned. الذين is a mubtadaʾ, آمنوا is the ṣila, and what follows it is conjoined to it; أعظم is the khabar; درجة is a tamyīz (specification); and the adverb عند الله is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفائِزُونَ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; its like has preceded.
(يُبَشِّرُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَرِضْوانٍ وَجَنَّاتٍ): يبشرهم ربهم is an imperfect verb, its object and its agent; برحمة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يبشرهم; منه is a naʿt (adjective); and برضوان and جنات are conjoined to رحمة.
(لَهُمْ فِيها نَعِيمٌ مُقِيمٌ): لهم is a khabar placed first; فيها is a ḥāl; نعيم is a mubtadaʾ placed after; and مقيم is an adjective.
(خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً): خالدين is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara); فيها is attached to خالدين; and أبدا is an adverb, also attached to خالدين.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ): إنّ and its noun; the adverb is a khabar placed first and أجر a mubtadaʾ placed after; عظيم is an adjective; and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are figures of rhetoric, which we set out below.

First — Crafted simile (al-tashbīh al-ṣināʿī) and its purposes:
1- The simile through which the speech takes the form of disapproval, in the words of the Exalted «أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة البيت الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر». This is disapproval of one who made the sanctity of jihad like the sanctity of one who believed in Allah and the Last Day; and in it is the fullest indication of the greatness of the believer's state through faith, and that no creature not of his description is made equal to him. This is one of the purposes of crafted simile. [Translator's note: the source quotes the verse as «وعمارة البيت الحرام», whereas the Qur'anic text is «وعمارة المسجد الحرام»; and «حرمة الجهاد» ("the sanctity of jihad") here appears to be a slip for the sanctity of the watering and upkeep. Translated as written.]
2- Bringing the more obscure out to the more evident by means of the simile, and to what the senses perceive, as in the words of the Exalted «والذين كفروا أعمالهم كسراب بقيعة يحسبه الظمآن ماء حتى إذا جاءه لم يجده شيئا»; more will be said about this verse later.
3- Among them is bringing what custom has not experienced out to what custom has experienced, as in the words of the Exalted «وإذ نتقنا الجبل فوقهم كأنه ظلة».
4- Among them is bringing what is not known intuitively out to what is known intuitively, as in the words of the Exalted «وجنة عرضها السماوات والأرض».
5- Among them is bringing what has no strength in the quality out to what has strength in the quality, as in the words of the Exalted «وله الجوار المنشآت في البحر كالأعلام».
6- Among them is showing that the thing likened is possible. That is when something strange is attributed to it whose strangeness is removed only by mentioning something resembling it, as in the words of al-Buḥturī:
دان إلى أيد العفاة وشاسع ... عن كل ندّ في الندى وضريب
كالبدر أفرط في العلو وضوءه ... للعصبة السّارين جد قريب
(Near to the hands of those who seek favour, and far removed from every rival and equal in generosity — like the full moon, exceedingly high, while its light is very near to the band of night travellers.)
In the first verse al-Buḥturī described the one he praised as near to the needy and far in rank, with a great gap between him and his peers in generosity. But when al-Buḥturī sensed that he had described the one he praised with two opposite qualities, nearness and farness, he wanted to show you that this is possible and that there is no contradiction in the matter; so he likened the one he praised to the full moon, which is in the sky, yet its light is very near to those travelling by night.
7- Among them is showing its state. That is when the quality of the thing likened is unknown before the simile, and the simile supplies the description, as in the words of al-Nābigha:
كأنك شمس والملوك كواكب ... إذا طلعت لم يبد منهنّ كوكب
(You are as though a sun and the kings are stars: when it rises, not one star of them appears.)
Al-Nābigha likened the one he praised to the sun and likened the other kings to stars, because the might of the one praised diminishes the might of every king, as the sun hides the stars; he wants to show the state of the one praised and the state of the other kings.
8- Among them is establishing its state. That is when the quality of the thing likened is known before the simile in a general way, and the simile shows the degree of this quality, as in the words of the Exalted «والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه». The verse speaks about those who worship idols: when they call upon their gods, they do not answer them, and this calling brings them no benefit. Allah the Exalted wished to establish this state and fix it in minds, so He likened these idolaters to one who stretches out his palms to water to drink, and the water obviously does not reach his mouth, because it escapes between his fingers as long as his palms are stretched out. This purpose comes when the thing likened is something abstract, because the soul is not as certain about abstract things as about sensible ones, so it is in constant need of persuasion.
9- Embellishing the thing likened, as in the words of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Anbārī about a crucified man:
مددت يديك نحوهم احتفاء ... كمدهما إليهم بالهبات
(You stretched out your hands toward them in welcome, as you used to stretch them toward them with gifts.)
This verse is from an ode that gained wide fame in Arabic literature for no reason except that it made beautiful what people agree is ugly and repugnant, namely crucifixion. He likens the stretching of the crucified man's arms on the wood, with people around him, to his stretching out his arms with gifts to those who asked, in the days of his life. The purpose of this simile is embellishment; this type occurs mostly in praise, elegy, boasting and the description of what souls incline to.
10- Making the thing likened ugly, as in the words of one of the Bedouins censuring his wife:
وتفتح- لا كانت- فما لو رأيته ... توهمته بابا من النار يفتح
(And she opens — may she not exist! — a mouth which, had you seen it, you would have imagined a gate of the Fire being opened.)
He prays against his wife that she be deprived of existence, saying "may she not exist", and likens her mouth when she opens it to one of the gates of Hell. The purpose of this simile is to make ugly; it is mostly used in satire and the description of what souls shun. From it are the words of al-Mutanabbī:
وإذا أشار محدثا فكأنه ... قرد يقهقه أو عجوز تلطم
(When he gestures while speaking, he is like a cackling ape or an old woman slapping her face.)
Further, more of the discussion of simile will come later.

Second — Al-laff wa-l-nashr (folding and unfolding):
In the words of the Exalted «يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم», after He had described the believers with three qualities — faith, emigration, and striving with self and wealth — He began with mercy, corresponding to faith, since it depends on it; second, good pleasure, which is the utmost of beneficence, corresponding to striving, in which lives and wealth are expended; then third, gardens, corresponding to emigration and leaving homelands — an indication that since they preferred to leave them, He gave them in exchange a great and everlasting abode, namely the gardens. This is an original figure, which they defined as: mentioning several things in detail or in summary, then mentioning what belongs to each of them without specifying, trusting that the hearer will distinguish what belongs to each one and return it to what it belongs to. The detailed type is of two kinds:
a- That the unfolding follows the order of the folding: the first of the several things in the unfolding belongs to the first in the folding, the second to the second, and so on to the last. One of them said:
ومقرطق يغني النديم بوجهه ... عن كأسه الملأى وعن إبريقه
فعل المدام ولونها ومذاقها ... في مقلتيه ووجنتيه وريقه
(A youth in a tunic whose face makes his drinking companion need neither his full cup nor his ewer: the effect of wine, its colour and its taste are in his eyes, his cheeks and his saliva.)
— and like the verse under discussion.
b- That the unfolding does not follow the order of the folding, as in the words of Abū Firās:
وشادن قال لي لما رأى سقمي ... وضعف جسمي والدمع الذي انسجما
أخذت دمعك من خدي وجسمك من ... خصري وسقمك من طرفي الذي سقما
(A young gazelle said to me when it saw my sickness, the weakness of my body and the tears that flowed: You took your tears from my cheek, your body from my waist, and your sickness from my languid eye.)
The summary type is that you fold two things together in mention, then follow them with speech containing what pertains to one and what pertains to the other without specifying, as in the words of the Exalted «وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا أو نصارى». He mentioned the two parties in summary rather than in detail, then mentioned what belongs to each of them. The several things mentioned in summary are the two parties or their sayings; the original is: The Jews said, none shall enter Paradise except one who is a Jew; and the Christians said, none shall enter Paradise except one who is a Christian. He folded them together because there is no ambiguity and in confidence that the hearer will return to each party its saying.
Third: the indefiniteness of what is announced as good tidings, namely His words «يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات», because it lies beyond the description of any describer and the definition of any definer.

dervis-irab:122-126.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَلُونَكُمْ): they are near to you. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "الوَلْي, like فَلْس: nearness. In the verb there are two forms; the more common is وَلِيَه يَلِيه, with two kasras, and the second is of the pattern of وعد, which is rarely used. 'I sat in what is next to him (مما يليه)', i.e. near him." It is as though the verse came according to the second form. Its original form is يَلْيُون, on the pattern of يَعِدُون [Translator's note: so in the source]; the ḍamma of the yāʾ was transferred to the lām after its own vowel was removed, then the yāʾ was dropped because of its meeting, while vowelless, with the wāw.

* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً): the wāw is a conjunction, to keep the speech coherent; for when they were rebuked by the saying of Allah the Exalted «ما كان لأهل المدينة…» etc., and the Prophet sent out a raiding party, they all went out together, so «وما كان المؤمنون…» etc. was revealed. (ما) is negative; (كان) is a deficient past verb and (المؤمنون) is its noun. In (لينفروا), the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), i.e. for emphasising the negation, and (ينفروا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of denial; the lām with what it enters on is the khabar (predicate) of (كان). (كافة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَلَوْلا نَفَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِنْهُمْ طائِفَةٌ لِيَتَفَقَّهُوا فِي الدِّينِ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), i.e. "why not"; (نفر) is a past verb; (من كل فرقة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نفر); (منهم) is a ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of (طائفة). In (ليتفقهوا), the lām is causal and (يتفقهوا) is accusative by an implied (أن); (في الدين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتفقهوا). So the meaning is one of request, as though He said: let one party go out and another remain. (وَلِيُنْذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ): (ولينذروا) is conjoined to (ليتفقهوا); the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and (قومهم) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). In (إذا رجعوا), the clause (رجعوا) is in a genitive construct with it; (إليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (رجعوا). (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (يحذرون) is its khabar.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُمْ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ): (قاتلوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (الذين) is a direct object; the clause (يلونكم) is a naʿt [Translator's note: so in the source; it is the ṣila of the relative noun]; and (من الكفار) is a ḥāl.
(وَلْيَجِدُوا فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; (يجدوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the lām of command, and the wāw is the agent; (فيكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يجدوا); (غلظة) is a direct object. (اعلموا) is conjoined to the preceding command; (أنّ) with what falls under it stands in place of the two objects of (اعلموا); (أنّ) and its noun, and (مع المتقين) is an adverb attached to its omitted khabar. (وَإِذا ما أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida); the clause (أنزلت) is in a genitive construct with it; and (سورة) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً): the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); (منهم) is a fronted khabar and (من) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); it is a relative noun, or a complete indefinite noun qualified by the clause (يقول), i.e. "a party who says" — and perhaps that is preferable; [on the first view] the clause (يقول) is the ṣila (relative clause). (أيكم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (زادته) is the khabar; the hāʾ is a direct object, (هذه) is the agent, and (إيمانا) is a second direct object. (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَزادَتْهُمْ إِيماناً وَهُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ): the fāʾ is of ramification (tafrīʿiyya); (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; the fāʾ is linking; (زادتهم) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object, and the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (الذين); (إيمانا) is a second direct object or a tamyīz (specification).
(وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزادَتْهُمْ رِجْساً إِلَى رِجْسِهِمْ): (وأما) is conjoined to the first (أما); (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; (في قلوبهم) is a fronted khabar and (مرض) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the ṣila. In (فزادتهم), the fāʾ is linking and the clause (زادتهم) is the khabar of (الذين); (رجسا) is a second direct object; and (إلى رجسهم) is a naʿt, i.e. joined to their filth. (وَماتُوا وَهُمْ كافِرُونَ): conjoined to (زادتهم); the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause (كافرون) [i.e. (هم كافرون)], made of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is a ḥāl. (أَوَلا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُمْ يُفْتَنُونَ فِي كُلِّ عامٍ مَرَّةً أَوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke (istifhām inkārī tawbīkhī), and the wāw is a conjunction joining to something implied; (يرون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (أنّ) with what falls under it stands in place of the two objects of the verb of mental perception; the clause (يفتنون) is the khabar of (أنّ); (في كل عام) is attached to (يفتنون); (مرة) is an adverb attached to (يفتنون); (أو) is a conjunction and (مرتين) is conjoined to (مرة). (ثُمَّ لا يَتُوبُونَ وَلا هُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; the clause (لا يتوبون) is conjoined to (يفتنون); the wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يذكرون) is the khabar.

* Benefits:
1- The obligation of fighting:
The commentators and the jurists said: fighting becomes an individual obligation on one of two groups: either those upon whom an enemy has descended while they have strength against him, and then on those near them until they suffice. And if Allah made it obligatory upon this community to fight and to dislodge the enemy from his abodes and drive him out of his land and his dwelling, then its obligation — when the enemy has descended upon the abode of Islam, occupied its holy places, violated their sanctity and wrought corruption in them — is all the more fitting.
2- A maṣdar with all three vowels:
الغلظة (harshness) is originally used of «الإجرام» [Translator's note: so in the source; probably الأجرام, physical bodies], then it was borrowed for severity, endurance and toughness in fighting. Among the wonders of this maṣdar is that it was read with all three vowels: الغِلظة with kasra, which is the dialect of Asad; الغَلظة with fatḥa, which is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; and الغُلظة with ḍamma, which is the dialect of Tamīm. One says غلظ يغلظ, of the patterns of تعب and ظرف, and the maṣdar is غِلَظ with kasra on the ghayn, غِلْظة, and غلظة with the three vowels as stated above, and غِلاظة with kasra — the opposite of being thin, delicate or soft.

dervis-irab:75-80.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ عاهَدَ اللَّهَ): a resumption brought to relate the story of Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥāṭib, who is an embodied example of hypocrisy; his story will come in the section of Benefits. منهم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and من, a relative noun, is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause عاهد الله is the ṣila (relative clause). (لَئِنْ آتانا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ وَلَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); إن is conditional; آتانا is a past verb and نا the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); لنصدقن is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted. The lām in لنصدقن occurs in the answer to the oath, and there is nothing to prevent combining the oath and the lām that prepares for it. لنكونن is conjoined to لنصدقن; من الصالحين is the khabar of نكونن, and the noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we". (فَلَمَّا آتاهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ بَخِلُوا بِهِ وَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is a temporal adverb (ḥīniyya) or a linking particle; آتاهم is a verb, a latent fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi; من فضله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) آتاهم; the clause بخلوا به has no grammatical position; تولوا is conjoined to بخلوا; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is the mubtadaʾ and معرضون the khabar. (فَأَعْقَبَهُمْ نِفاقاً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ إِلى يَوْمِ يَلْقَوْنَهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أعقبهم is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a first mafʿūl bihi; نفاقا is the second mafʿūl bihi; في قلوبهم is an adjective of نفاقا, i.e. firmly established and rooted in their hearts; إلى يوم is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. extending; and the clause يلقونه is the one to which the adverb is annexed. (بِما أَخْلَفُوا اللَّهَ ما وَعَدُوهُ وَبِما كانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ): the bāʾ is a causal preposition and ما is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. because of their breaking the promise to Allah; الله is the object of أخلفوا; ما is maṣdariyya, and it with what is within its scope is the object of أخلفوا; وبما كانوا يكذبون is conjoined to what preceded, parallel to it in i'rab. (أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْواهُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ): the hamza is for the disapproving interrogative; يعلموا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; أنّ and what is within its scope stands in place of the two objects of يعلموا; سرهم is the object of يعلم and نجواهم is conjoined to سرهم; وأن الله علام الغيوب is أنّ with its noun and khabar, conjoined to the first أنّ. (الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي الصَّدَقاتِ): الذين is in the position of the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are", or it is a mubtadaʾ; يلمزون is the ṣila; المطوعين is the mafʿūl bihi; من المؤمنين is a ḥāl; and في الصدقات is attached to يلمزون, i.e. they find fault with them in it.
(وَالَّذِينَ لا يَجِدُونَ إِلَّا جُهْدَهُمْ): conjoined to الذين يلمزون [i.e. to المطوعين]; إلا is a particle of restriction, and جهدهم is the object of يجدون. [Translator's note: the source says "conjoined to الذين يلمزون"; in meaning it is conjoined to المطوعين.] (فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُمْ): conjoined to يلمزون; منهم is attached to يسخرون. (سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ):
the clause سخر الله منهم is the khabar of الذين; لهم is a fronted khabar, عذاب a delayed mubtadaʾ and أليم an adjective. (اسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ أَوْ لا تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ): a command by which a statement is meant, as if it were said: Allah will not forgive them, whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. أو is for "takhbīr" and conjunction [Translator's note: the source has «للتخبير», probably a misprint for «للتخيير» (for choice)]; لا is prohibitive; تستغفر is jussive by لا; and لهم is attached to the verb. Further discussion of it will come in the section of Rhetoric. (إِنْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ): إن is conditional; تستغفر is the protasis; لهم is attached to تستغفر; سبعين is an adverb — contrary to Abū al-Baqāʾ, who parsed it as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); but the occurrence of مرة after it, which is an adverb, confirms that it must be an adverb — and مرة is a tamyīz (specification). Seventy is used proverbially in their speech for a large number. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said:
لأصبحن العاصي وابن العاصي ... سبعين ألفا عاقدي النواصي
(I will surely come upon al-ʿĀṣī and the son of al-ʿĀṣī at dawn with seventy thousand, their forelocks tied.)
The fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; لن is a particle of the subjunctive; يغفر is subjunctive by لن; الله is the fāʿil; and لهم is attached to يغفر. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ): ذلك is the mubtadaʾ and بأنهم the khabar; أنّ and what is within its scope is a maṣdar made genitive by the bāʾ; the clause كفروا is the khabar of أنّ; بالله is attached to كفروا and رسوله is conjoined to الله; الله is the mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يهدي the khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi and الفاسقين is a naʿt (adjective).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم» the command and the prohibition depart from their original meaning to another meaning, namely equivalence (al-taswiya), as in the saying of Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
أسيئي بنا أو أحسني لا ملومة ... لدينا ولا مقلية إن تقلت
(Treat us badly or treat us well — you will not be blamed by us, nor hated if you turn to hatred.)
It is as if he were saying to her: test your place with me and the strength of my love for you; treat me badly and well, and see whether my state with you differs, whether you are doing ill or doing good. Likewise the meaning of the verse: ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, and see whether they will be forgiven in either state — asking forgiveness or leaving it. It is among the most eloquent of speech.

* Benefits:
The story of Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥāṭib:
1- This is a remarkable story in which hypocrisy is embodied; we summarize it because of its length, and the reader may refer to it in the extensive works. History relates that Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥāṭib asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for him that Allah grant him wealth, and that he would give from it every one who had a right his right. He prayed for him, and his means were widened. Thaʿlaba was sound in Islam at the beginning of his affair and kept constantly to the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, until he was nicknamed "the dove of the mosque". When abundant provision came to him in full, he stopped attending the Friday prayer and the congregation and withheld the zakāt — to the end of that story, unique in history.
2- An important rule: a request may be put in the place of a statement, to express contentment with what happens, as though it were something requested. On this is the saying of Kuthayyir:
أسيئي بنا أو أحسني لا ملومة ... لدينا ولا مقلية إن تقلّت
i.e. you are not blamed by us, nor hated. He used the wording of command, then conjoined to it with the word أو; the command conveys the doing of ill, and the meaning is that of a statement, i.e. we are content with whatever you do; we do not blame you whether you did ill or good, and we do not hate you if you hate. In it there is a signal of showing greater contentment with everything ʿAzza chose regarding him, and a signal that Kuthayyir's response does not vary with the variation of what ʿAzza chose. On this pattern is the noble verse mentioned above: Allah's not forgiving them does not vary with the variation of the Messenger's (upon him be peace) asking forgiveness, whether it occurs or does not occur. For what the context requires here is a statement, not a command, because it cannot properly be taken here as a real command, which would be requesting a thing together with its opposite.
The use of seven, seventy, seven hundred and the like for a large number has become widespread, because seven comprises all the categories of number, as if it were number in its entirety. The explanation of this is that seven is the first complete number, since it brings together all of number: for numbers are even and odd, and of the evens and odds there is a first and a second — two is the first even and four the second even; three is the first odd and five the second odd. If you combine the first even with the second odd, or the first odd with the second even, it is seven; and this property is not found in any number before seven. It is also said that the Arabs exaggerate number with seven because the balance is at half of the decade, which is five: if one is added to it, it is for the least exaggeration, and if two are added to it, it is for the utmost exaggeration, and there is no addition beyond that. For this reason they called the lion sabʿ, because its strength has been multiplied seven times. Then seventy is the limit of limits, because the limit of the units is the tens. So the meaning of the verse is that He the Exalted will not forgive them, even if you were always to ask forgiveness with all the numbers.

dervis-irab:81-82.t:
* I'rab:
(فَرِحَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلافَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ): فرح المخلفون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent). They are those whom laziness left behind and kept from contributing to their sacred duties, after they had asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to stay behind. بمقعدهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) فرح. خلاف رسول الله, i.e. behind him, is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they stayed behind to oppose him, or opposing him. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar by an implied verb indicated by His saying مقعدهم, since it is in the sense of تخلفوا, i.e. "they stayed behind (تخلفوا) — staying behind the Messenger of Allah". It may also be accusative as an adverb, i.e. after the Messenger of Allah; Abū ʿUbayda, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash held this view, and Abū al-Baqāʾ confined himself to it. (وَكَرِهُوا أَنْ يُجاهِدُوا بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): conjoined to فرح المخلفون; أن and what is within its scope is the object of كرهوا, i.e. they disliked going out to jihad. (وَقالُوا لا تَنْفِرُوا فِي الْحَرِّ قُلْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ حَرًّا لَوْ كانُوا يَفْقَهُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تنفروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; في الحر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تنفروا; قل is an imperative verb; نار جهنم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and أشد the khabar (predicate); حرا is a tamyīz (specification); لو is conditional; كان and its noun, and the clause يفقهون is its khabar; and the apodosis of لو is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have stayed behind".
(فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا وَلْيَبْكُوا كَثِيراً): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition); the lām is the lām of command; يضحكوا is jussive by it; قليلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or an adverb of time, meaning "a little laughter" or "a little time"; and وليبكوا كثيرا is conjoined. (جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): جزاء is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; بما is attached to جزاء, or to an omitted adjective of it; ما is maṣdariyya or a relative noun; كان and its noun, and the clause يكسبون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between laughing and weeping and between "little" and "much"; so it is a muqābala (correspondence of contrasts).
2- Expressing a statement in the form of a command (inshāʾ), because its meaning is "they will laugh little and weep much"; but the statement was put in the form of a command to indicate that it is an inevitable matter that must happen.

dervis-irab:127-129.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عَزِيزٌ): grievous, hard.
(العنت): hardship and meeting with what is hateful.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا ما أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ نَظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ): conjoined to what preceded; the clause (نظر بعضهم) is the answer of (إذا) and has no grammatical position; (إلى بعض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نظر), i.e. they winked at each other with their eyes out of their rage. (هَلْ يَراكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ): the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "saying", and the clause of saying is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (يراكم) is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من) is redundant (zāʾida); and (أحد) is the fāʿil (agent) in position. (ثُمَّ انْصَرَفُوا صَرَفَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَفْقَهُونَ): (ثم انصرفوا) is conjoined to (نظر بعضهم). The clause (صرف الله قلوبهم) may properly be informative, as a ḥāl, or it may properly be performative, as an imprecation, in which case it has no grammatical position. (بأنهم) is attached to (صرف), the bāʾ being causal; (أنّ) and its noun, and the clause (لا يفقهون) is its khabar (predicate). (لَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ): the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (جاءكم رسول) is a verb, a direct object and an agent; (من أنفسكم) is a naʿt (adjective), i.e. of your kind and of your lineage, an Arab like you.
(عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ ما عَنِتُّمْ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): (عزيز) is a second naʿt of (رسول). Among the grammarians there are those who forbid placing a non-explicit description before an explicit one; this can be answered by [saying] that (من أنفسكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جاءكم). (عليه) is attached to (عزيز); (ما) is maṣdar-forming or relative, and on both suppositions it with what it enters on — i.e. it with its ṣila — is the agent of (عزيز), which is a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha). It is also possible that (عزيز) is a fronted khabar and that (ما عنتم), interpreted as a maṣdar, is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being a naʿt of (رسول). (حريص) is a third naʿt, or a second; (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (حريص); (بالمؤمنين) is attached to (رءوف); and (رءوف رحيم) are a fourth and fifth naʿt, or a third and fourth, of (رسول).
(فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُلْ حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (تولوا) is a verb and its agent, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is linking; (حسبي الله) is a fronted khabar and a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): its i'rab has been given in full before, so renew your acquaintance with it; the clause is a ḥāl. (عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ): (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (توكلت); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (رب العرش) is the khabar, and (العظيم) is a naʿt of (العرش).

dervis-irab:23-24.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العشيرة): one's closest kin. It was said: they are a man's kin by whom he becomes numerous, whether they reach ten (ʿashara) or more. And it was said: it is a group joined by lineage, contract or affection, like the "knot of ten" (ʿaqd al-ʿashara).

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has preceded.
(لا تَتَّخِذُوا آباءَكُمْ وَإِخْوانَكُمْ أَوْلِياءَ): لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); آباءكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إخوانكم is conjoined to it; and أولياء is a second object. The clause is resumptive, introduced to answer what they said after Allah the Exalted commanded disavowal of the polytheists: they said, "How can a man cut off his father, his brother and his son?" So Allah answered them with this, i.e. a man's cutting off his kin in religion is obligatory, and the believer does not take the disbeliever as an ally even if he is his father, brother or son.
(إِنِ اسْتَحَبُّوا الْكُفْرَ عَلَى الْإِيمانِ): إن is conditional; استحبوا is a verb and its agent, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); الكفر is the object of استحبوا; and على الإيمان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) استحبوا, which contains the sense of "chose".
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional [noun], a mubtadaʾ (subject); يتولهم is the protasis, in which the wording [of من] is observed, so it is singular; منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ pronoun; الظالمون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك or of هم, with the clause being the khabar of أولئك; and here the meaning of من is observed.
(قُلْ إِنْ كانَ آباؤُكُمْ وَأَبْناؤُكُمْ وَإِخْوانُكُمْ وَأَزْواجُكُمْ وَعَشِيرَتُكُمْ وَأَمْوالٌ اقْتَرَفْتُمُوها وَتِجارَةٌ تَخْشَوْنَ كَسادَها وَمَساكِنُ تَرْضَوْنَها أَحَبَّ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَجِهادٍ فِي سَبِيلِهِ): إن is conditional; كان and its noun, and what follows it is conjoined to it; أحب is the khabar of كان; إليكم is a ḥāl; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أحب; and رسوله and جهاد في سبيله are conjoined to الله, i.e. than emigrating to them [Allah and His Messenger].
(فَتَرَبَّصُوا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; تربصوا is an imperative verb and its agent; حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يأتي is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; الله is the agent; بأمره is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يأتي; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين the khabar. The meaning of the command here is threat, and its object is omitted, i.e. await a punishment, immediate or deferred. This verse is among the most severe verses in threat, thunder, lightning and deterrence for everyone whose soul tempts him to prefer the perishing over the lasting, and to have regard for kin and clan while abandoning regard for Allah.

dervis-irab:25-27.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المواطن): plural of mawṭin; al-mawāṭin are like al-waṭan. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Al-waṭan is a person's place and abode; the plural is awṭān, like sabab and asbāb. Al-mawṭin is like al-waṭan, and its plural is mawāṭin, like masjid and masājid. Al-mawṭin is also a scene among the scenes of war." Al-Zamakhsharī's phrasing: "The mawāṭin of war are its stations and its stands." [A poet] said:
وكم موطن لولاي طحت كما هوى ... بأجرامه من قلة النيق منهوي
(How many a battle-place where, but for me, you would have perished, as one falling with his bulk drops from the peak of the mountain-top.)
That is: many a battle-place where, were it not for my presence, you would have perished — ṭiḥta, with kasra or ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, from [the patterns of] bāʿa and qāla, i.e. you would have perished in it — as a faller (munhawin) drops from the qullat al-nīq, i.e. from the top of the mountain. Sībawayh's view is that lawlā is a preposition when an accusative pronoun follows it; al-Akhfash's view is that he put the accusative pronoun in the place of the nominative pronoun as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Mubarrad denied its occurrence, and he is refuted by this verse and others. By the many mawāṭin Allah the Exalted meant the places where the battles of Badr, Qurayẓa, al-Naḍīr, al-Ḥudaybiya, Khaybar and the Conquest of Mecca took place. In al-Qāmūs: al-mawṭin is the homeland and a scene among the scenes of war; so there is then no need to assume an omitted muḍāf, as some held. The verb from it is waṭana yaṭinu — of the pattern ḍaraba — waṭnan, and awṭana īṭānan bi-l-balad: he resided in the land; and istawṭana al-balad: he took the land as a homeland.
(حُنَيْنٍ): a valley between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif, i.e. the day of your fighting Hawāzin there. That was in Shawwāl of the year eight, right after the Conquest. Reference to this battle will come in the section of Benefits.
(رَحُبَتْ): in al-Mukhtār: al-ruḥb, with ḍamma, is spaciousness; from it one says: fulān raḥīb al-ṣadr (broad-chested, magnanimous). Al-raḥb, with fatḥa, is the spacious, of the pattern ẓarufa and qaruba; the maṣdar (verbal noun) is raḥāba, like ẓarāfa, and ruḥb, like qurb. End of quotation.

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي مَواطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ): a resumptive clause introduced to remind the believers of His favours upon them. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); نصركم الله is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent); في مواطن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نصركم; and كثيرة is a naʿt (adjective).
(وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إِذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; يوم is an adverb conjoined to His word مواطن. There is nothing to prevent conjoining an adverb of place and an adverb of time to one another, just as one object is conjoined to another with the verb being one; for you may say: ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran fī al-masjidi wa-yawma al-jumuʿa (Zayd struck ʿAmr in the mosque and on Friday), just as you say ḍarabtu Zaydan wa-ʿAmran, without needing to imply a new verb other than the first. This is so even though the two actions falling on the two objects must in reality be distinct: if you say: iḍrib Zaydan al-yawma wa-ʿAmran ghadan (strike Zayd today and ʿAmr tomorrow), there is no doubt that the two strikings are distinct by the distinctness of the two adverbs, yet the verb is one in grammatical terms. On this basis it is permissible in the verse for each of the two adverbs to remain as it is, without being interpreted in terms of the other. However, al-Zamakhsharī and others require multiplying the verb and assuming a governor for the adverb of time other than the first verb — even if both were [adverbs of] time — on the grounds that their great numbers were not present in all the battle-places. That is why al-Zamakhsharī assumed an omission. He said: "If you say: how was time conjoined to place, i.e. يوم حنين to المواطن? I say: its meaning is 'and the battle-place of the day of Ḥunayn', or 'in the days of many battle-places and the day of Ḥunayn'. It is also possible that by mawṭin time is meant, like maqtal al-Ḥusayn (the time of al-Ḥusayn's killing) and maqdam al-ḥājj (the time of the pilgrims' arrival). However, what is necessary is that يوم حنين be accusative by an implied verb, not by this overt one. What necessitates this is that إذ أعجبتكم is a badal (substitute) of يوم حنين; if you made this overt verb its governor, it would not be sound, because their great numbers did not please them in all those battle-places, nor were they numerous in all of them. So it remains that its governor is a verb particular to it."
إذ is an adverb for the past, accusative as a badal of يوم حنين, as has preceded, or accusative by an implied "remember" (udhkur); the clause أعجبتكم is annexed to the adverb, and أنفسكم is the agent. [Translator's note: so in the source, «وأنفسكم فاعل»; the agent in the verse is كثرتكم.]
Some disallowed making إذ a substitute of يوم حنين; rather, it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "remember when your great numbers pleased you".
(فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنْكُمْ شَيْئاً): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and the jussive; تغن is an imperfect, jussive (majzūm) by لم; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a direct object.
(وَضاقَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْأَرْضُ بِما رَحُبَتْ): ضاقت is conjoined to what preceded; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ضاقت; الأرض is the agent; the bāʾ is a preposition meaning "with"; and ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. "with its spaciousness", the preposition and its genitive noun being in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "while bound up with its spaciousness", as in your saying: dakhaltu ʿalayhi bi-thiyābi al-safar (I went in to him in travelling clothes), i.e. clothed in them — you mean with the travelling clothes.
(ثُمَّ وَلَّيْتُمْ مُدْبِرِينَ): conjoined to what preceded; مدبرين is a ḥāl of the tāʾ in وليتم.
(ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): ثم is a conjunction [indicating] delay; أنزل الله is a verb and its agent; سكينته is the direct object; على رسوله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنزل; and على المؤمنين is conjoined to رسوله.
(وَأَنْزَلَ جُنُوداً لَمْ تَرَوْها): أنزل جنودا is conjoined to what preceded, and the clause لم تروها is an adjective of جنودا.
(وَعَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الْكافِرِينَ): also conjoined; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and جزاء الكافرين its khabar (predicate).
(ثُمَّ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): conjoined to what preceded, coupled with delay; من بعد ذلك is a ḥāl; على من يشاء is attached to يتوب; and الله is a mubtadaʾ with غفور رحيم as its two predicates.

* Benefits:
[1-] The biographies (al-siyar) abound in reports of this battle. What is taken from them is that the Muslims were twelve thousand — those who had been present at the Conquest of Mecca, joined by two thousand of the freedmen (al-ṭulaqāʾ) — when they met Hawāzin and Thaqīf together with those reinforcements from the rest of the Arabs who joined them; so they were a great multitude. When they met, a man among the Muslims said: "We shall not be defeated today for lack of numbers." This displeased the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They fought fiercely; the intoxication of pride in their numbers overtook the Muslims, and it slipped from them that Allah is the Helper, not the number of troops. So they were routed, until their fugitives reached Mecca, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained alone, firm in his position, unmoving, with none with him but his uncle al-ʿAbbās, holding the bridle of his mount, and Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith, his cousin. Abū Jaʿfar ibn Jarīr narrated with his chain from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from a man who was among the polytheists on the day of Ḥunayn, who said: "When we and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met on the day of Ḥunayn, they did not stand before us for as long as it takes to milk a ewe. When we met them, we began driving them before us until we reached the rider of the white mule, and it was the Messenger of Allah. Men with white, handsome faces met us by him and said to us: 'May the faces be disfigured! Go back!' So we were routed and fled headlong."
There are many reports differing in their narration but agreeing in meaning that that stand was a true testimony to the utmost courage of the Prophet and his steadfastness of heart, and that men become many through victory and few through abandonment.
2- Al-Ṣafāqusī said: The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words at first is the prohibition of conjoining time to place; I have not seen anyone state this explicitly, and it is open to question. As for the necessity of implying the verb, it is based on the conjoined and what it is conjoined to sharing in what is attached to the verb, and this is not granted; Ibn al-Ḥājib pointed to its rejection in his Mukhtaṣar on the principles [of jurisprudence].
The careful and precise verdict is that His word يوم حنين — if you make it conjoined to مواطن, then the wāw stands in place of the preposition «في», as though He said: "Allah has helped you in many battle-places on the day of Ḥunayn", and this meaning is false, because it would specify the place and the time of the help; and there is no doubt that the time of the help in the many battle-places is not the day of Ḥunayn, whether you make «إذ أعجبتكم» a substitute or not. But if you conjoin «ويوم حنين» to the position of «في مواطن», as is apparent, then the conjunction stands in place of «نصركم», which governs «في مواطن», as though He said: "Allah has helped you in many battle-places, and on the day of Ḥunayn in particular." In that case «إذ أعجبتكم» may be a substitute of يوم. This is as you say: I saw [him] many times in Egypt, and on the night of the ʿĪd when people poured forth from ʿArafa. This is the true truth, with no veil over its shining face; so do not fear the clatter of al-Zamakhsharī's weapons, for it is noise without grinding — but even a fine steed stumbles.

dervis-irab:83-85.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رَجَعَكَ): Allah returned you to Medina. رجع is used intransitively and transitively: the intransitive is of the pattern of جلس and the transitive of the pattern of قطع. The meaning of al-rajʿ is bringing a thing back to the place where it was; one says رجعته رجعا, as you say رددته ردّا (I returned it).

* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ رَجَعَكَ اللَّهُ إِلى طائِفَةٍ مِنْهُمْ فَاسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِلْخُرُوجِ): the fāʾ derives the command [from what precedes] (tafrīʿiyya); إن is conditional; رجعك الله is a verb, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and fāʿil (agent), and the verb is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); إلى طائفة is attached to (mutaʿalliq) رجعك — they are the hypocrites; منهم is an adjective; فاستأذنوك is conjoined to رجعك; and للخروج is attached to استأذنوك. (فَقُلْ لَنْ تَخْرُجُوا مَعِيَ أَبَداً): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لن is a particle of negation, of the subjunctive and of the future; تخرجوا is an imperfect verb, subjunctive by لن, and the wāw is the fāʿil; معي is an adverb of place attached to تخرجوا; and أبدا is an adverb of time also attached to تخرجوا. (وَلَنْ تُقاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا): conjoined to لن تخرجوا, and its i'rab is like what preceded. (إِنَّكُمْ رَضِيتُمْ بِالْقُعُودِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause رضيتم is its khabar (predicate); بالقعود is attached to رضيتم; and أول مرة is an adverb of time. Abū al-Baqāʾ considered that unlikely and said: "مرة is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though it were said: the first going-out to which you were called. Because it was not the first going-out on which the Messenger went out for campaigns, it must be restricted, since 'firstness' requires precedence. And it is said:
the implied form is 'the first going-out on which the Messenger went in person for the campaign against the Byzantines'; and it is said: 'the first time' is before the asking of permission." On this view, أول مرة is parsed as a maṣdar of an omitted [verb]. (فَاقْعُدُوا مَعَ الْخالِفِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; اقعدوا is an imperative verb and the wāw the fāʿil; مع is an adverb attached to اقعدوا, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of اقعدوا; الخالفين is muḍāf ilayhi — they are those who stay behind, so the lām [of the article] is for prior reference (ʿahd); they are the group of the chronically ill, the women, the children and the crippled. (وَلا تُصَلِّ عَلى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ ماتَ أَبَداً):
the wāw is resumptive; لا is prohibitive; تصلّ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and its fāʿil is "you"; على أحد is attached to تصل; منهم is an adjective of أحد; the clause مات is a second adjective; and أبدا is an adverb of time attached to تصل. (وَلا تَقُمْ عَلى قَبْرِهِ): conjoined to ولا تصل; على قبره is attached to تقم. (إِنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَماتُوا وَهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause كفروا is its khabar; بالله is attached to كفروا and رسوله is conjoined to it; ماتوا is conjoined to كفروا; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and فاسقون the khabar, and the clause is in the accusative as a ḥāl; the clause إنهم is causal, with no grammatical position. (وَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَأَوْلادُهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تعجبك is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; أموالهم is the fāʿil; and أولادهم is conjoined to أموالهم. (إِنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ بِها فِي الدُّنْيا): إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); يريد الله is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; أن and what is within its scope is the object of يريد; the clause is causal, with no grammatical position; بها is attached to يعذبهم; and في الدنيا is a ḥāl.
(وَتَزْهَقَ أَنْفُسُهُمْ وَهُمْ كافِرُونَ): تزهق is conjoined to يعذبهم; أنفسهم is the fāʿil; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is the mubtadaʾ and كافرون the khabar; and the clause is a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
The variation and difference between the wordings in His saying «ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم» etc., and in the verse mentioned earlier, «فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون». As for the secret of the repetition and the wisdom in it: renewed revelation has a role in establishing and confirming what was revealed first, as though He wants the one addressed by it to keep it in mind, not to neglect it or forget it, and to believe that acting on it is important. This meaning was repeated because of its strength in what one must beware of, namely that the thing most powerful in attracting and luring hearts is preoccupation with wealth and children; and whatever is of this degree of deception and seduction must be warned against time after time. As for the secret of the variation and difference between some of the wordings of the two verses, we explain its reason as follows:
1- He the Exalted said in the first verse «فلا تعجبك» with the fāʾ, and said here:
«ولا تعجبك» with the wāw. The difference between them is that He conjoined the first verse to His saying «ولا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون», describing them as averse to spending because of their intense love of wealth and children; so it was good to conjoin to it with the fāʾ, for sequence and order. As for this verse, it has no connection with what precedes it, and so He brought the wāw.
2- He the Exalted said in the first verse «فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم», and dropped the particle لا in the second, saying «وأولادهم». The reason is that the particle لا entered there for added emphasis, indicating that they were pleased with the abundance of wealth and children, and their being pleased with their children was greater; and dropping the particle لا here is evidence that there is no difference between the two matters.
3- He the Exalted said in the first verse «إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم» with the particle lām, and said here «أن يعذبهم» with the particle أن. The benefit in this is to point out that causation (taʿlīl) in the rulings of Allah is impossible, and that even where the particle lām occurs in it, its meaning is «أن», as in His saying «وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله», whose meaning is: they were commanded only to worship Allah (bi-an yaʿbudū).
4- He the Exalted said in the first verse «في الحياة الدنيا» and said here:
«في الدنيا». The benefit in dropping the word الحياة is to point out that the life of this world has reached such a degree of baseness and contemptibility that it does not deserve to be mentioned or called "life"; rather, when it is mentioned one must confine oneself to the word الدنيا, to point out how complete its blame is.

dervis-irab:86-89.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَجاهِدُوا مَعَ رَسُولِهِ): the wāw is resumptive; إذا is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition; أنزلت is a passive past verb; سورة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) — by the sūra its whole may be meant, or part of it may be meant. أن is explicative (mufassira), because in "sending down" there is the meaning of saying without its letters. It may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), in which case it, with what it governs, is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with: believe" (bi-an āminū). بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنوا, and وجاهدوا مع رسوله is conjoined to آمنوا بالله. (اسْتَأْذَنَكَ أُولُوا الطَّوْلِ مِنْهُمْ): the clause استأذنك is the answer of إذا; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أولو الطول is the fāʿil (agent) — they are the rich and those with ample standing and power; and منهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَقالُوا ذَرْنا نَكُنْ مَعَ الْقاعِدِينَ):
ذرنا is an imperative verb whose past tense the Arabs let die, so only the imperfect and the imperative of it occur; نا is the mafʿūl bihi; نكن is the answer to the request, hence it is jussive; the noun of نكن is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we"; and مع القاعدين is an adverb of place attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of نكن. (رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوالِفِ): the clause رضوا is resumptive, brought to show the evil of their conduct; بأن يكونوا is attached to رضوا; the wāw is the noun of يكونوا; and مع الخوالف is the khabar. (وَطُبِعَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لا يَفْقَهُونَ): conjoined to رضوا; على قلوبهم is attached to طبع. فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, هم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause لا يفقهون is the khabar. (لكِنِ الرَّسُولُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ جاهَدُوا بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ): لكن is lightened and inoperative; الرسول is the mubtadaʾ; الذين is conjoined to it; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); معه is an adverb attached to آمنوا; and the clause جاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم is the khabar of الرسول. (وَأُولئِكَ لَهُمُ الْخَيْراتُ وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ): أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; لهم is a fronted khabar and الخيرات a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause لهم الخيرات is the khabar of أولئك; and وأولئك هم المفلحون is conjoined to what preceded, and its i'rab has passed. (أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): a resumptive clause to show their good final outcome; أعد is a past verb and الله its fāʿil; لهم is attached to أعد; جنات is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause تجري is an adjective. (خالِدِينَ فِيها ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): خالدين is a ḥāl and فيها is attached to خالدين; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ and الفوز العظيم its khabar.

dervis-irab:90-92.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمُعَذِّرُونَ): active participle of عذّر في الأمر, when one falls short in it, is slack and does not exert oneself. Its real sense is that one gives the impression of having an excuse for what one does while having none. Or [it is] al-muʿtadhirūn (those offering excuses), with the tāʾ assimilated into the dhāl and its vowel transferred to the ʿayn.
(الْأَعْرابِ): the dwellers of the desert. They are more specific than "Arab" (ʿarabī), since an ʿarabī is whoever speaks the Arabic language, whether he lives in the desert or in settled areas.

* I'rab:
(وَجاءَ الْمُعَذِّرُونَ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to begin explaining the conditions of the desert dwellers. جاء المعذرون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من الأعراب is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ليؤذن is causal — an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن; and لهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يؤذن. (وَقَعَدَ الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): conjoined to جاء; الذين is the fāʿil; كذبوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; the Name of Majesty is the object of كذبوا, and رسوله is conjoined to it. (سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the sīn is a particle of the future; يصيب is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "it"; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كفروا is the ṣila; منهم is a ḥāl; عذاب is the fāʿil of يصيب; and أليم is an adjective. [Translator's note: the source first says the fāʿil of يصيب is latent and then names عذاب as its fāʿil; translated as written.] (لَيْسَ عَلَى الضُّعَفاءِ وَلا عَلَى الْمَرْضى وَلا عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يَجِدُونَ ما يُنْفِقُونَ حَرَجٌ): ليس is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; على الضعفاء is the fronted khabar (predicate) of ليس; ولا على المرضى is conjoined to الضعفاء; ولا على الذين لا يجدون ما ينفقون is also conjoined; and حرج is the noun of ليس. (إِذا نَصَحُوا لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ما عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the adverb is attached to a notional [verb] drawn from the negation, i.e. blame is removed from them when they are sincere, so then they do not go out. The clause نصحوا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; رسوله is conjoined to الله; ما is negating; على المحسنين is a fronted khabar; من is redundant (zāʾida); سبيل is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) by position; الله is the mubtadaʾ, غفور the first khabar and رحيم the second khabar. (وَلا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذا ما أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction and لا negating; على الذين is conjoined to His saying على الضعفاء, so it stands as a fronted khabar, and the mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. حرج. The clause إذا ما أتوك is the ṣila of الذين; إذا is a future adverb; ما is redundant; the clause أتوك is the one to which the adverb is annexed; and لتحملهم is the reason for the coming, i.e. that you carry them with you to the campaign. They were, as history relates, seven of the Anṣār; and it is said they were the companions of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, as in al-Bukhārī. (قُلْتَ لا أَجِدُ ما أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ): the clause قلت is a ḥāl from the kāf in أتوك, with قد implied before it, i.e. when they came to you while you were saying "I do not find"; ما is the object of أجد; the clause أحملكم is the ṣila; and عليه is attached to أحملكم. (تَوَلَّوْا وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ حَزَناً أَلَّا يَجِدُوا ما يُنْفِقُونَ): the clause تولوا is the answer of إذا. It is also permissible that the clause قلت لا أجد be the answer of the conditional إذا, with إذا and its answer in the place of the ṣila; on this view His saying تولوا is an answer to an implied question, as if someone asked: "What was their state at the time they were given this answer?" and the answer was given with His saying تولوا. أعينهم is the mubtadaʾ; the wāw is circumstantial; the clause تفيض is the khabar; من الدمع is a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "overflowing with tears" — which is more eloquent than "its tears overflow", because the eye is made as though it were all overflowing tears. Discussion of this clause preceded in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida, with an elaboration not previously offered, so renew your acquaintance with it. حزنا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or a ḥāl; ألا يجدوا: أن and what is within its scope is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and what governs it is حزنا. We may also parse حزنا as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), in which case what governs ألا يجدوا is تفيض. ما is the object of يجدوا, and the clause ينفقون is the ṣila.
Abū al-Baqāʾ objected to al-Zamakhsharī's parsing of من الدمع as a tamyīz, saying: "That is not permissible, because a tamyīz which is originally a fāʿil cannot be made genitive by من; moreover it is definite, and that is permissible only according to the view of the Kufans, who allow the tamyīz to be definite."

* Rhetoric:
The art of al-talmīḥ (allusion) or al-tamlīḥ (adding grace):
In His saying «ما على المحسنين من سبيل» there is an art among the arts of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment) called «al-talmīḥ». It is that the purport of the speech points to a current proverb, a rare verse, a famous story, or something that runs like a proverb. Of it is the saying of Yasār ibn ʿAdī when the news of his brother's killing reached him while he was drinking wine:
اليوم خمر ويبدو في غد خبر ... والدهر من بين إنعام وإيئاس
(Today is wine, and tomorrow news will appear; and time is between bestowing favour and bringing despair.)
Some call it «al-tamlīḥ», with the mīm before [the lām], as though the poet in his verse or the prose writer in his passage brought a fine subtlety that increased the grace (malāḥa) of the speech, like the saying of Ibn al-Muʿtazz:
أترى الجيرة الذين تداعوا ... عند سير الحبيب وقت الزوال
علموا أنني مقيم وقلبي ... راحل فيهم أمام الجمال
مثل صاع العزيز في أرحل القو ... م ولا يعلمون ما في الرحال
(Do you think the neighbours who called to one another at noon when the beloved set off knew that I stay behind while my heart travels among them ahead of the camels — like the measuring-cup of al-ʿAzīz in the people's saddlebags, while they do not know what is in the saddlebags?)
This tamlīḥ alludes to the story of Joseph, upon him be peace, when he put the cup in his brother's saddlebag and his brothers were unaware of it. Among the subtle examples of talmīḥ is the saying of Abū Firās:
فلا خير في رد الأذى بمذلة ... كما رده يوما بسوءته عمرو
(There is no good in warding off harm by a humiliation, as ʿAmr one day warded it off with his private parts.)
This tamlīḥ or talmīḥ alludes to the story of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ with the Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, on the day of Ṣiffīn, when the Imam charged at him and ʿAmr saw there was no escape from him, so he had no recourse but to uncover his nakedness.
Among the subtleties of talmīḥ is the story of al-Hudhalī with al-Manṣūr of the Banū al-ʿAbbās. It is related that al-Manṣūr promised al-Hudhalī a reward and forgot. They went on pilgrimage together and passed, in the Prophet's city, by the house of ʿĀtika. Al-Hudhalī said: "O Commander of the Faithful, this is the house of ʿĀtika, about whom al-Aḥwaṣ says:
يا بيت عاتكة الذي أتعزل ... حذر العدا وبه الفؤاد موكل
(O house of ʿĀtika, which I keep away from for fear of enemies, though my heart is devoted to it.)"
The Commander of the Faithful disapproved of him because he had spoken without being asked. When the caliph returned, he looked through the ode to its end to know what al-Hudhalī meant by reciting that verse without being invited, and there in it was:
وأراك تفعل ما تقول وبعضهم ... مذق اللسان يقول ما لا يفعل
(And I see you do what you say, while some are insincere of tongue, saying what they do not do.)
He knew that he had pointed to this verse by his strange allusion, so he remembered what he had promised him, fulfilled it for him and apologized to him for forgetting.
Similar is what is related that Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī was partisan to al-Mutanabbī. One day he attended the gathering of al-Sharīf al-Murtaḍā, and Abū al-Ṭayyib was mentioned, and al-Murtaḍā belittled him. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said to him: "If he had no poetry except his saying:
«لك يا منازل في القلوب منازل» (You, O dwellings, have dwellings in the hearts)
it would suffice him." Al-Murtaḍā became angry and ordered him to be dragged out and expelled. After his expulsion al-Murtaḍā said:
"Do you know what he meant by mentioning that verse?" They said: "No, by Allah." He said: "He meant Abū al-Ṭayyib's saying in that ode:
وإذا أتتك مذمتي من ناقص ... فهي الشهادة لي بأني كامل
(When my disparagement comes to you from a deficient man, it is testimony for me that I am perfect.)"
Of this sort is the story of al-Sarī al-Raffāʾ with Sayf al-Dawla, also on account of al-Mutanabbī. Al-Sarī al-Raffāʾ was one of Sayf al-Dawla's panegyrists. One day in his gathering Abū al-Ṭayyib was mentioned, and Sayf al-Dawla praised him lavishly. Al-Sarī said to him: "I would like the Emir to select for me one of his finest odes so that I may compose a rival to it, and thereby it will be confirmed that he has put al-Mutanabbī on a saddle not his own." Sayf al-Dawla said to him at once: "Compose a rival for us to his qāf-rhymed ode that begins:
لعينيك ما يلقى الفؤاد وما لقي ... وللحب ما لم يبق مني وما بقي
(For your eyes is what the heart meets and has met, and to love belongs what has not remained of me and what remains.)"
Al-Sarī said: "I wrote out the ode and examined it that night, and did not find it among Abū al-Ṭayyib's choice pieces; but I saw him saying at its end about the one he praised:
إذا شاء أن يلهو بلحية أحمق ... أراه غباري ثم قال له: الحق
(When he wishes to make sport of a fool's beard, he shows him my dust and then says to him: catch up.)
So I said: By Allah, Sayf al-Dawla pointed only to this verse — and I refrained from composing a rival to the ode."
More subtle than this is what Ibn al-Jawzī related in the book of the Littérateurs (Kitāb al-Udabāʾ), for it is among the rarities of talmīḥ. He said: A man sat on the bridge of Baghdad, and a woman of surpassing beauty came from the direction of al-Ruṣāfa toward the western side. A young man met her and said to her:
"May Allah have mercy on ʿAlī ibn al-Jahm." She said to him: "May Allah have mercy on Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī." And they did not stop, but went on, one westward and one eastward. The man said: I followed the woman and said to her: "By Allah, if you do not tell me what he meant by Ibn al-Jahm, I will expose you." She said: "He meant by it:
عيون المها بين الرصافة والجسر ... جلبن الهوى من حيث أدري ولا أدري
(The eyes of the wild cows between al-Ruṣāfa and the bridge brought on love from where I know and do not know.)
And by Abū al-ʿAlāʾ I meant his saying:
فيا دارها بالكرخ إن مزارها ... قريب ولكن دون ذلك أهوال
(O her house in al-Karkh — visiting it is near, but short of that lie terrors.)"

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām cited this verse as evidence of إذا departing from the future, which is in two ways. The first is that it comes for the past, just as إذ comes for the future in the view of some. The second is that it comes for the present, and that is after the wāw of oath, as in «والليل إذا يغشى» and «والنجم إذا هوى». It is said [that it is for the present] because, if it were for the future, it could not be an adverb of the verb of oath, since that is a performative (inshāʾ), not a statement about an oath to come — because the oath of Allah, Glorified is He, is eternal — nor of an omitted كائنا that is a ḥāl from الليل and النجم, because present and future are incompatible. When these two ways are invalid, it is determined that it is an adverb of one of them, on the basis that what is meant by it is the present. End of quote.
The correct view is that attaching it to the performative "I swear" is not valid, because the eternal has no time, neither present nor other; rather it precedes time. And attaching it to كائنا is not impossible while keeping إذا for the future, as evidenced by the validity, by agreement, of the anticipated ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muqaddara), as in "I passed by a man with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow", i.e. intending to hunt with it tomorrow — thus they render it; and clearer than that is to say "wanting to hunt with it tomorrow", just as قمتم in «إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة» was explained as "you intended".
The judge Muḥibb al-Dīn, the commentator on al-Tashīl, said: it is possible that what is meant is a narration of their state when they began the act, so إذا is in its proper place. Al-Damāmīnī refuted him on the grounds that narration only establishes the present, and إذا is in its proper place only if the future is established. Al-Shumunnī answered that presentness at the beginning of the act entails futurity with respect to its completion, so by this second aspect إذا is in its proper place. Perhaps you will say: the judge's words concern the beginning of the act of coming, and there is no doubt that the turning away, or the saying that governs إذا according to what preceded, is future relative to that moment — so reflect.

dervis-irab:28-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَجَسٌ): In al-Qāmūs: "Al-najs, with fatḥa, with kasra, and with vowels throughout (najas), and like katif and ʿaḍud [i.e. najis, najus], is the opposite of the pure. It has become najis, like samiʿa and karuma; anjasahu and najjasahu, so it became tanajjasa. A dāʾ nājis and najīs, like karīm, is [a disease] from which one does not recover. Tanajjasa: he did a deed by which he came out of impurity. Al-tanjīs is the name of something of filth, or bones of the dead, or a menstruating woman's rag, which used to be hung on someone feared to be afflicted by the jinn's attachment to him; and the one who wears an amulet is munajjas." In the commentary al-Tāj on al-Qāmūs, commenting on his words "the one who wears an amulet is munajjas", it came: "Thaʿlab said: I said to Ibn al-Aʿrābī: Why is the one who wears an amulet called munajjas, when it is taken from impurity? He said: The Arabs have verbs whose meanings run contrary to their wordings; one says fulān yatanajjasu when he does a deed by which he comes out of impurity." And in the rhymed sayings of al-Asās: "When destiny comes, neither the astrologer nor the amulet-hanger avails, nor the philosopher nor the geometer." And from al-Ḥasan, concerning a man who married a woman with whom he had committed fornication: "He made her impure (anjasahā), so he has the most right to her."
(عَيْلَةً): poverty. In al-Miṣbāḥ: al-ʿayla, with fatḥa, is poverty. It is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ʿāla yaʿīlu — of the pattern sāra — so he is ʿāʾil, and the plural is ʿāla, which is construed as faʿala, like kāfir and kafara. ʿAylān, with fatḥa, is the name of a man, and from it is Qays ibn ʿAylān. Some said: there is no ʿAylān with the undotted ʿayn in the speech of the Arabs other than this. In al-Mukhtār: a man's ʿiyāl are those he supports; the singular of ʿiyāl is ʿayyil and the plural ʿayāʾil, like jayāʾid. Aʿāla al-rajul: his dependants became many, so he is muʿīl and the woman muʿīla. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. he came to have dependants.
(الْجِزْيَةَ): it was called jizya because it is a portion of what the protected people (ahl al-dhimma) must yajzūhu, i.e. pay; or because by it they repay (yajzūna) the one who favoured them by exempting them from killing. Among the remarkable things about jīm and zāy is that when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word, they indicate the meaning of taking and force. Jazzaʾtu al-shayʾ tajziʾa (I divided the thing), and a thing mujazzaʾ is divided into parts, and that cannot be done except with strength and force. A camel mujziʾ is strong and fat, because it suffices (yujziʾu) the rider and the load-carrier. Jazara lahum al-jazzār: the butcher slaughtered a camel (jazūr) for them, and they are slaughterers of camels (juzur). The butcher took his jizāra, which is his due; and "beware of these slaughterhouses (majāzir)". From it are al-jazr (ebb) and al-madd (flow), and al-jazīra and al-jazāʾir (islands). The Arabian Peninsula (Jazīrat al-ʿArab) is said of their land and dwelling place, because the Persian Sea, the Abyssinian Sea, the Tigris and the Euphrates surround it. Jazza: he sheared hair, and reaped crops and dates; this is the time of al-jazāz (shearing/harvest). One says: they sheared their sheep and shaved their goats. Jazaʿa al-wādī: he crossed it widthwise. Abū Tammām said:
إليك جزعنا مغرب الملك كلما ... قطعنا ملا صلت عليك سباسبه
(To you we crossed the west of the realm; whenever we traversed a plain, its deserts prayed for you.)
And they are at the jizʿ of the valley, which is its bend. Tajazzaʿa al-shayʾ: the thing broke into pieces and scattered. Al-Rāʿī said:
ومن فارس لم يحرم السيف خطّه ... إذا رمحه في الدارعين تجزّعا
(And how many a horseman who did not deny the sword its share, when his spear shattered among the mail-clad.)
