From it is al-jazʿ al-ẓafārī (Ẓafār onyx), because its colour may be striped with white and black. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
كأن عيون الوحش حول خبائنا ... وأرحلنا الجزع الذي لم يثقّب
(As though the eyes of the wild animals around our tent and our saddles were unpierced onyx beads.)
Jazafa such-and-such: ittibāʿuhu minhu jizāfan and bi-l-jizāf [Translator's note: so in the source, «اتباعه منه», apparently a misprint for «ابتاعه منه» — he bought it from him by guesswork, without measure]. Jāzafahu fī al-bayʿ mujāzafatan and jizāfan: he dealt with him in sale by estimate. Ḥaṭab jazl: hard, dry firewood. Thaʿlab recited:
فويها لقدرك ويها لها ... إذا اختير في المحل جزل الحطب
(Bravo to your cooking-pot, bravo to it, when in drought thick firewood is chosen.)
And he said:
فأصبحت أنى تأتها تستجر بها ... تجد حطبا جزلا ونارا تأججا
(So she became such that wherever you come to her seeking refuge, you find thick firewood and a blazing fire.)
Ḍaraba al-ṣayd fa-jazalahu jazlatayn: he struck the game and cut it in two pieces. Figuratively: a man jazl is one of intelligence and judgement; jazula, and how evident is the jazāla in him; he is jazl al-ʿaṭāʾ (abundant in giving); "if you do such-and-such, you will have fair mention and abundant (jazīl) reward"; and a woman jazla is one with ample hips. Jazamtu mā baynī wa-baynahu: I cut it off. Jazm al-yamīn: cutting [i.e. making] the oath decisively. Jazama ʿalā kadhā: he resolved on it. You say: this is a decisive ruling (ḥukm jazm) and an inevitable decree.
If we return to jazā, we see wonders from this root. You say: yajzīka Allāhu ʿannī and yujāzīka (may Allah repay you on my behalf). Labīd said:
وإذا جوزيت قرضا فاجزه ... إنما يجزى الفتى ليس الجمل
(When you are repaid a loan, repay it; only a true man is repaid, not a camel.)
And al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
من يفعل الخير لا يعدم جوازيه ... لا يذهب العرف بين الله والناس
(Whoever does good will not lack its rewards; a kindness is never lost between Allah and people.)

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has preceded.
(إِنَّمَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ): إنما is [inna as] a restraining particle with the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); المشركون نجس is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. possessors of impurity, because they have with them polytheism, which is equivalent to impurity; or because they do not purify themselves, do not bathe and do not avoid impurities, so these never cease to cling to them; or they were made as though they were impurity itself, by way of hyperbole in describing them with it. Al-najas is a maṣdar in which masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike. Or it is a metaphor for inner foulness and corrupt belief.
(فَلا يَقْرَبُوا الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرامَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); لا is prohibitive; يقربوا is an imperfect, jussive (majzūm) by it, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); المسجد is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and الحرام a naʿt (adjective).
(بَعْدَ عامِهِمْ هذا): the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقربوا; عامهم is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and هذا is an adjective of عامهم or a badal (substitute) of it. It is the ninth year of the Hijra. This ruling involves juristic questions to be consulted in the extended sources.
(وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً فَسَوْفَ يُغْنِيكُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِنْ شاءَ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; خفتم is a verb and its agent, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عيلة is the direct object; فسوف: the fāʾ links [the apodosis] and سوف is a particle of the future; يغنيكم الله is an imperfect verb, its object and its agent, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); من فضله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يغنيكم; إن is conditional, شاء is its verb, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then He will enrich you".
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): إنّ with its noun and its two predicates.
(قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَلا بِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): a resumptive clause introduced to command campaigning against the polytheists. قاتلوا is an imperative verb and its agent; الذين is the direct object; the clause يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause); بالله is attached to يؤمنون; and ولا باليوم الآخر is conjoined to بالله.
(وَلا يُحَرِّمُونَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ): conjoined to what preceded; ما is the object of يحرمون, and the clause حرم الله ورسوله is the ṣila.
(وَلا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ الْحَقِّ): the wāw is a conjunction; دين الحق may be the maṣdar of يدينون, so that it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); or it may be a direct object, with يدينون made to include the sense of "believe". It may also be accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. bi-dīn al-ḥaqq — and perhaps this is the most apparent.
(مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in يدينون, or of the first الذين together with what falls within its scope; the clause أوتوا الكتاب is the ṣila, and الكتاب is a second object.
(حَتَّى يُعْطُوا الْجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَدٍ): حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يعطوا is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; الجزية is the direct object; and عن يد is a ḥāl — further discussion of it will come in the section of Rhetoric.
(وَهُمْ صاغِرُونَ): a second ḥāl; هم is a mubtadaʾ and صاغرون the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the words of the Exalted «عن يد» there is a kināya (metonymy) for submission. One says: aʿṭā fulān bi-yadihi (so-and-so gave his hand) when he surrendered and submitted, because one who refuses and resists does not give his hand, unlike the obedient and submissive. It is as though it were said: fight them until they give the jizya willingly and submissively, without being compelled to it. Further, what is meant by it is either the hand of the giver or that of the taker. On the intention of the giver's hand, its meaning is: until they give it from a compliant, unresisting hand, because one who refuses and resists does not give his hand, unlike the obedient and submissive — do you not see their saying "he withdrew his hand from obedience", just as one says "he threw off the noose of obedience from his neck"? As for the taker's hand, its meaning is: until they give it on account of a subduing, dominant hand, or on account of a favour bestowed on them, because accepting the jizya from them and sparing their lives is a great favour to them. Further, the discussions of metonymy have preceded, and much of it will come in its place.

dervis-irab:30-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُضاهِؤُنَ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: ḍāhaʾahu muḍāhaʾatan, with hamza: he imitated him and vied with him. The lightened form is also permissible, so one says ḍāhaytuhu muḍāhātan; it is the resembling of one thing to another.
(يُؤْفَكُونَ): they are turned away.
(أَحْبارَهُمْ): In al-Mukhtār: al-ḥibr is that with which one writes, and its place is the miḥbara, with kasra. Al-ḥibr is also the trace; in the ḥadīth: "A man will come out of the Fire whose ḥibr and sibr have gone." Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. his appearance and his colour. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: beauty, splendour and the trace of well-being. Taḥbīr of handwriting, poetry and other things is making it beautiful. Al-ḥabr, with fatḥa, is al-ḥubūr, which is joy; ḥabarahu, i.e. he gladdened him, of the pattern naṣara; and ḥabra, also with fatḥa. From it are the words of the Exalted «فهم في روضة يحبرون», i.e. they are gladdened, given delight and honoured. Al-ḥabr, with fatḥa or kasra, is the singular of aḥbār of the Jews, and kasra is more eloquent because it is pluralised on afʿāl and not on fuʿūl. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is with kasra; Abū ʿUbayda said: it is with fatḥa. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I do not know whether it is with fatḥa or kasra; and he said: al-ḥibr, with kasra, is attributed to the ink (ḥibr) with which one writes, because he was a man of books. Al-ḥibara, like al-ʿinaba, is a Yemeni cloak; the plural is ḥibar, like ʿinab, and ḥibarāt with fatḥa on the bāʾ. In al-Munjid: al-ḥabr and al-ḥibr, with fatḥa and kasra: the righteous scholar; joy and well-being; a head among the heads of religion; al-ḥabr al-aʿẓam: the successor of the Lord Christ on earth; the chief of the priests among the Jews; the plural is aḥbār and ḥubūr.
(رُهْبانَهُمْ): plural of rāhib, which is one who withdraws from people to a monastery seeking worship. The feminine is rāhiba, and its plural rāhibāt and rawāhib.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ): the wāw is resumptive; قالت اليهود is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عزير is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and ابن الله the khabar (predicate). For that reason the alif of ابن is retained, since it is dropped when ابن occurs as a naʿt (adjective) or a badal (substitute) between two proper names. عزير takes tanwīn because it is Arabic, so only one cause [of diptosis] remains in it, namely being a proper name; and it was read as a diptote, considering it foreign. The words of the Exalted «وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله» were read in two ways: with tanwīn on عزير, because ابن is a khabar of عزير, so it runs like your saying Zaydun ibnu ʿAmr (Zayd is the son of ʿAmr); and the other reading without tanwīn, which has two explanations: first, that عزير is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ and ابن an adjective of it, so the tanwīn was dropped from عزير because ابن is its adjective, as though they said: "he is ʿUzayr son of Allah"; the other explanation is that ابن was made a khabar of عزير and the tanwīn was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(وَقالَتِ النَّصارى الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ): a similar clause conjoined to the one before it; the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is the maqūl al-qawl (object of "said").
(ذلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and قولهم the khabar; بأفواههم is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The secret of mentioning the mouths will come in the section of Rhetoric.
(يُضاهِؤُنَ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ): the clause is circumstantial; قول is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); and من قبل is a ḥāl.
(قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ): قاتلهم الله is a verb, its object and its agent; the clause is one of imprecation, with no grammatical position. أنى is an interrogative noun meaning "how", in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl placed first; يؤفكون is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. how are they turned away from the truth?
(اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبارَهُمْ وَرُهْبانَهُمْ أَرْباباً مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَالْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): اتخذوا is a verb and its agent; أحبارهم is the direct object; رهبانهم is conjoined to أحبارهم; أربابا is a second object; من دون الله is an adjective of أربابا; المسيح is conjoined to أحبارهم, and the second object with respect to it is omitted, i.e. "a lord"; ابن is an adjective of المسيح or a substitute of it, and the alif is retained in it because it is an adjective between two proper names [Translator's note: so in the source; this conflicts with the rule the source states above, that the alif of ابن is dropped when it is an adjective between two proper names. Translated as written.]; المسيح is a title (laqab), and the title is one of the categories of proper name.
(وَما أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا إِلهاً واحِداً): the wāw is circumstantial; ما is negative; أمروا is a passive past verb and the wāw is the deputy agent; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); the lām is causal; يعبدوا is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause; and واحدا is an adjective of إلها.
(لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): the clause is a second adjective of إلها. The i'rab of «لا إله إلا الله» has been discussed in detail before.
(سُبْحانَهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and the hāʾ is the muḍāf ilayhi; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning declaring Allah transcendent above having partners associated with Him. عما is attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحانه, and the clause يشركون is the ṣila of ما.
(يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ): the clause يريدون is circumstantial, to represent their state in attempting to nullify the prophethood of Muhammad by denial as the state of one who wants to blow upon a mighty light; a discussion of this will come in the section of Rhetoric. أن and what falls within its scope is the object of يريدون; نور الله is the direct object; and بأفواههم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يطفئوا.
(وَيَأْبَى اللَّهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ): يأبى الله is conjoined to يريدون; إلا is a particle of restriction, because the speech is on the supposition of negation, since يأبى functions like "did not want"; أن and what falls within its scope is the object of يأبى. ولو: the wāw is circumstantial and لو is conditional, its apodosis omitted because what precedes indicates it, its implied form being "He would complete it and not care about their aversion"; the clause is circumstantial. The meaning is: Allah wants nothing but the completion of His light, even if they are averse to it. It was asked: how did the exceptive «إلا» enter upon يأبى, when it is not permitted to say "I disliked" or "I hated except Zayd"? Al-Farrāʾ said: it entered only because there is an element of negation in the speech. Al-Zajjāj said: the Arabs make an omission with abā, the implied construction being "and Allah refuses everything except that He complete His light". ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: this was permitted with abā only because it is preventing or refraining, so it resembles negation. Al-Naḥḥās said: this is best, as the poet said:
وهل لي أم غيرها إن تركتها ... أبى الله إلا أن أكون لها ابنا
(Have I any mother but her, if I were to abandon her? Allah refuses anything but that I be her son.)

* Rhetoric:
In the words of the Exalted «ذلك قولهم بأفواههم» there is a suggestion (īhām) that speech is only by the mouth — so what is the meaning of mentioning their mouths? But the secret lies in the mouths: namely, that what it [the sect] proclaims [Translator's note: the source has «ما تندبه», possibly a misprint for «ما تدعيه», "what it claims"] is nothing but a mere saying, paid no heed, supported by no proof and upheld by no argument; it is nothing but an empty word and drivel with no substance beneath it, like meaningless words that are mere bells and tunes containing no meanings — and what has no meaning goes no further than the lips.

dervis-irab:93-95.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَسْتَأْذِنُونَكَ وَهُمْ أَغْنِياءُ): إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); it is said that it is for emphasis and intensifying it, and it is said that it is for restriction (ḥaṣr). السبيل is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and على الذين the khabar (predicate); the clause يستأذنونك is the ṣila (relative clause); وهم: the wāw is circumstantial, هم is the mubtadaʾ and أغنياء the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوالِفِ): a resumptive clause, or a ḥāl with قد implied; بأن يكونوا is attached to (mutaʿalliq) رضوا; the wāw is the noun of يكونوا and the adverb is its khabar. (وَطَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the clause is conjoined to what preceded; the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم is the mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يعلمون the khabar. (يَعْتَذِرُونَ إِلَيْكُمْ إِذا رَجَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ): a resumptive clause, brought to show how they justify their cowardly stance. It is related that they were some eighty-odd men; when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, they came offering him false excuses. إليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعتذرون; إذا is a future adverb attached to its omitted answer, i.e. "they offer excuses"; the clause رجعتم is the one to which it is annexed; and إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رجعتم. (قُلْ لا تَعْتَذِرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ): the clause لا تعتذروا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause لن نؤمن لكم is resumptive, as though it were the reason for the prohibition; and لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نؤمن. (قَدْ نَبَّأَنَا اللَّهُ مِنْ أَخْبارِكُمْ): قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); نبأنا here takes two objects in the accusative, the first being نا and the second the preposition and its genitive noun — or the phrase من أخباركم, which is in reality an adjective of the omitted object. As for the third object, it has been omitted for brevity because it is known, the implied form being: "Allah has informed us, of your news, of lies and false rumours." (وَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُ): the sīn is a particle of the future; يرى is an imperfect verb and الله the fāʿil (agent); seeing here means knowing; عملكم is the first object of يرى, and the second is omitted, its implied form being "occurring"; and رسوله is conjoined to الله. (ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلى عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ): ثم is a conjunction for order with delay; تردون is an imperfect verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and إلى عالم الغيب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تردون. (فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ينبئكم is a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and the kāf is its first object; بما كنتم is its second object; the clause تعملون is the khabar of كنتم; and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "you used to do it". ما here is a relative noun or maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). (سَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكُمْ إِذَا انْقَلَبْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لِتُعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ): the sīn is for emphasis together with the future; يحلفون is an imperfect verb and the wāw the fāʿil; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; the clause is a badal (substitute) for يعتذرون; لكم is a ḥāl; and what is sworn to is omitted, relying on the reader's understanding, i.e. that they are excused in staying behind. إذا is an adverb attached to يحلفون; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to انقلبتم. لتعرضوا: the lām is causal; تعرضوا is subjunctive by an implied أن after it; and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to يحلفون. The accusative of a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) was not possible because the agent differs; i.e. so that you leave off reproaching them. عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعرضوا. (فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ رِجْسٌ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition); أعرضوا is an imperative verb and the wāw the fāʿil; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعرضوا; and إنّ with its noun and khabar. (وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; مأواهم is the mubtadaʾ and جهنم the khabar; جزاء is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense"; بما is attached to جزاء; ما is maṣdariyya; and كان with its noun, and the clause يكسبون is its khabar.

dervis-irab:96-98.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَعْرابُ): it has been discussed already, and we add here that the lām in it is for the genus, i.e. their genus, not every one of them, because some of them will be excepted, as will come. It is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) that comes in the form of a plural; it is not the plural of عرب, lest the plural be more specific than its singular — because the aʿrāb are specifically the desert dwellers, while the ʿarab are those who speak the Arabic language, whether desert dwellers or settled. In al-Miṣbāḥ:
"As for al-aʿrāb, they are the people of the desert among the Arabs; the singular is aʿrābī, also with fatḥa, and he is one who seeks pasture and goes in search of grazing. Al-Azharī added, saying: whether he is of the Arabs or of their clients. He said: whoever settles in the desert, lives as a neighbour to the desert folk and moves when they move, they are aʿrāb; and whoever settles in the cultivated lands and makes his home in the towns and villages, Arab or other, among those who trace themselves to the Arabs, they are ʿarab, even if they are not eloquent." Another said: "عرب لسانه عرابة (his tongue became pure Arabic); and I have not heard anything more eloquent (أعرب) than his speech; and he spoke clearly (أعرب); and he is of the pure Arabs (al-ʿarab al-ʿarbāʾ) and al-ʿāriba, who are the unmixed and pure; and so-and-so is of the mustaʿriba, who are those who entered among them; and in him there is a touch of Bedouin roughness (lawtha aʿrābiyya)." [The poet] said:
وإني على ما فيّ من عنجهيتي ... ولوثة أعرابيتي لأديب
(For all my arrogance and the touch of Bedouin roughness in me, I am indeed a man of refinement.)
And al-Kumayt said:
لا ينقض الأمر إلا ريث يبرمه ... ولا تعرّب إلا حوله العرب
(He does not undo an affair except while he firmly twists it, and the Arabs do not act as proud Bedouins except around him.)
i.e. they are not mighty and unassailable, with the might of the Bedouins in their desert, except in his presence. More discussion of it will come.
(الدَّوائِرَ): the dawāʾir of time are its turns and vicissitudes. It is the plural of dāʾira, and al-dāʾira is the calamity and misfortune that surrounds a person, taken from the circle (dāʾira) surrounding a thing. Its origin is dāwira, because it is from دار يدور, and the wāw was changed into a hamza. The lexicographers differed about it: some said it is of the pattern fāʿila, like qāʾima, and some said it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-ʿāqiba.

* I'rab:
(يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ لِتَرْضَوْا عَنْهُمْ): يحلفون is a badal (substitute) for سيحلفون; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحلفون, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the causal lām with its genitive noun is attached to يحلفون; and عنهم is attached to ترضوا. (فَإِنْ تَرْضَوْا عَنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَرْضى عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. if you are pleased with them, your being pleased will not benefit them. فإن: the fāʾ is causal; إنّ and its noun, and the clause لا يرضى عن القوم الفاسقين is its khabar (predicate). (الْأَعْرابُ أَشَدُّ كُفْراً وَنِفاقاً): الأعراب is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and أشد the khabar; كفرا is a tamyīz (specification) and نفاقا is conjoined to it. That is because of their coarseness, harshness and remoteness from the features of civilization. It is a case of describing the genus by one of its individuals or some of them, as in His saying «وكان الإنسان كفورا», since not all of them are as described. A discussion of «the defining al» with mention of its kinds will come in the section of Benefits. (وَأَجْدَرُ أَلَّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ): أجدر is conjoined to أشد; أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "more apt not to know (bi-an lā yaʿlamū)", and it is attached to أجدر; حدود is the object of يعلموا; ما is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): a mubtadaʾ and its two khabars. (وَمِنَ الْأَعْرابِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَماً): من الأعراب is a fronted khabar and من a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause يتخذ is the ṣila; the fāʿil (agent) of يتخذ is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he"; ما is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the clause ينفق is the ṣila; مغرما is the second object of يتخذ, i.e. a loss, because he does not hope for reward but fears punishment. (وَيَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ الدَّوائِرَ): ويتربص: the wāw is circumstantial, and it may be a conjunction, in which case يتربص falls within the scope of the ṣila; بكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and الدوائر is the mafʿūl bihi. (عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the clause is one of supplication with no grammatical position; عليهم is a fronted khabar and دائرة السوء a delayed mubtadaʾ; الله is the mubtadaʾ, سميع its first khabar and عليم its second khabar.

* Benefits:
The rules of أل:
(أل), in all its kinds, is a particle of definition according to the soundest view. It is either for defining the genus, and is called «al-jinsiyya» (generic), or for defining a known portion of it, and is called «al-ʿahdiyya» (of prior reference).

The ʿahdiyya أل is of three kinds:
a- It may be for mentioned reference (al-ʿahd al-dhikrī): that whose companion [noun] was previously mentioned in the speech, as when you say: "A guest came to me, and I honoured the guest", i.e. the one mentioned. Of it is His saying: «كما أرسلنا إلى فرعون رسولا فعصى فرعون الرسول».
b- It may be for present reference (al-ʿahd al-ḥuḍūrī): that whose companion is present, as in "I came today (al-yawm)", i.e. the present day we are in.
c- It may be for mental reference (al-ʿahd al-dhihnī): that whose companion is known in the mind, so thought turns to it merely by its being uttered, as in "The man came", i.e. the man known in mind between you and the one you are addressing.

The jinsiyya أل is of two kinds:
a- It may be for encompassing all the individuals of the genus (istighrāq): that which includes all its individuals, as in His saying: «وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا».
b- Or for encompassing all its characteristics, as in "You are the man", i.e. all the qualities of men are combined in you.

Important notes:
1- The sign of the encompassing (istighrāqiyya) أل is that «كل» (every/all) can properly take its place.
2- The أل that is for explaining the reality, quiddity and nature of the genus, regardless of the individuals to which it applies — and for that reason «كل» cannot take its place — is called «the lām of reality, quiddity and nature». For example: "Man (al-insān) is a rational animal", i.e. his reality is that he is intelligent and perceiving, though not every human is so; and "Man (al-rajul) is more patient than woman" — not every man is so, and among women there may be those who surpass many men in patience and endurance. So أل here is for defining the reality, without regard to the individuals of the genus but to its quiddity as such. On this is to be taken the أل that enters «الأعراب»: not all of them are at this degree of intense disbelief and hypocrisy and aversion to hearing good words.

The redundant أل:
أل may be added (zāʾida) without conveying definiteness. Its addition is either necessary, so that it does not leave its companion — as its addition in proper names with which it was coupled at their coining, like al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and al-Samawʾal, and its addition in relative nouns like الذي, التي and the like, since a relative noun is made definite by its ṣila, not by أل, according to the soundest view — or its addition is not necessary, as its addition in some proper names transferred from an original [meaning], to glance at the original meaning, like al-Faḍl, al-Ḥārith, al-Nuʿmān, al-Walīd, al-Rashīd and the like. Its addition is based on what is heard (samāʿī), so one does not say "al-Muḥammad" or "al-Maḥmūd": what has come from the Arabs of this is accepted as heard, and nothing else is formed by analogy with it.

The relative أل:
أل may be a relative noun with a single form in all cases. It is the one that enters active and passive participles, on condition that neither prior reference nor genus is meant by it, as in أكرم المكرم ضيفه، والمكرم ضيفه, i.e. "the one who honours his guest" and "the one whose guest is honoured" (الذي يكرم ضيفه والذي يكرم ضيفه). [Translator's note: the source text is unvocalized; the two examples are presumably al-mukrim (active) and al-mukram (passive), with yukrim / yukram in the paraphrase.] When the adjective occurring as the ṣila of the relative أل is equivalent to a verb and its subject, it is good to conjoin a verb and its subject to it, as in His saying «والعاديات ضبحا فالموريات قدحا فالمغيرات صبحا فأثرن به نقعا فوسطن به جمعا». Discussion of this will come in its place.

dervis-irab:33-35.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَكْنِزُونَ): they amass and bury. In al-Miṣbāḥ: kanaztu al-māl kanzan — of the pattern ḍaraba — I amassed it and stored it; and kanaztu al-tamr fī wiʿāʾihi kanzan as well (I packed the dates into their container); and this is the time of al-kanāz. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: it has been heard only with fatḥa. Al-Azharī reported: kanaztu al-tamr kanāzan and kināzan, with fatḥa and kasra. Al-kanz is buried wealth, well known, named by the maṣdar (verbal noun); its plural is kunūz, like fals and fulūs. Iktanaza al-shayʾ iktināzan: the thing became compact and full. In al-Asās: innahu la-kanīz al-laḥm muktanizuhu: firm of flesh; and a she-camel kināz al-laḥm (firm-fleshed). Figuratively: he has a treasure among the treasures of knowledge. Zuhayr said:
عظيمين في عليا معد وغيرها ... ومن يستبح كنزا من المجد يعظم
(Two great men among the highest of Maʿadd and others; and whoever lays open a treasure of glory becomes great.)
And: this is a book packed (muktaniz) with benefits.
(الذَّهَبَ): well known; it is treated as masculine and feminine, and it has many names, namely: naḍr, nuḍār, naḍīr, zibrij, zukhruf, ʿasjad, ʿiqyān.

* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ): the clause is resumptive; هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي its khabar (predicate); the clause أرسل رسوله is the ṣila (relative clause); بالهدى, i.e. with the Qur'an, is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسل; and دين الحق is conjoined to الهدى.
(لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ): the lām is causal; يظهر is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), referring to the Messenger; على الدين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يظهره; كله is a tawkīd (emphasis) of الدين; the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional and connective (waṣliyya); كره المشركون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the object is omitted, i.e. "that".
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has preceded.
(إِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْأَحْبارِ وَالرُّهْبانِ لَيَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوالَ النَّاسِ بِالْباطِلِ): إنّ and its noun; من الأحبار is a naʿt (adjective) of كثيرا; الرهبان is conjoined to الأحبار; ليأكلون: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the clause يأكلون is the khabar of إنّ; أموال الناس is the direct object; بالباطل is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The verification of "eating" will come in the section of Rhetoric.
(وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): conjoined to يأكلون.
(وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلا يُنْفِقُونَها فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is resumptive; الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يكنزون is the ṣila; الذهب is the object of يكنزون; الفضة is conjoined to الذهب; ولا ينفقونها is conjoined to يكنزون; and في سبيل الله is attached to ينفقونها.
(فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): the fāʾ links [the predicate] because of the sense of generality and the hint of condition in the condition [Translator's note: so in the source, «لما في الشرط»; presumably «لما في الموصول», "in the relative noun", is meant]; بشرهم is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object; بعذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بشرهم; أليم is an adjective; and the clause بشرهم is the khabar. It is better that الذين be accusative, on the supposition "give tidings to those who amass".
(يَوْمَ يُحْمى عَلَيْها فِي نارِ جَهَنَّمَ فَتُكْوى بِها جِباهُهُمْ وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ): the adverb is attached to His words بعذاب أليم; it was also said [that it is attached] to an omitted [verb] indicated by عذاب, i.e. "they will be punished on the day it is heated", or to an omitted [verb] whose implied form is "remember"; the clause يحمى is annexed to the adverb. يحمى may be from ḥamaytu or aḥmaytu, triliteral or quadriliteral; one says ḥamaytu al-ḥadīda and aḥmaytuhā, i.e. I lit a fire upon it so that it became hot. The omitted nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the Fire, its implied form being "on the day the Fire is heated upon it"; when the deputy agent was omitted, the sign of the feminine went with it, as when they say rufiʿat al-qiṣṣa ilā al-amīr (the petition was raised to the governor), and then you say rufiʿa ilā al-amīr. عليها is in the position of the nominative as the deputy agent, as has preceded; في نار جهنم is attached to يحمى. فتكوى: the fāʾ is a conjunction and تكوى is conjoined to تحمى; بها is attached to تكوى; جباههم is the deputy agent; and جنوبهم and ظهورهم are conjoined to جباههم. The secret of singling out these members will come in the section of Rhetoric.
(هذا ما كَنَزْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ): the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object) of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "it will be said to them"; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and ما its khabar; the clause كنزتم is the ṣila; and لأنفسكم is attached to كنزتم.
(فَذُوقُوا ما كُنْتُمْ تَكْنِزُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); ذوقوا is an imperative verb and its agent; ما is the direct object; the clause كنتم تكنزون is the ṣila, and the clause تكنزون is the khabar of كنتم.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are many figures among the varieties of rhetoric, which we summarise below:
1- Istiʿāra (metaphor) in "eating" wealth, since it is not something eaten; rather, eating was borrowed for taking. The meaning of their eating by falsehood is that they used to take bribes in judgements.
2- The pronoun in His word «ينفقونها» is singular although He mentioned two things, gold and silver, the pronoun being directed to the meaning rather than the wording, because each of them is an ample total and a large number.
3- He singled out the foreheads, the faces and the backs [Translator's note: so in the source, «الجباه والوجوه والظهور»; the verse mentions foreheads, sides (الجنوب) and backs] because they sought, by amassing and hoarding wealth, worldly aims by which they would raise their foreheads and preserve the water of their faces [i.e. their dignity]; people would make much of them on seeing them, and they would throw soft garments upon their backs. These are secrets that the Mighty Qur'an alone possesses.

* Benefits:
History relates that Abū Dharr said: These verses were revealed concerning the People of the Book and concerning the Muslims. The rationale of this saying is that the People of the Book are described as greedy to take wealth by any means; then after that Allah mentioned the threat against whoever amasses wealth and withholds the obligatory dues on it, whether he is of the People of the Book or of the Muslims.
Muslim narrated from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: I passed by al-Rabadha, and there was Abū Dharr. I said to him: "What brought you to this place?" He said: "I was in Syria, and Muʿāwiya and I differed over this verse: «والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله». Muʿāwiya said: It was revealed concerning the People of the Book; and I said: It was revealed concerning us and them. There were words between him and me about that, so he wrote to ʿUthmān complaining about me, and he [ʿUthmān] wrote to me to come to Medina. I came to it, and people crowded around me as though they had never seen me before. I mentioned that to ʿUthmān, and he said: If you wish, you may withdraw and be near us. That is what brought me to this place; and even if they had put an Abyssinian slave in command over me, I would have heard and obeyed."

An important ḥadīth about gold and silver:
Sālim ibn al-Jaʿd narrated that when it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Perdition to gold, perdition to silver" — he said it three times. They said to him: "What wealth, then, shall we take?" He said: "A remembering tongue, a humble heart, and a wife who helps one of you in his religion." Further, the scholars differed over the limit of capital. ʿAlī said: "Four thousand and less is maintenance; whatever exceeds it is a hoard (kanz)." They replied to him that this is reasonable [only] before zakāt was made obligatory. There is a long discussion, to be consulted in the extended works, and it is not within the aim of this book.

dervis-irab:36-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النَّسِيءُ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of nasaʾa when he postponed it. One says: nasaʾahu nasʾan, nasīʾan and nasāʾan, like your saying massahu massan, misāsan and masīsan. It was also said that it is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, from nasaʾahu when he postponed it, so it is mansūʾ; then mafʿūl was turned into faʿīl, as maqtūl was turned into qatīl. In al-Mukhtār: al-nasīʾa, like al-faʿīla, is postponement, and likewise al-nasāʾ, with fatḥa and lengthening, is postponement. Al-nasīʾ in the verse is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, from your saying nasaʾahu — of the pattern qaṭaʿa — i.e. he postponed it, so it is mansūʾ; then mansūʾ was turned into nasīʾ, as maqtūl was turned into qatīl. What is meant by it here is postponing the sanctity of al-Muḥarram to Ṣafar; the details of this will come in the section of Benefits. [Translator's note: the source writes «مصدر نساء», apparently for «مصدر نسأ».]

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ اثْنا عَشَرَ شَهْراً): إنّ and its noun; الشهور is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); عند الله is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in His ruling"; اثنا is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the alif because it is dual; عشر is a numeral component, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; and شهرا is a tamyīz (specification). They are the well-known lunar months.
(فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ): في كتاب الله is a naʿt (adjective) of اثني عشر; يوم is an adverb attached to an omitted [word], or to كتاب الله if it is made a maṣdar. The meaning is: this is a matter fixed in reality since Allah created the beings. It was also said that يوم خلق is a badal (substitute) of His word عند الله, the implied construction being: "the number of months with Allah, in the Book of Allah, on the day He created the heavens and the earth"; the benefit of the two substitutions is to establish the statement firmly in minds. The clause خلق is the one to which the adverb is annexed.
(مِنْها أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ): منها is a khabar placed first and أربعة a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; حرم is an adjective; and the clause is a second adjective of اثني عشر شهرا. They are three consecutive — Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja and al-Muḥarram — and one by itself, which is Rajab.
(ذلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, الدين the khabar, and القيم an adjective.
(فَلا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); لا is prohibitive; تظلموا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); فيهن is attached to تظلموا; and أنفسكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(وَقاتِلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ كَافَّةً كَما يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ كَافَّةً): the wāw is a conjunction; قاتلوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the agent; المشركين is the direct object; كافة is a ḥāl of the agent or of the object. It is originally a maṣdar meaning "all together"; it is not made dual or plural, does not take al-, and is not used in any function other than ḥāl. This is what the grammarians have established regarding kāffa. But al-Shihāb al-Khafājī declared it correct to say jāʾat al-kāffa (the whole came), and discussed it at length in his commentary on al-Shifāʾ. The commentator on al-Lubāb said that it has been used in the genitive, and adduced as evidence the words of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: «على كافة بيت مال المسلمين» (upon the whole of the Muslims' treasury). Ibrāhīm al-Kūrānī said: whoever among the grammarians said that kāffa never leaves the accusative — his judgement arises from incomplete induction. Al-Zamakhsharī used it in the genitive after the bāʾ [Translator's note: the source says «مجرورة بالكاف», "genitive by the kāf", but the quotation that follows has the bāʾ] in the preface of his book al-Mufaṣṣal, saying: «محيط بكافة الأبواب» (comprehending all the chapters), just as he used it for non-humans. كما: the kāf means "like" and is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; or it is a preposition and ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what falls within its scope as a maṣdar, [and the whole is] an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a fighting like their fighting you" [Translator's note: the source has «كقتالكم», "like your fighting"]. Its like has preceded, so refresh your memory of it.
(وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ): أنّ and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا; أنّ and its noun; and مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar.
(إِنَّمَا النَّسِيءُ زِيادَةٌ فِي الْكُفْرِ): إنما is [inna as] a restraining particle with the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); النسيء is a mubtadaʾ and زيادة the khabar; and في الكفر is attached to زيادة.
(يُضَلُّ بِهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): a verb and its agent; به is attached to it; الذين كفروا is its agent. It was also read يضل به الذين كفروا in the passive. The clause is a second khabar of النسيء. [Translator's note: the source parses the verb as active (yaḍillu, with الذين كفروا as agent) and mentions the passive as a variant, although the vocalised text above reads it as passive (يُضَلُّ, with الذين كفروا as deputy agent).]
(يُحِلُّونَهُ عاماً وَيُحَرِّمُونَهُ عاماً): the clause explains the misguidance, so it has no grammatical position; it may also be parsed as circumstantial. عاما is an adverb attached to يحلونه.
(لِيُواطِؤُا عِدَّةَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ): the lām is causal, and together with its interpreted genitive it is attached to يحرمونه or to يحلونه according to the rule of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one word); عدة is its object; ما is a relative noun, the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause حرم الله is the ṣila (relative clause).
(فَيُحِلُّوا ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ): conjoined to ليواطئوا; ما is the object of يحلوا.
(زُيِّنَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ أَعْمالِهِمْ): the clause is a ḥāl of the agent, i.e. "while made to see as fair", or resumptive — and perhaps this is preferable. لهم is attached to زين, and سوء أعمالهم is the agent. [Translator's note: زين is passive, so سوء أعمالهم is strictly its deputy agent; the source says «فاعل».]
(وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكافِرِينَ): a mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا يهدي is the khabar.

* Benefits:
What history says about al-nasīʾ:
History relates that the Arabs in the Jāhiliyya believed in the sanctity of the sacred months and honoured them. Most of the Arabs' livelihood came from hunting and raiding, and it was hard on them to refrain from that for three consecutive months. Sometimes wars broke out in some of the sacred months, and they disliked postponing their wars to the lawful months; so they practised nasīʾ, i.e. they postponed the sanctity of one month to another month. So [the verse] was revealed.
Al-Mubarrad said in his Kāmil: "Nasaʾa Allāhu fī ajalika, nasaʾa Allāhu ajalaka and ansaʾa Allāhu ajalaka (may Allah prolong your term); al-nasīʾ is from this, and its meaning is postponing one month from another. Those who did the postponing (al-nasaʾa) were from Banū Mudlij ibn Kināna. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed «إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر», because they used to postpone the months, making sacred what was not sacred and making lawful what was not lawful, according to what they planned for their wars and dealings; and the months were set straight when Islam came."
